## M-OIT-COVERAGE-AND-FLIP-EVIDENCE — WebGPU MRT-OIT is unreachable for standard translucency; default-flip verdict NO-GO (2026-07-18, Batch 700, maintainer-directed)

**Not a bug fix — a coverage + evidence slice (zero engine code).** Built OIT test coverage and a
default-flip evidence package for `FAR-003` (WebGPU MRT-OIT contained off, ratified 2026-07-16).

**Root architectural finding (this is the load-bearing result).** The WebGPU MRT-OIT accumulation
path (`WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.executeTranslucentPass`) enters only when
`hasOITPipelines` is true, which needs a `Pass.TRANSLUCENT` command carrying `_shaderCode`
(auto-built into `_oitPipeline`) or a pre-built `_oitPipeline`. Exhaustive grep: the ONLY
`_shaderCode` producers on WebGPU draw commands are `WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer` (splats →
`Pass.GAUSSIAN_SPLATS`) and `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceShaders` (the OPAQUE globe → `Pass.GLOBE`). Neither
lands in `Pass.TRANSLUCENT`; no primitive/model/collection produces `_shaderCode`. Therefore
`hasOITPipelines` is **always false**, and the accumulation path — including the Batch-697
`_ensureSceneColorResolved` composite line — has **never executed** at HEAD.

**Empirical (probe-oit-transparency.mjs, all oracles GREEN):** WebGL OIT-on vs off differ 9.80% at
intersections (OIT genuinely active on WebGL); WebGPU default vs WebGL-off 0.69% (sorted≈sorted);
`CesiumDebug.webgpuOIT(true)` flips the gate (requested/capable/safetyGate true) with 0
device/validation errors but reports `active=false` and stays pixel-identical to the WebGPU default
(parity vs WebGL-OIT-on 10.33% — WebGPU keeps the OIT-*off* look); a synthetic splat with
`_webgpuOITEnabled`+`_splatOITDeferral` armed never sets `_webgpuOITActiveThisFrame`;
`webgpuOIT(false)` restores within the dither noise floor. PNGs read (WebGL-on desaturated WBOIT
deep-overlap vs WebGL-off saturated sorted; WebGPU on≡default≡WebGL-off). Perf spot: OIT-on ≈ OIT-off
(0.4–0.6 ms median CPU/render, null cost shape — path not entered).

**Probe gotcha noted:** the probe recreates the viewer per backend (to control the
`orderIndependentTranslucency` constructor option), which destroys the app device and emits benign
`reason=destroyed` teardown console lines the Node fault-regex over-matches; the real GPU error gate
(`device.onuncapturederror`, `device.lost`) is clean. The probe filters those benign lines.

**Verdict:** NO-GO on defaulting WebGPU OIT on for parity (flip is a visual no-op). Real prerequisite
= `NEW-WEBGPU-OIT-TRANSLUCENT-PRIMITIVE-WIRING` + closing the 2 live FAR-003 adjacencies. Flip
nothing; maintainer ratifies. **Regression net:** ellipsoidprim-translucent + globe-translucency PASS
(the guide's 25.49% "standing FAIL" is RESOLVED → 0.46%), classification-debug clean;
custom-shader-translucency RED (NEW pre-existing Batch-699 finding —
`NEW-WEBGPU-CUSTOMSHADER-TRANSLUCENCYMODE-ALPHA-UNDERAPPLIED`, alpha override under-applied, not this
slice). Full package: `migration_doc/OIT_DEFAULT_FLIP_EVIDENCE_2026-07-18.md`. Files: new
`Tools/visual-regression/probe-oit-transparency.mjs`, `packages/sandcastle/gallery/order-independent-translucency/`,
evidence doc; docs (DEBUGGING_GUIDE, FEATURE_INVENTORY, DEFERRED_WORK, QUEUE C10 §3.2, this log).

## C10-04-SPLAT-ASYNC-SORT — STOP-AND-BLOCK verdict: WebGPU splat FR has no production data producer; the target sync sort never runs in production (BLOCKED, 2026-07-18, Campaign 10 W1)

**Finding (register S6-1 = S11-2; guide H4 STOP-AND-BLOCK #1):** C10-04 targets the synchronous main-thread comparator sort in `WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.maybeSortSplats` (`Array.prototype.sort` over a per-sort `new Float64Array(count)`, uploaded to `sortedIndexBuffer`). The Phase-0 producer trace proves that sort **never executes in production**, so the slice's perf premise is unverifiable and the slice is BLOCKED (no code change — this note + the doc updates are the deliverable). This is a valid honest block (C9-12 precedent).

**Trace (repo-wide, 2026-07-18):**

- Production loader chain exists: `Cesium3DTileContentFactory` (when `GaussianSplat3DTileContent.tilesetRequiresGaussianSplattingExt`) → `GaussianSplat3DTileContent.fromGltf` → `tileset.gaussianSplatPrimitive = new GaussianSplatPrimitive(...)`; splat attributes load via `GltfLoader`/`GltfSpzLoader` into snapshot buffers.
- `GaussianSplatPrimitive.update()` (`:1186`) resolves the FR; when the WebGPU FR is ready it calls `fr.update(this, frameState)` and **returns at `:1197`**. The WebGL data-commit — `commitSnapshot` (`:407`, sets `_positions`/`_indexes`/`gaussianSplatTexture`), `GaussianSplatTextureGenerator`, `buildGSplatDrawCommand` (`:1967`, WebGL `usampler2D` texture + VertexArray + `DrawCommand`) — runs only in the continuation reached AFTER the return (`resolveSteadySort:681` → `commitSnapshot`). Under WebGPU none of it runs.
- The WebGPU FR reads ONLY `primitive._splatData || primitive._renderResources?.splatBuffer` (`WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:1231`) — nothing else off the primitive. `git grep '_splatData ='` = **0** production hits (excl. `_splatDataGeneration`); `git grep '_renderResources ='` = **0**; `_renderResources` is **never referenced** in `GaussianSplatPrimitive.js`.
- Therefore under WebGPU `splatData === undefined` → buffer-build branch (`revision !== cache.lastRevision && splatData`, `:1233`) never fires → `cache.splatBuffer` null, `cache.splatCount` 0 → `maybeSortSplats` returns at the `count === 0` guard (`:920-923`). The renderer never draws.
- Only exerciser: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-splat-sort.mjs` synthetically injects a 3-splat interleaved `_splatData` `Float32Array` onto a hand-rolled fake primitive.
- Independently corroborated by two prior in-tree notes: Batch 288 (below, `## Batch 288`) "the renderer never actually drew before — no `_splatData` producer is wired, so these were dormant"; C10-09 (`## C10-09`... 2026-07-17) "production `_splatData` has no JS producer — C10-04 territory".

**Resolution:** filed **NEW-WEBGPU-SPLAT-DATA-PRODUCER** (`DEFERRED_WORK.md`, 2026-07-18) as the C10-04 prerequisite — the WebGPU analog of `commitSnapshot`/`buildGSplatDrawCommand` that packs the loaded snapshot into the 16-float interleaved `_splatData` record + exposes model-space positions for the sort/depth-key. C10-04 ledger row (`QUEUE_2026-07-16_CAMPAIGN10.md` §3.2) flipped to BLOCKED with the full analysis + smallest-unblock plan. FEATURE_INVENTORY §B splat line annotated (SHIPPED→probe-only-until-producer). Do NOT build the async-sort worker/GPU machinery against data that never arrives (the STOP-AND-BLOCK's "unverifiable async-sort machinery"). Note: the synthetic probe path CAN be scaled to drive + correctness-verify an async rewrite, but such a rewrite cannot claim a default-hot-path banner (no production consumer), so it is premature until the producer lands.

**Files modified:** none (code). Docs: `migration_doc/DEFERRED_WORK.md`, `migration_doc/QUEUE_2026-07-16_CAMPAIGN10.md`, `migration_doc/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md`, this log.

## C10-10-SHADOW-CAST-SINGLE-SWEEP — fold shadow cast-candidate collection into the single PVS walk, killing the second full-`commandList` sweep per shadow map per frame (2026-07-18, Campaign 10 W1 R1)

**Symptom / finding (register S1-2 / deep-dive §1 secondary):** with shadows enabled, the frame builds the per-cascade cast lists with a **second full-`commandList` sweep per shadow map** — `SceneRenderer.insertShadowCastCommands` iterated the *entire* `frameState.commandList`, re-ran `scene.updateDerivedCommands(command)` on every command, allocated a `shadowedPasses = [GLOBE, CESIUM_3D_TILE, OPAQUE, TRANSLUCENT]` literal per call, `.includes`-scanned each command's pass, then light-frustum + per-cascade `isVisible`-culled. This duplicated the walk the PVS pass (`View.createPotentiallyVisibleSet`) already makes over the same list — the PVS loop already visits every command, camera-culls, and (for camera-visible commands) calls `updateDerivedCommands` via `insertIntoBin`. Cost (shadows on, 1 CSM map, N = 3–5k commands): N `updateDerivedCommands` + N `.includes` + N light-frustum tests + (casters × up to 4 cascades) `isVisible` per frame — an O(N × cascades) sweep on scenes already CPU-bound. **PRE evidence** (new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-c10-10-shadow-single-sweep.mjs`, shadowed CSM wall + off-camera box scene): N(commandList)=17–18, K(casters)=2, maps=1, cascades=4, `camInvisCasters=1` (an off-camera caster the camera frustum culls).

**Root cause:** cast-candidate *collection* was a separate pass over the command list rather than folded into the single walk the frame already pays for.

**Fix (backend-agnostic, Scene/View — above the WebGL/WebGPU split; JS-only):** collect a per-frame **caster sublist** during the PVS walk and iterate only that in the cast build.
- `View.js` — module-scope `isShadowedPass[]` lookup (O(1) pass test, replaces the per-call array + `.includes`); persistent `this._shadowCasters` reset by length each PVS (T-5/T-6). In `createPotentiallyVisibleSet`, once `pass` is known: `isCaster = shadowsEnabled && command.castShadows === true && isShadowedPass[pass] === true` (matches the old `!castShadows || !includes` gate exactly — `castShadows` is a strict boolean flag getter). Camera-**INVISIBLE** casters (before the camera-cull `continue`, INV-1) get `scene.updateDerivedCommands(command)` at collection — their ONLY cast-derived-command build site (INV-2 / Trap T-1: `insertIntoBin` never runs for them, so without this the WebGL dispatch reads `derivedCommands.shadows` = undefined → lost/crashed off-screen shadow). Camera-**VISIBLE** and **no-BV** casters push-only (Trap T-2/T-4: `insertIntoBin` builds their derived command — a second call would re-clone every re-dirtied globe caster). Publish `shadowState.casterCommands = shadowCasters` in the `shadowsEnabled` block; `= undefined` when shadows off (Trap T-5).
- `SceneRenderer.js` — `insertShadowCastCommands(scene, casters, shadowMap)` now iterates the sublist doing ONLY the light-frustum `isVisible` + per-cascade/point-light split (INV-3). Removed: the full-`commandList` scan, per-command `updateDerivedCommands`, the `shadowedPasses` literal, the `.includes`. `executeShadowMapCastCommands` reads `shadowState.casterCommands` with a `!defined` conservative no-op guard.
- `FrameState.js` — `shadowState.casterCommands` slot + typedef.

**Why order is safe:** `updateShadowMaps` (which bumps `shadowState.lastDirtyTime`) runs BEFORE PVS (`ViewportExecutor.updateAndRenderPrimitives`), so the cast derived commands `insertIntoBin`/collection build *during* PVS see this frame's finalized shadow state — identical to what the old post-PVS `insertShadowCastCommands` built. Output (`passes[].commandList` + each command's `derivedCommands.shadows`) is byte-identical; only *how* the caster set is gathered changed.

**Verification (probe-first, both backends):** **POST** `probe-c10-10-shadow-single-sweep` OVERALL PASS all 3 cells (WebGPU-CSM / WebGPU-single / WebGL): `setEqual = true` (the folded `casterCommands` set === the set the old full-`commandList` scan would produce, compared by **object reference** in-probe — the tightest fold-parity oracle); `camInvisInSublist === camInvisCasters === 1` (INV-1 off-camera caster preserved through the fold); WebGPU-CSM `castDispatches = 292`; umbra byte-identical PRE↔POST (WebGPU-CSM 25,192 / WebGPU-single 876 / WebGL 28,485); **scene-ROI pixel diff PRE↔POST = 0** (sharp raw-decode; the only PRE↔POST delta is the bottom Cesium-credits DOM strip y696–717, which drifts across page loads), PNGs read — the wall casts the same shadow on both backends. 0 device errors. `probe-csm-cast-dispatch` PASS, `probe-csm-soft-shadow` PASS (PCF parity 1.24×). `probe-contact-shadows` is N/A (screen-space `WebGPUContactShadowsEffect`; does not use `insertShadowCastCommands`). Regression: `probe-frustum-count-3d` PASS (WebGPU=WebGL=1 at all altitudes, sky-only fallback intact — **C10-01 preserved byte-for-byte**), capture-and-diff globe-default crossBackend 0.43% (band 0.43–0.77), `probe-camera-track` 9/9 PASS (meanDiff 0.017%, maxDiff 0.08%, 0 errors both backends). Gates: eslint + `tsc --noEmit` + `gulp build` clean.

**Perf (honest — temp in-build on/off/restored A/B oracle, removed before final):** named-stage cast-BUILD CPU (candidate collection, GPU dispatch excluded) on a WebGPU CSM caster-grid, folded (ON) vs pre-fold full-scan (OFF), counterbalanced reps. N=294/K=256: OLD mean 0.143 ms vs NEW 0.145 ms (flat, below the browser 0.1 ms `performance.now()` clamp). N=1194/K=1156: OLD mean 0.573 ms vs NEW 0.560 ms (**2.2% mean**), p95 within one timer quantum. **Banner NOT claimed** — below the ≥5% p95 / >3× noise bar on achievable offline scenes: these grids have K≈N + static casters, so the eliminated redundant `updateDerivedCommands` is a cheap dirty-check early-return; the dramatic win the register describes needs N≫K with globe/tile casters that re-dirty every frame (Trap T-2), which offline scenes here don't carry — exactly the queue's "default benchmark has no casters" caveat. Default no-shadow route is a structural no-op (collection guarded on `shadowsEnabled`) → whole-route CPU-p95 delta = 0 (INV-5). Truthful miss + green mechanics = VALID COMPLETE. **Follow-up (Principle 9):** a truly *revision-maintained* (rebuilt-only-on-change) sublist depends on a retained command list above the split (S1-6, un-owned next-campaign seed) — out of scope; the single-sweep fold is the achievable win.

**Files modified:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/View.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Scene/SceneRenderer.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Scene/FrameState.js`; new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-c10-10-shadow-single-sweep.mjs`.

## C10-09-VELOCITY-PREV-BUFFER-GPU-COPY — revision-skip + GPU self-copy kills the per-frame static prev-instance re-upload in the point-cloud / splat / cloud TAA velocity path (2026-07-18, Campaign 10 W1 R1)

**Symptom / finding (register S6-2):** three WebGPU renderers keep a CPU mirror of the previous-frame instance buffer for the TAA motion-vector VS and **re-upload the entire array via `queue.writeBuffer` every frame TAA is on** — even for static content whose bytes are identical to what already resides in the current-frame GPU `instanceBuffer`. Measured (new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-c10-09-prev-buffer-upload.mjs`, `writeBuffer`/`copyBufferToBuffer` wrapped by destination buffer label, single render/frame): static `CloudCollection` under TAA = **1 writeBuffer/frame to "Cloud prev instances" = 15,300 B/frame** (225×68 B); frozen `TimeDynamicPointCloud` under TAA = **1 writeBuffer/frame to "PointCloud prev instances" = 40,000 B/frame** (1000×40 B); both with `prevInstanceData === instanceData` (identity/static). The S6 F2 quantification: 1M-splat = 64 MB/frame (~3.8 GB/s, 6–13 ms main-thread memcpy — alone caps ~30 fps). TAA defaults off so default benchmarks don't see it, but it is a hard wall for any "≥2× with TAA" claim on point/splat content. Billboard/Label/Point collections already migrated to `WebGPUResidentInstanceBuffer` (dirty-range coalesced); these three never got that migration.

**Root cause:** no reference/revision check to skip the write, and no GPU-side alternative — the prev buffer is rebuilt from CPU each frame regardless of whether the content changed.

**Fix (three renderers, JS/TS-only, zero shader/pipeline/RTE/layout change):** revision-skip + GPU self-copy for the identity case. Each cache gains a monotonic `instanceDataRevision` bumped at the single `instanceBuffer`/`splatBuffer` content-write (rebuild) site, and a resident `prevBufferRevision` (= the revision whose bytes reside in the prev buffer). The prev-upload block becomes three-branch: (1) **identity** (`prevData === currData` → static) — if `prevBufferRevision !== instanceDataRevision`, seed once via `copyBufferToBuffer(instanceBuffer → prevBuffer)` (the identical bytes already live on the GPU) and record the revision, else do NOTHING; (2) **animated distinct-array** (`prevData !== currData`, sufficient size) — the existing `writeBuffer(prevSrc)` unchanged, reset resident marker; (3) **first-frame / count-change seed** — the existing GPU copy unchanged, reset marker. On every prev-buffer realloc (grow) the resident marker is reset to `undefined` (T-4). `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts` handles BOTH the default VB path (`attachPointCloudVelocityCommand`) and the LOD storage path (`attachLODPointCloudVelocityCommand`, own `lodPrevBufferRevision`); `instanceBuffer` is written ONLY at the rebuild site (the LOD path uploads positions to the LOD processor's own buffers, so one bump site covers both — T-3). Private mid-frame submit left alone (FAR-200 is a separate concern).

**COPY_SRC enabling flag (necessary, in-scope):** the point-cloud and cloud `instanceBuffer`s were created `VERTEX | COPY_DST` — no `COPY_SRC` — so the *pre-existing* seed `copyBufferToBuffer(instanceBuffer → prev)` was latent-broken (it only ever ran on the first-TAA-frame or a count-change, and TAA defaults off, so it was never exercised). The identity-seed now hits `copyBufferToBuffer` reliably, so `COPY_SRC` was added to both `buildInstanceBuffer` usages (the splat renderer already had it for exactly this reason). Benign flag addition; no content/behavior change.

**INV-3 velocity byte-identical:** for static content geometry velocity = 0 in both PRE and POST by construction — the identity-seed copies the same `instanceBuffer` bytes that `writeBuffer(prevSrc = instanceData)` uploaded, so prev ≡ curr either way; camera-induced velocity (via `previousViewProjection`) is untouched. Rendering unchanged (bright cloud px 174,629 → 174,749; the delta is the mutation-test moving one cloud).

**Verification (probe-first):** **POST** — both sites = **0 writeBuffer/frame** at settled (seed fires once during warmup, before the window), `instanceDataRevision === prevBufferRevision`, 0 console/device errors. **Mutation exactness (cloud):** edit one cloud position → mutation frame = 1 `writeBuffer` (animated branch, captures the edit's real velocity — correct), next frame = 1 `copyBufferToBuffer` identity re-seed, then 0/0 forever (bounded per edit, no per-frame re-upload). Gates: `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean, `gulp build` clean; `probe-taa-jitter` GATE PASS; `probe-taa-model-skinned-velocity` PASS (skinned velocity streaks intact, PNG read); `probe-timedynamic-pointcloud-load` PASS (animated non-identity path still captures motion, INV-2); `probe-splat-sort` PASS (T-5: sort writes `sortedIndexBuffer`, untouched); `probe-cloud-property-edit` PASS (rebuild+dirty gate not regressed); `probe-model-instance-bg-cache` settled green; `capture-and-diff globe-default` crossBackend 0.46%. Splat velocity leg not driven live (no offline `.spz`/`.splat`; production `_splatData` has no JS producer — C10-04 territory) — verified by code-inspection parity with the two live sites + splat-sort no-regression.

**Perf (honest, no banner):** named-stage prev-buffer upload on/off oracle (PRE build = off / POST build = on) = **100% elimination** (15.3–40 KB/frame → 0) on TAA + instanced-content scenes; the default moving-altitude route is a structural no-op (no point/splat/cloud primitives + TAA off), so whole-route CPU-p95 delta = 0 by construction; the 1M-splat 64 MB/frame win needs an offline asset unavailable here. **Banner NOT claimed** — whole-route CPU-p95 bar not clearable on the achievable-offline workload; the bandwidth elimination is the structural win that lands the slice (promotion rule: truthful miss + green mechanics = VALID COMPLETE).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts` (each independently revertable), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-c10-09-prev-buffer-upload.mjs` (new). Rollback restores the unconditional per-frame `writeBuffer(prevSrc)`; no velocity/RTE/feature change.

## C10-01-ENV-COMMAND-FRUSTUM-BINNING — BV-less Pass.ENVIRONMENT near/far exclusion collapses the default-3D WebGPU 2-frustum floor to 1 (2026-07-18, Campaign 10 anchor)

**Symptom / finding (register S7-1):** every default 3D WebGPU frame rendered with `scene.numberOfFrustums === 2` (at 18,000 km and at 300 m alike) while WebGL rendered 1. The five WebGPU environment feature renderers push BV-less `Pass.ENVIRONMENT` draw commands into `frameState.commandList` (the Batch-247 dual-path convention: SkyAtmosphere shell + opt-in fullscreen variant, Sun, **Moon**, StarField — five sites, not the register's three). In `View.createPotentiallyVisibleSet` the no-bounding-volume else branch fed the camera worst-case span into the scene near/far accumulators. Under log depth the Scene constructor overrides the camera frustum to `[0.1, 1e10]` (ratio 1e11), so `updateFrustums` computed `ceil(ln(1e11)/ln(1e9)) = 2`. Scene content alone never exceeds ratio ~4.6e8 → content-driven count is 1; the environment commands alone manufactured the second frustum. WebGL never routes these effects through `commandList` (they execute via `environmentState`), so it always ran 1. The empty far band `[1e8, 1e10]` held only sky yet paid the full per-frustum scaffold (~6 render-pass boundaries + 2 fullscreen RGBA8 depth packs + an aux 65,536-object GPU culler + duplicate camera-UB writes + a doubled frustum-loop CPU walk, ≈150–240 MB/frame of attachment traffic — S7-2/S7-5). Same defect class as Batch 268's BV-less command exploding the SCENE2D split 1→~9.

**Root cause:** BV-less `Pass.ENVIRONMENT` commands are directional/full-screen effects with no meaningful world-space extent; treating their extent as the camera's `[0.1, 1e10]` and feeding it into the near/far accumulators (View.js no-BV else branch) forced the log-depth frustum count to its ceiling of 2 on every frame.

**Fix (JS-only, `packages/engine/Source/Scene/View.js`, zero shader/pipeline change):** in `createPotentiallyVisibleSet`, the no-BV else branch is split on pass — commands with `pass === Pass.ENVIRONMENT` still get extent `[frustum.near, frustum.far]` (so they bin into and execute once in the farthest frustum exactly as before, Batch-247 dedupe byte-untouched) but do NOT feed the `near`/`far` accumulators; instead they set a `sawEnvironmentNoBV` flag. Immediately before `updateFrustums`, a sky-only fallback `if (near > far && sawEnvironmentNoBV) { near = frustum.near; far = frustum.far; }` restores the camera window when ONLY BV-less env commands were present (globe hidden, facing space), so those frames keep the frustum(s) they produce today — no black canvas. The exclusion is pass-keyed (covers all five current producers + any future one) and conservative (BV-less commands of any OTHER pass keep the worst-case widening). `Scene.getDebugSnapshot()` gains `frustums.count` so the invariant is observable and a future BV-less near/far-widener regression fails loudly.

**WebGL byte-identical:** no WebGL/shared path pushes `Pass.ENVIRONMENT` into `frameState.commandList` (Trap 4 verified — `CubeMapPanorama` uses the separate `panoramaCommandList`), so the new branch is dead code on WebGL and `sawEnvironmentNoBV` never trips. `MultifrustumSpec`/`FrustumCommandsSpec` construct only BV'd OPAQUE / pure-data cases → never reach the branch.

**Verification (probe-first, Principle 8):** new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-frustum-count-3d.mjs` (both backends, waypoints 18,000 km / 500 km / 300 m + sky-only leg, globe-pipeline-warm gating so the `createRenderPipelineAsync` race doesn't read a cold GLOBE-command-less frame). **PRE:** WebGPU=2 all three (env binned `[3,3]` into both frusta), WebGL=1. **POST:** WebGPU=1===WebGL all three (globe bins 6/36/147 == WebGL); sky-only WebGPU=2 unchanged (fallback, star catalog renders); PNGs read — atmosphere limb + sun + stars + moon pixel-equivalent to PRE and to WebGL. Battery: `tsc`/eslint/`gulp build` clean; capture-and-diff globe-default crossBackend 0.46% + repaired historical lane 0.01% both backends, 5 other globe scenes 0.46–0.75% (high-density-5k-spheres 8.62% = pre-attributed standing red, BV'd OPAQUE spheres untouched); camera-track 9/9 both backends max 0.079% zero errors; celestial battery green (sun/star extinction PARITY match=true, moon dimmer/warmer both backends, atmosphere-orbit 0.42%); 2D safe (`probe-2d-frustum-bins` `noBV=0` in SCENE2D → no-op there; `probe-model-scene-modes` GATE PASS all modes); pick point/billboard PASS; `probe-pickposition-webgpu` red is pre-existing `NEW-WEBGPU-PICKPOSITION-CONVERGENCE-REGRESSION` **confirmed via OFF-oracle** (identical failure with the fix neutralized). Perf spot (clean lane, 2 reps): WebGPU CPU-p95 4.85 ms (~−6.7% vs the 5.20 ms C9-30 reference), WebGL 5.36 ms (flat/noise) — characterization only; structural frustum parity is the landing bar and is met.

**Files:** `Scene/View.js` (two hunks in `createPotentiallyVisibleSet` + `sawEnvironmentNoBV` local), `Scene/Scene.js` (`getDebugSnapshot().frustums.count`), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-frustum-count-3d.mjs` (new), `migration_doc/DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md` + `Tools/visual-regression/README.md` (probe + snapshot-field docs). Rollback = single revert; probe + telemetry survive.

## C9-12A-IMAGERY-SOURCE-REALIZATION-DEDUP-AND-MIP-PREP — one shared imagery realization + frame-owned mip prep; probe-gate attribution (2026-07-17, Batch 685)

**Symptom / finding (C9-01 attribution):** on the moving-camera altitude track the WebGPU globe created **513** identical full-mip imagery `GPUTexture`s (one per terrain tile), each generating mips through a **private `"MipmapGeneration"` command encoder + private `queue.submit` from draw emission** (513 encoders, 513 submits, 4104 `Mipmap_RenderPass_Level*`), retaining **173 MiB with zero retirement** — because `GridImageryProvider` returns the SAME constructor-drawn canvas for every tile yet the cache key was `${x}_${y}_${level}` (per-tile), and the direct-upload path registered no cleanup.

**Root cause:** (a) no source-identity concept — a source reused across tiles was realized once per tile coordinate; (b) mip generation was a synchronous private submit inside `uploadImageSource` (draw emission); (c) the direct-upload branch never destroyed its GPUTexture (the declared `imageryOwnedRetirements` counter was never incremented).

**Fix:**

- New backend-neutral `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/ImagerySourceIdentity.ts` — object-identity id + declared-immutable/`ImageBitmap` shareability verdict (NO pixel hashing). `GridImageryProvider` calls `declareImmutableImagerySource(this._canvas)`.
- New `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSharedImageryRealizations.ts` — per-context, device-scoped table: refcounted shared realizations released with quadtree/imagery lifetime, a byte-budgeted grace LRU (120 frames / 64 MiB, oldest-first), `destroyAll` on teardown/device change; destruction only via `context.scheduleTextureDestroy`.
- `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.uploadImageSource` — for a shareable imagery source, share one realization (fingerprint = `sourceId·revision | WxH | rgba8unorm | mips | flipY | srgb`), reusing the ONE view (which also collapses the group-1 bind-group key); for non-shareable/owned sources, keep an owned texture but now retire it on eviction. Mips are enqueued (`WebGPUContext.enqueueImageryMipGeneration`), never submitted here.
- `WebGPUContext.endFrame` — encodes all pending mip jobs into ONE `"ImageryMipPreparation"` encoder submitted **before** the frame encoder in the same `queue.submit` (queue order: `copyExternalImageToTexture` → mip passes → scene passes → complete mips sampled the same frame). Zero private submits from draw emission.

**Probe-gate attribution (the Batch-683 block, resolved this batch):** the WIP had been stranded on branch `c9-12a-imagery-dedup-wip` because `probe-grid-multizoom` check A (grid lines render at both zooms) failed with the WIP applied but passed on clean 682 — an unexplained A/B flip. Batch 685 ran the attribution protocol: 3 reps on clean main@684 + 3 reps on the branch build, with the probe printing full console-error CONTENTS (the `ImageryMipPreparation`/command-buffer-invalid text would be the combined-submit fingerprint). Result: **all 6 reps byte-identical across builds** — 400 m renders 1260/1263 line-runs on both backends, 2000 m is a **black canvas on BOTH backends, zero errors, no fingerprint text ever**. The WIP is exonerated; the gate was red because of a **probe-scene framing defect**: at alt 2000 with pitch −35° from a fixed 333 m south offset, the polygon spans 65.6–86° depression while the frustum's bottom edge is at 65° (60° vfov) — the subject is deterministically OUT OF FRAME. The probe was reframed to true nadir (pitch −90 over the polygon, ALTS 700/2000 — matching its own "straight down" header), hardened (error contents + pageerror printed, try/finally browser close, `prim.ready` settle), thresholds unchanged → 3/3 GREEN on main and 3/3 GREEN on the branch build, byte-identical (gpuRatio 1.33). Forensic note: the C2-10 authoring notes (`DEFERRED_WORK.md` C2-10 RESOLUTION) recorded far-zoom line measurements ("close/far zoom ratio 1.5") that are **unreproducible with the committed camera** at ≥682 on either backend — either the recorded numbers came from a pre-commit probe variant or camera behavior changed after authoring; the reframe restores an honestly-measurable gate either way.

**Verification (Batch 685, applied diff on main):** `npx eslint`/`npx tsc --noEmit`/`npx gulp build` clean; `probe-imagery-tex` PASS; reframed `probe-grid-multizoom` GATE PASS; `capture-and-diff globe-default` crossBackend PASS **0.46%** (PNGs read — correct mipped SF-Bay imagery, diff chrome-only); `probe-demand-canvas-pass` ALL PASS both backends (combined submit coexists with C9-07 demand-clear); `probe-terrain-selection-parity` (GridImagery) **webglHash === webgpuHash exact**. Shares reconciliation (runtime `__webgpuGlobeLogicalCounters` + an `enqueueImageryMipGeneration` wrapper, GridImagery 3-altitude route): `imageryRealizationsCreated`=**1**, `imageryRealizationShares`=**31**, `imageryRealizationLiveBytes`=**349,524** (one 256² full-mip texture), owned live textures/bytes **0**, `imageryMipFallbackSubmits`=**0**, pending jobs after settle 0, exactly ONE imagery-labelled mip-prep job. The same instrumentation surfaced a **pre-existing** ~37/frame `Globe oceanNormal` re-upload+mip-enqueue storm from the per-tile water/ocean bind-group path (identical call path + missing cache guard on clean main, which also paid a private submit per call) — filed as `NEW-WEBGPU-OCEANNORMAL-PER-CALL-REUPLOAD` in `DEFERRED_WORK.md` (exact mechanism there); not fixed in this slice.

**Files:** `Renderer/ImagerySourceIdentity.ts` (new), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSharedImageryRealizations.ts` (new), `Renderer/WebGPU/{WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures,WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer,WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTypes,WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileBuffers,WebGPUContext,WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapCapture}.ts`, `Scene/GridImageryProvider.js`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-grid-multizoom.mjs` (reframed + hardened).

**Hardening pass (Batch 686 — 16-agent adversarial review provenance):** the C9-12A implementation had never been reviewed (the original author session hung; audit R6 was blocked), so a 16-agent adversarial review ran before landing: 10 findings verified with quoted code (3 P1, 7 P2), 3 refuted. All 10 fixed/dispositioned in the same uncommitted diff:

- **F0 (P1) multi-viewer clock + pinned context:** the renderer (and therefore the table) is per pooled `GPUDevice` — two viewers share one table. The table now keeps its OWN monotonic clock (one tick per `sweep`; scene `frameNumber`s are only per-renderer edge detectors), and `release`/`sweep`/`destroyAll` take a `scheduleDestroy` callback supplied by the CALLING context at call time — no constructor-injected closure, so a dead first context can no longer pin destruction to inline `texture.destroy()` while the device lives on for another viewer. Module docstring corrected (per-renderer, not per-context).
- **F1 (P2) refcount leak:** `removeImageryTexture`'s shared branch deleted the cache entry without `table.release()` — the identity-guarded imagery cleanup then early-returned, orphaning the reference forever. The branch now releases (and hits the retirement/live-bytes counters).
- **F2 (P2) streamed-bitmap class:** entries track `everShared` (any `get` hit / refCount>1). Never-shared realizations (unique streamed per-tile bitmaps) retire PROMPTLY at zero refs via the caller's scheduleDestroy (owned-path parity); the zero-ref pool is bounded HARD — over `BYTE_BUDGET` the sweep retires oldest-first regardless of age (age exemption only under budget), so churn can no longer grow the pool unboundedly.
- **F3 (P1) private-submit zero mips:** new `WebGPUContext.flushPendingImageryMipJobs()` (encode + immediate submit, no-op when empty). Called from `WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapCapture.runSceneCapture` immediately before its private submit (it replays globe tile commands with the imagery bind groups — same-frame realizations would sample zero-initialized mips at cube-face resolution) and from `WebGPUContext.readPixelsAsync`'s mid-frame frame-encoder submit. All other `queue.submit(` sites under `Renderer/WebGPU` were audited: readback-only copies (CSM debug, pick framebuffer, buffer mapper, compute engine) and private-resource generators (BRDF LUT, IBL, cloud noise, atmosphere LUT, SH/sky env-map passes, reprojection Route B, effects clears, stubs, FFT ocean, point cloud, splats, fog, weather, NPR, texture atlas) never sample direct-upload imagery realizations — no flush needed. Pick mini-frames route through the shared `endFrame` and are covered inherently. Runtime demonstration: synthetic probe on the live context (enqueue real 3-mip job → flush → queue drained, `popErrorScope` clean, no-op path clean); the capture call site itself is verified by inspection — the scene-capture feature is double-opt-in with no existing probe/Sandcastle scene.
- **F7 (P1) destroy-skip over-reach:** the endFrame mip encode previously skipped any texture in `_pendingTextureDestroys` — but scheduled textures stay LIVE until after the submit and this frame's draws still sample them (their mip chains were being dropped). The skip now applies ONLY to textures explicitly destroyed inline, tracked via `WebGPUContext.noteInlineTextureDestroy` (a WeakSet) stamped at the inline-destroy sites (`removeImageryTexture` owned branch, renderer-destroy water-mask/ocean-normal cache loops).
- **F8 (P2) atomic-submit coupling:** the prep buffer is now its own `queue.submit([prepBuffer])` immediately before `queue.submit([frameBuffer])` — same-queue ordering is guaranteed, and an invalid prep buffer can no longer invalidate the whole frame. Capture-and-clear of the job list retained.
- **F4 (P2) sweep per tile:** the sweep ran inside `createTileCommands` (per tile). Now gated by a `_lastRealizationSweepFrame` frameNumber edge detector — once per frame per scene; with F0's self-clock, multi-scene sharing just ages the pool faster (safe direction).
- **F6 (P2) dead device guard:** `table.device !== device` is unreachable with the per-device renderer construction; kept as cheap defense with a truthful comment. No behavior change.
- **F5 (P2) cross-layer key collision — ROOT-FIXED:** the C9-12A cleanup had converted the FILED stale-texture aliasing into delete/recreate churn; the root fix landed within the review's envelope — `imageryCacheKey(imagery)` prefixes a stable per-`ImageryLayer` WeakMap id (`L{n}_x_y_level`; both derivation sites route through it). Memory stays deduped for shareable sources (the realization table below the cache keys on source identity). **Gated at runtime:** the reconciliation probe now runs TWO GridImagery layers — `imageryRealizationsCreated`=**2** (collision would leave 1), mip-job labels `Globe L1_1_0_1` + `Globe L2_1_0_1`, shares=62, liveBytes=699,048 (exactly 2×349,524), zero errors. The `NEW-WEBGPU-IMAGERY-CACHE-KEY-CROSS-LAYER-COLLISION` DEFERRED_WORK entry can close.
- **F9 (P2) probe gate strength:** `probe-grid-multizoom` keeps the nadir zoom pair AND restores a close OBLIQUE waypoint (C2-10-style anisotropic derivatives); check A requires INTERIOR-region lines (central third of the band) at every waypoint; WebGL's own zoom ratio is gated identically to WebGPU's. Honest re-baseline: interior medians remove the polygon-border pollution that had WebGL's global-median ratio at 2.0 — measured gpuRatio **1.33** / glRatio **1.5**, both < 1.8 (threshold unchanged), 2 reps byte-identical, zero errors, PNGs read.

**Post-hardening verification (Batch 686):** `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npx gulp build` + eslint/prettier clean; hardened `probe-grid-multizoom` 2/2 GATE PASS; `probe-imagery-tex` PASS; `probe-demand-canvas-pass` ALL PASS both backends; `capture-and-diff globe-default` crossBackend PASS 0.46% (unchanged); two-layer shares reconciliation PASS (above); F3 synthetic flush probe PASS.

**Left for separate slices (Principle 9):** the oceanNormal per-call re-upload storm (`NEW-WEBGPU-OCEANNORMAL-PER-CALL-REUPLOAD`) — pre-existing, unchanged by this batch (its inline-destroy sites are now F7-stamped).

## C9-07-DEMAND-OPEN-CANVAS-PASS / FAR-405-C0 — demand-open the default canvas render pass (2026-07-16)

**Files affected:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts`,
`packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`,
`packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererPassRedirect.ts`,
`Tools/visual-regression/probe-demand-canvas-pass.mjs` (new acceptance probe).

**Root cause (performance, not a rendering bug):** every WebGPU frame opened the
`"Scene Main Render Pass"` (canvas swap-chain pass) twice — unconditionally in `beginFrame()`
(immediately ended by the scene-FB redirect) and unconditionally after the post-process blit
(`_runPostProcessing` tail resume) — and BOTH were empty on the default route (C9-05 API lane:
2,250/2,250 empty over 1,125 frames; re-confirmed live pre-change: 2,394/2,394 over 1,197 frames).

**Fix (safe boundary per the C9 ledger):** `beginFrame` keeps encoder/swap-view/depth-texture
acquisition but no longer opens the pass; `_beginDefaultRenderPass` derives its load ops from new
per-frame demand flags — the FIRST open of a frame clears each untouched channel (depth is
load-bearing: untouched depth reads lazy-zero 0.0, not the historical 1.0), re-opens load; explicit
`_activePassTarget` (`"default-canvas" | "scene-framebuffer" | "external"`) replaces the `clear()`
label-prefix inference and is nulled at every encoder end site; the background clear defers to the
pending first-open clear; PP blit + debug overlays mark the canvas written
(`markCanvasContentWritten()` — they write via raw encoder passes); legacy overlay draws demand-open
in `executeDrawCommand`; `endFrame` presents a `"Canvas Demand Clear Pass"` clear only when the
acquired swap view was never touched (empty scene / truncated frames; pick mini-frames excluded by
the null swap view).

**Verification:** moving-route API lane SMRP opens 2,394→0 (total −2 passes/frame, zero errors);
`probe-demand-canvas-pass.mjs` pre/post both backends — empty-scene canvas BYTE-IDENTICAL to
pre-change, request-render retention/update, resize, debug overlays (+MSAA1 overlay writes 100%
non-black); probe-2d-globe-render / probe-taa-jitter / probe-point-pick-webgpu /
probe-collections-regression / capture-and-diff green. `probe-pickposition-webgpu` failure attributed
pre-existing via stash-rebuild-rerun (see queue row `NEW-WEBGPU-PICKPOSITION-CONVERGENCE-REGRESSION`).
Audit GO-WITH-FIXES follow-up (2026-07-16): probe case 1 strengthened to a canvas-element capture
gated on the CENTER third of the canvas (the old full-page >20% nonBlack gate passed on UI chrome
alone with a black globe interior); the strengthened gate correctly reddens on the pre-existing
BIMODAL offline WebGPU black-globe-interior repro (center avgRGB 2,2,2, tilesLoaded=true, zero
errors; reproduced byte-identically on the pre-change tree) now ledgered on the
`NEW-WEBGPU-PICKPOSITION-CONVERGENCE-REGRESSION` queue row — all other assertions, including
empty-scene byte-identity, remain green.

## NEW-MODEL-IBL-AMBIENT-RELAND — model IBL ambient olive tint: SH cube-lookup flip + faithful czm_computeScattering port (2026-07-04)

**Files affected:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/ProjectRadianceToSH.wgsl`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/ProceduralSkyCubemap.wgsl`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapManager.ts`.

**Context:** re-land of the audited-GO fix from the NEW-MODEL-SCENE2D-SHADING (B3) attempt, which had been auto-reverted by a since-fixed harness gate flaw (not a code defect). The B3 investigation DISPROVED the SCENE2D light-direction premise: every SCENE2D lighting input is mode-consistent with WebGL; the divergence was ENTIRELY the always-on IBL ambient — a mode-INDEPENDENT defect that top-down SCENE2D merely maximizes (the milk-truck roof read olive instead of WebGL's blue-gray).

**Root causes (two, both in the WebGPU dynamic-env IBL pipeline):**

1. **`ProjectRadianceToSH.wgsl` sampled the radiance cube RAW** where WebGL's `ComputeIrradianceFS.glsl:94-95` applies a `(-x, -y, z)` lookup flip. The Batch-354 claim that raw sampling was an intentional backend difference was NUMERICALLY DISPROVEN (JS re-projection with the flip reproduces WebGL SH c1 blue 0.151 vs 0.152; raw gives 0.029 — 5× short = the olive tint). Fix: apply the flip.
2. **`ProceduralSkyCubemap.wgsl`'s scattering march diverged from `czm_computeScattering` / `ComputeRadianceMapFS`**: uniform 16-step midpoint integrator vs WebGL's adaptive scheme (tanh split weights → 4 primary / 2 light steps from inside the atmosphere, growing step length, full-step sample placement); a fixed 111 km ray clamp vs WebGL's 1.025R `atmosphereOuterRadius` ray-length semantics; no onEllipsoid classification (down rays marched through the planet; sky/ground split was the local hemisphere sign); near-degenerate NONE-mode light direction (the 111 km-capped sky point normalizes to ~zenith; WebGL's `normalize(skyPositionWC)` at 1.025R is direction-dependent); no skyAlpha composite; radii packed as |position| / +111 km instead of WebGL's `|scaleToGeodeticSurface(position)|` / ×1.025 (`DynamicEnvironmentMapManager.js` `atmosphereNeedsUpdate`). Fix: faithful line-for-line port (including `czm_approximateTanh` + the Batch-304 precision-scaled `czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval`), ellipsoidHeight-aware view origin via uniform slot 39 (the reserved always-0 pad — add-only, byte offsets unchanged), skyAlpha composite over black, ground blend by `ellipsoidHeight/atmosphereHeight`, and the manager packing the WebGL radii semantics. ENV-AERIAL-MS LUT path + both cloud-IBL paths untouched.

**Verification (2026-07-04 00:37–00:58 EDT, same-session clean-HEAD baselines — wall-clock pinned because magnitudes are time-of-day dependent):** `probe-model-scene-modes` GATE FAIL→PASS with ALL THREE modes improving: 3D interiorDiff 13.81→10.94, **2D 34.42→11.85** (pulled into the 3D/CV band), CV 18.36→10.30. White-box SH check (re-dispatch of the live SH pipeline against the live cube): WebGPU c1 blue **0.1513** vs WebGL **0.1512** (pre-fix ~0.03). PNGs read: 2D roof blue-gray on both backends, olive gone. Off-gate: zero WebGL-file edits; standing gates probe-cloud-ibl-full / probe-env-temporal / probe-ibl-hdr green post-fix; probe-model-ibl + probe-model-pbr-ibl-parity re-baselined same-hour (both GREEN at this clock even at clean HEAD — the NEW-PROBES-RED-AT-HEAD-IBL-PAIR redness is sun-elevation dependent) and not regressed.

## ENV-SKYBOX-STARMAP — skybox star cube-map mirrored + half-dimmed on WebGPU (2026-07-02)

**Files affected:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCubeMapPanoramaRenderer.js` (only).

**Symptom (user-reported, screenshot):** the milky-way/faint-star cube-map background no longer visible on WebGPU — only the bright catalog stars (StarField point renderer) remained. Suspected regression in Batches 482–497.

**Root cause — two longstanding defects, NOT a 482–497 regression:**

1. **Cube-face vertical mirror (wrong sky region).** WebGL loads skybox faces with `UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL=true` (`Renderer/loadCubeMap.js` `flipY: true`); the WebGPU panorama loader's `copyExternalImageToTexture` did not flip, so every face sampled vertically mirrored and the visible star map was a different sky region than WebGL for the same camera. Fix: `{ source, flipY: true }` in `loadCubeMap`.
2. **Unconditional cloud-cover star occlusion at 50%.** The Phase 1.4 occlusion multiplies the cube-map color by `(1 - cloudCover)` in `CubeMapPanorama` WGSL, and the uniform pack read `atmosphericConditions.weather.cloudCover` (→ `globe.cloudCoverage`, **default 0.5**) ungated. Every default WebGPU scene dimmed the skybox to 50% — the faint texture fell below visibility while the catalog StarField (which never applied cloud cover) kept drawing: "star map gone, sparse dots remain". WebGL's `SkyBoxFS.glsl` applies no cloud occlusion. Fix: gate the packed `cloudCover` on `weather.enabled === true` (`scene.enableWeather`, default false) — the occlusion is now opt-in alongside the rest of the weather system, matching the existing default-off gate of the Phase 1.3b star-brightness modulation.

**Verification:** `probe-env-skybox-stars.mjs` (new acceptance + standing gate): density ratio 0.62→0.97, luminance ratio 0.76→0.89, aligned pattern correlation 1.00 vs mirrored 0.12 (same sky region as WebGL), 0 device errors; opt-in check (weather on + `cloudCoverage=1`) still fully occludes stars and restores on disable. Standing probes for Batches 489/490 + stars-HDR pass. NOTE: `probe-colorgrading-wired` (checks D/F), `probe-pp-library-builtins` (off-gate restored-vs-default), and `probe-globe-translucency` (~22% mismatch) were verified **already failing at HEAD with identical diff numbers before this fix** — pre-existing, not caused by this change.

## GLOBE-CLIPPOLY-GEODETIC — clipping polygons never worked end-to-end on WebGPU (globe OR model data path) (2026-07-02)

**Files affected:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/ClippingPolygonCollection.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUClippingPolygonCollection.ts`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Globe/GlobeTerrain.wgsl`.

**Symptom (task premise vs reality):** the parity report described a ~0.19° geocentric-vs-geodetic boundary offset in the globe FS SDF lookup (GlobeTerrain.wgsl). Live-code audit showed the gap was much wider — `globe.clippingPolygons` produced **no clipping at all** on WebGPU, and the Batch 160/163 model WGSL (`modelClipByPolygon`) was starving for data:

1. **No CPU pack on WebGPU** — `ClippingPolygonCollection.update` early-returns into the feature renderer, skipping `packPolygonsAsFloats`, so `_extentsFloat32View` / `_extentsCount` (which `WebGPUEffectsBindGroup` packs into `clippingPolygonControl`/`clippingPolygonExtents`) were never populated → `invDim = 0` → `modelClipByPolygon` early-out.
2. **Producer packed the wrong layout** — `updateWebGPUClippingPolygons` packed raw geodetic `(lon, lat)` pairs with **no header/extent pixels**, which the SDF compute shader (a port of `PolygonSignedDistanceFS.glsl` expecting `[header|extent×2|vertices…]` in spherical fastApproximateAtan2 coords) cannot consume.
3. **Consumer read fields nobody wrote** — the effects bind group looked for `polyCache._signedDistanceTexture` / `._sdfSampler`; the producer stored `signedDistanceTexture`/`sampler` → `hasPolygonClipping` was permanently false, placeholder SDF always bound.
4. **Globe renderer never passed the collection** — `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer` omitted `clippingPolygons` from `createEffectsBindGroup`, so `effects.clippingPolygonCount` stayed 0 for every globe tile.
5. **Globe FS used the wrong convention AND wrong offsets** — the naive block derived exact geocentric `atan2` lon/lat and sampled a whole-globe equirect UV (the SDF is a per-merged-extent atlas in fastApproximateAtan2 spherical coords — upstream uses `czm_approximateSphericalCoordinates`, NOT geodetic, on both authoring and lookup sides). The globe `EffectsUniforms` struct was also missing the `edgeControl`/`edgeViewport` slots (offsets 272/288), so `pointLightControl` read offset 272 instead of 304 — a latent Batch 108 globe point-light receive misalignment, fixed as a side effect.

**Fix:**

1. `ClippingPolygonCollection.packDataForFeatureRenderer(maxTextureSize)` — new `@private` method running the SAME `packPolygonsAsFloats` CPU pack the WebGL path uses (scene-logic-extractor pattern: shared packing, backend-specific upload). Returns the packed texture layout.
2. `WebGPUClippingPolygonCollection.ts` rewritten — uploads `_float32View` (rg32float, upstream `[header|extent×2|vertices…]` layout) + `_extentsFloat32View` (rgba32float merged extents), allocates the SDF atlas r32float at the upstream `max(128, ceil(4096·quality))` resolution, and dispatches the **canonical** `Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/PolygonSignedDistance.wgsl` (deleted the stale inline WGSL duplicate). Change detection mirrors upstream (totalPositions + length).
3. `WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js` — SDF lookup reads the fields the producer actually writes (`signedDistanceTextureView`/`sdfSampler`).
4. `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts` — passes `tileProvider.clippingPolygons` (enabled && length > 0) into `createEffectsBindGroup` + gate condition.
5. `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` — `EffectsUniforms` grows `edgeControl`/`edgeViewport` (byte-parity padding, fixes point-light offsets) + the Batch 160 `clippingPolygonControl`/`clippingPolygonExtents` tail (offsets 336/352); the naive equirect block is replaced by `globeClipByPolygon(v_positionMC)` — a verbatim parity port of `modelClipByPolygon` (fastApproximateAtan2 spherical coords, merged-extent region select, atlas slot sample, inverse-flag handling at all early-outs). The fork-invented polygon "edge highlight" was dropped (WebGL globe has no polygon edge styling — discard only).

**Verification:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-globe-clippoly-geodetic.mjs` (new) — hexagonal clipping polygon at 45°N on a solid-color globe, top-down camera, UI hidden: hole present on BOTH backends (center 100% background), WebGL-vs-WebGPU mismatch **0.06%** (boundary aligned), PNGs read. Off-gate: WebGPU default globe (no polygons) screenshot **byte-identical** pre-change vs post-change build (determinism verified with a double-capture first). Standing `probe-clipping-planes-parity.mjs` visual diff 2.97% ≈ its recorded 2.35–2.4% UI-noise baseline (its sync-`scene.pick` section reports 0 hits on WebGPU — the known intrinsic cold-start sync-pick gap, unrelated). `npx gulp build` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## PARITY-CLIP-PLANES — model clipping planes clipped the wrong space on WebGPU (2026-06-30)

**Files affected:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUClippingPlaneCollection.ts`, `packages/engine/Source/Scene/Model/Model.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`.

**Symptom:** `model.clippingPlanes = new ClippingPlaneCollection({ planes: [new ClippingPlane(new Cartesian3(1,0,0), 0)] })` clipped the correct half on WebGL but had **no visible effect on WebGPU** — the full model rendered. (A position-independent plane such as `normal=(0,0,0), distance=-1` *did* clip everything, proving the bind-group wiring + `modelClipByPlanes` discard were live; only the position-dependent test was wrong.)

**Root cause:** `updateWebGPUClippingPlanes` bakes the per-plane eye-space equation on the CPU using **only** `uniformState.inverseViewTranspose` (world→eye). That is correct for the **globe** (planes are authored in world/ECEF space) but wrong for a **Model**: a model's clipping planes are authored in **model-local** space and must be taken `model-local → world → eye`. WebGL does exactly that per-fragment via `model._clippingPlanesMatrix = inverseTranspose(view3D · referenceMatrix · clippingPlanes.modelMatrix)` (`Model.updateReferenceMatrices`) fed to `czm_transformPlane`. The WebGPU packer skipped the `referenceMatrix · collection.modelMatrix` factor entirely, so the plane `(1,0,0,0)` in the model's ENU frame was treated as an ECEF plane and clipped nothing in view.

**Fix:**

1. `WebGPUClippingPlaneCollection.ts` — fold an optional owner world matrix (`collection._webgpuOwnerMatrix`) **and** the collection's own `modelMatrix` into the eye-space transform: `planeTransform = inverseTranspose(view · ownerMatrix · collection.modelMatrix)`. Byte-identical fast path preserved: when both are identity (globe / any world-space-authored collection) the code never builds the combined matrix and falls through to the original `inverseViewTranspose`-only transform (guarded by an `isIdentityMat4` check).
2. `Model.js::updateClippingPlanes` — stash `model.referenceMatrix ?? modelMatrix` on `_clippingPlanes._webgpuOwnerMatrix` each frame before `.update(frameState)`. WebGL ignores this transient field; only the WebGPU packer reads it.
3. `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl::fragmentPickMain` — added the same runtime-gated `modelClipByPlanes` / `modelClipByPolygon` discards the color path already has, so clipped-away geometry is not pickable (matching WebGL). Runtime-gated on `effects.clippingPlaneCount > 0u` (no new ShaderDefine; consistent with the existing color-path clipping and byte-identical when count=0).

**Verification:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-clipping-planes-parity.mjs` (new). WebGL vs WebGPU on a CesiumMilkTruck glTF with a +X-half clip: visual mismatch **16.36% → 2.35%** (residual is help-overlay/logo AA edges); WebGPU PNG read confirms the model is now clipped to the same half as WebGL. Off-gate: a no-clip model render is byte-identical (full truck, both backends). `npx gulp build` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

**Known remaining gap (pre-existing, NOT clipping-related):** WebGPU `scene.pick` returns `undefined` for a standalone `Model.fromGltfAsync` model in this scene (0 hits with clipping OFF too), so the pick-parity leg of the probe cannot pass yet. This is a separate WebGPU model-pick gap; the pick-shader clip discard added here is correct and will take effect once that gap is closed. Surfaced per Principle 9.

## Batch 428 — A-LUT-REPARAM: sun-relative sky-view LUT keystone (NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE) (2026-06-29)

**Item:** Phase-1 keystone (P0) — the root blocker `NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE`. The old WebGPU atmosphere inscatter bake (`AtmosphereLUT.wgsl::computeInscatter`) parameterizes only `(cosViewZenith × altitude)` in a synthetic Y-up frame, so it carries no view↔sun azimuth axis and cannot represent sky color off the sun meridian. That is why `ENABLE_SKY_INSCATTER_LUT=false` and why SKY-MS (Batch 427) gets no directional lift.

**Approach:** Added a NEW sun-relative **sky-view LUT** (Hillaire 2020) rather than re-parameterizing the existing inscatter LUT in place — the inscatter LUT is sampled directly by the globe/voxel/splat/point-cloud + primitive fog-drape paths (`sampleAtmosphereFogLut`, gated on `effects.atmosphereLutControl.x > 0.5`, which is true whenever the perf manager has LUT resources), so re-paramming it would break their output and violate flag-off parity. New table: `computeSkyView` writes a 256×128 rgba16float texture, U = relative view↔sun azimuth `[0,π]`, V = Hillaire horizon-warped view-zenith. Rides the existing group-1 extended bind group (added binding 6), dispatched chained after the single-scatter bake.

**Bug found during bring-up:** first flag-on capture was ~37× too dark (lum 6 vs inline 223) despite correct directionality. Root cause: `computeSkyView` derived the sun's elevation as `dot(sunDirection, (0,1,0)) = sunDir.y` — but `sunDirection` is the WORLD sun direction, whose `.y` is unrelated to the observer's local sun zenith at an arbitrary lat/lon. **Fix:** thread the observer-relative sun-zenith cosine (`dot(sunDir, normalize(cameraWC))`) through the params `_pad2`→`sunCosZenith` slot and place the synthetic-frame sun at that elevation. After the fix: meridian horizon lum 205.8 vs inline 223.1 (close), strong correct azimuthal variation (warm/bright near the sun → cool/dim anti-sun), no seams/banding/f16-blowout.

**Opt-in + parity:** `skyAtmosphere.useScatteringLut` (default false) → `u.debug.z`. Flag-off byte-identical to pre-change (stash-baseline diff **0.0000% mismatch, maxDelta 0**) — the default path never samples the new LUT; the new bake writes a texture nothing reads.

**Files:** `Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl` (computeSkyView + sunCosZenith param), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAtmosphereLUT.ts` (sky-view texture + bind group binding 6 + dispatch + sunCosZenith pack), `Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/SkyAtmosphere.wgsl` (skyViewLut binding 6 + sampleSkyViewLut + debug.z path), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js` (flag thread + skyViewReady + sunCosZenith bake input + binding 6), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPerformanceManager.ts` (skyViewView passthrough), `Scene/SkyAtmosphere.js` (`useScatteringLut` property), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-sky-view-lut.mjs` (NEW).

## Batch 423 — Weather particles never rendered: two latent gaps closed by the Phase E wiring (2026-06-28)

**Item:** Atmospheric Effects Phase E (wiring slice) — drive `effects.precipitation` into the existing `WebGPUWeatherRenderer`. While wiring it I found the renderer was effectively dormant: the GPU compute simulation ran every frame, but NO particles were ever drawn.

**Root cause (two stacked bugs):**
1. **Control-surface disconnect.** The env-effects dispatch (`WebGPUSceneRendererEnvironmentalEffects.ts`) passed `scene` directly as the 3rd arg to `updateWeatherParticles(context, frameState, weatherConfig)`. The renderer reads its config off that object (`weatherConfig.enabled/type/intensity/…`), but `scene` has NO `.enabled`/`.type`/`.intensity` — only the flat `_enableWeather`/`weatherType`/`weatherIntensity` fields (the `atmosphericConditions.weather` facade writes those). So `weatherConfig.type`/`intensity`/`wind` silently fell back to defaults and `weatherConfig.enabled` was `undefined`.
2. **Render half never reached + 2-target pipeline.** Env effects run AFTER post-process (Batch 127); the post-frustum chain ENDS the active render pass before the chain runs (the snapshot `copyTextureToTexture` at `WebGPUSceneRendererPostFrustumChain.ts:255` fires whenever any env effect — including weather — is enabled). So `context.currentRenderPassEncoder` was null in the weather block and the render half was skipped (`renderInitialized` stayed false forever). Even once forced to run, the weather render pipeline used `makeSceneFBTargets(...)` which (MRT mode on globally) produced a 2-target `[bgra8unorm, rgba16float]` descriptor — incompatible with the 1-attachment canvas default pass → "Attachment state not compatible" validation error.

**Fix:**
- Dispatch builds a real `CesiumWeatherConfig` from the flat `scene.weather*` fields (`buildWeatherConfig`), mapping the numeric `weatherType` → renderer string. These are the SAME fields the facade writes and the 417a auto-master pushes → one control surface for manual + automatic precip.
- Weather render half resumes the default canvas pass (`context.resumeDefaultRenderPass()`, loadOp:"load") when no pass is active, and draws the particles on top of the post-processed scene.
- Weather render pipeline now declares a SINGLE canvas-format alpha-over target (not the scene-FB MRT layout); format keys off `presentationFormat` (canvas) not `scenePipelineFormat` (HDR scene FB).
- `applyAtmosphericConditions` pushes `effects.precipitation.{enabled,type,intensity}` to the flat scene fields under `effects.auto`. New `PrecipitationType` enum (`0=none,1=rain,2=snow,3=fog,4=hail`) + `precipitationTypeToString` is the single index→string home.

**Verification (`probe-precip-wiring.mjs`, WebGPU-only, PNGs READ):** drove precip through BOTH the auto hierarchy and the direct facade. Snow renders strongly (4272-px union footprint vs a 0-px auto-off control), rain renders subtly (~1000 px) but cleanly beats the zero control, rain ≠ snow (1059-px delta), 0 device errors. Snow PNG shows white flakes distributed across sky + bay + city; OFF baseline has none.

**Files:** `WebGPUSceneRendererEnvironmentalEffects.ts`, `WebGPUWeatherRenderer.ts`, `Scene/AtmosphericEffects.ts`, `Renderer/WebGPU/cesium-js-types.d.ts`, `scripts/build.js`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-precip-wiring.mjs`.

**Lessons:** a feature can be "SHIPPED" in the inventory (the particle system, Session 62) yet have a dead consumer path. The compute-runs-but-nothing-draws shape is exactly the Principle-7 anti-pattern ("called every frame but produces no visible output → the consumer half is missing") — here the consumer (render pass) genuinely WAS missing its pass, so it was a real gap to finish, not scaffolding to leave alone.

## Batch 366 — WebGPU cloud quad 2× too wide; `*0.5` half-extent fix (NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-SIZE-PARITY) (2026-06-23)

**Item:** NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-SIZE-PARITY — the B365 residual: with the worley grain finally matching WebGL, the WebGPU CloudCollection cloud was still ~1.9× linear larger than WebGL at the same maximumSize+camera. B365 had (correctly) ruled out the noise and verified the raymarch/Gardner/TR/color WGSL line-by-line identical, hypothesizing a "non-shader cause."

**Root cause (pinned by the backlog-triage workflow):** the quad-offset **half-extent**. The cloud quad VB spans `quadPos ∈ [-1,1]` (half-extent 1.0), and `vertexMain` scaled the FULL `quadPos` by `scale * projScale`. WebGL's quad uses `offset = dir - 0.5 ∈ [-0.5,0.5]` (half-extent 0.5; `CloudCollectionVS.glsl:34` adds `scale * offset` in eye space). So the WebGPU quad was exactly **2× too wide**. The raymarch varying `vOffset = quadPos*0.5` was ALREADY correctly halved, which is why the noise/shape/grain all matched while only the SIZE was off — the ellipsoid filled a 2×-oversized quad.

**Fix:** a single `* 0.5` on the quad offset in `vertexMain` AND `vertexVelocityMain` (so velocity covers the same fragments). The raymarch coordinate (`vOffset`) is untouched.

**Verification (`probe-cloud-volumetric-parity.mjs`, PNGs READ):** WebGPU filled-px **7746 → 1947 vs WebGL 1797 (4.3× → 1.08×)**, area ratio **2.41× → 0.99×**; the WebGL and WebGPU clouds are now visually near-identical (same ~63 px grainy core, same deterministic specks). Didn't-break: probe-cloud-property-edit PASS; probe-collections-regression cloud gate re-baselined 100→50 (the 3 small clouds now correctly render ~85 green px at the corrected half-size, the anticipated re-baseline), PASS.

**Lessons:** (1) a "more-correct" sub-fix (B365 worley) un-masked a separate residual that a wronger one had been hiding — and the residual turned out to be a *different* one-liner. (2) The backlog-triage workflow pinned this exact `*0.5` from a read-only pass in minutes, where B365's inline investigation had only narrowed it to "non-shader." Parallel read-only triage is the right tool for *finding* the lever; serial build/probe/READ is the right tool for *landing* it. **Completes the cloud trilogy:** B363 shape + B365 grain + B366 size.

**Files:** `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts` + the collections-regression cloud-gate re-baseline.

## Batch 365 — WebGPU CloudCollection baked worley-texture port for grain parity (NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-WORLEY-TEXTURE-PARITY) (2026-06-23)

**Item:** NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-WORLEY-TEXTURE-PARITY (B363 residual). B363's volumetric cloud used an inline procedural worley FBM for the W/W2/W3 erosion — coarser + smoother than WebGL's baked 3D worley texture, so the cloud was "denser/less grainy."

**Fix:** ported WebGL's baked-texture path faithfully. `createNoiseTexture` (in `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts`) now CPU-generates a 3-channel worley-FBM atlas (port of `CloudNoiseFS.glsl` worley + `CloudCollection.js`'s 3D→2D packing) and the cloud FS samples it via a WGSL `voxelToUV` + manual trilinear `csm_cloudSampleNoise` (1:1 port of `CloudCollectionFS.glsl`) at `NOISE_DETAIL * cloudPoint`, exactly like WebGL.

**Key sizing trick:** SLICE=64 / DETAIL=8 (vs WebGL's 128 / 16) makes the W value at ANY cloudPoint **identical** to WebGL — both reduce to `worleyFBM(cloudPoint mod 8)` (same wrapRange=8 integer cell points from `random3`, same tile period in cloudPoint space) — at 1/8 the generation cost. The worley cell points only depend on cells wrapped to `[0, 8)³` = 512 values → precomputed once so the per-voxel hot loop has NO trig (gen <1 frame even at 1024×256). Sampler switched to NEAREST (the FS does its own trilinear over the packed atlas; hardware filtering would bleed across slice seams).

**Verification (`probe-cloud-volumetric-parity.mjs`, PNGs READ):** the WebGPU cloud is now finely speckled, matching WebGL's worley grain (vs B363's smooth blob). Didn't-break: probe-cloud-property-edit PASS, probe-collections-regression PASS (cloud green 316 > 100 gate), 0 errors.

**Lesson + exposed residual:** the now-faithful W erodes LESS than B363's coarse inline worley, which had been OVER-eroding and *coincidentally masking* a pre-existing size gap. With the worley correct, the cloud is now ~1.9x linear vs WebGL (was ~1.6x). Since the raymarch + Gardner + TR + color WGSL are line-by-line ALGORITHMICALLY IDENTICAL to `CloudCollectionFS.glsl` (re-verified) and W now matches exactly, the residual size/density is a NON-shader cause — tracked as **NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-SIZE-PARITY** (candidates: clip-space-vs-eye-space quad-offset projection, maxSize delivery, a WebGL quad-projection quirk). A "more correct" sub-fix can EXPOSE a larger residual that a wronger one was hiding — measure against the reference, not against the prior WebGPU build.

**Files:** `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts` only. **Probes:** `probe-cloud-volumetric-parity.mjs`, `probe-cloud-property-edit.mjs` + `probe-collections-regression.mjs` (didn't-break).

## Batch 364 — WebGPU HDR night sky crushed black by always-on auto-exposure (NEW-WEBGPU-SKYBOX-HDR-FAINT-STAR-PARITY) (2026-06-23)

**Item:** NEW-WEBGPU-SKYBOX-HDR-FAINT-STAR-PARITY (QUEUE Tier-3). Under `scene.highDynamicRange = true`, the WebGPU night sky rendered dramatically under-bright vs WebGL — bright catalog stars + their bloom halos vanished. Prior re-investigation correctly localized it to the "shared HDR post-process path" but left 3 unpinned suspects (tonemap / auto-exposure / bloom) and scoped it as needing broad HDR regression.

**Root cause (pinned):** auto-exposure. WebGL only runs the auto-exposure luminance reduction when the user opts in (`PostProcessStageCollection._autoExposureEnabled`, default `false`). WebGPU calls `addAutoExposure` UNCONDITIONALLY (`WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts`, AUDIT B.14 "always-on"), `WebGPUAutoExposure.enabled` defaults `true`, and `configureWebGPUPostProcessPipeline` never synced the flag — so WebGPU auto-exposed EVERY frame. On a near-black HDR starfield the adaptive exposure collapsed the entire frame to pure black.

**Decisive diagnostic (no rebuild — runtime toggle of `scene._alternateSceneRenderer._postProcess.autoExposureEnabled`):** `diag-stars-hdr-autoexposure.mjs` — AE-on → bright(>120)=0 / maxLum=**0** (black); AE-off → bright=235 / maxLum=761 / **5 saturated** bloom-feeding star points. That single toggle flips the whole bug.

**Fix:** `configureWebGPUPostProcessPipeline` now sets `pipeline.autoExposureEnabled = collection._autoExposureEnabled === true` — the SAME opt-in flag WebGL honors, so both backends expose identically by default. The always-on B.14 behavior is itself a WebGL divergence (WebGL never auto-exposes by default) and is dropped for parity; `autoExposure = true` still gets the adaptive path on both backends.

**Verification:** `probe-stars-hdr-autoexposure-parity.mjs` (NEW) — WebGPU HDR sky bright=231 / maxLum=756 / 4-saturated vs WebGL 282 / 717 / 0 (was 0/0/0), PNGs READ (no longer black; near-parity). **Didn't-break (shared HDR infra):** `probe-disc-size-orbit` identical to baseline (atmosphere disc 1.01%/0.01%); `probe-bloom-parity` PASS with WebGPU globe pixel `rgb(31,38,51)` == WebGL byte-for-byte + bloom ratio 1.01x; SDR night-sky control unchanged (READ — AE is a no-op in SDR). **Residual:** WebGL catalog sprites still marginally brighter (~82% bright-px) → separate `NEW-WEBGPU-STARFIELD-TUNE`.

**Lesson:** when a "shared HDR" symptom has 3 suspects, a runtime toggle of each suspect (here `autoExposureEnabled`) pins the lever in one probe run with zero rebuilds — far cheaper than reading the tonemap/exposure/bloom math three times.

**Files:** `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts` only. **Probes:** `diag-stars-hdr-autoexposure.mjs` (NEW, root-cause toggle), `probe-stars-hdr-autoexposure-parity.mjs` (NEW, regression gate), `probe-disc-size-orbit.mjs` + `probe-bloom-parity.mjs` (didn't-break).

## Batch 363 — WebGPU CloudCollection volumetric raymarch port (NEW-CLOUD-IMPOSTOR-FS-PARITY) (2026-06-23)

**Item:** NEW-CLOUD-IMPOSTOR-FS-PARITY (QUEUE Tier-3). The active WebGPU cloud shader (`CLOUD_WGSL`, inlined in `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts` — NOT the unused `Shaders/WebGPU/Collections/CloudCollection.wgsl`) was a flat 2D-noise impostor: a radial smoothstep × 2D noise sample filling most of the billboard quad. WebGL's `CloudCollectionFS.glsl` raymarches a per-cloud ellipsoid volume. At 2000x1300 m / 15 km nadir the WebGPU cloud was a 282x184 px smooth blob vs WebGL's 63x53 px lumpy raymarched core (~4-5x linear / ~15x area), with `maximumSize`/`slice` ignored.

**Root cause:** two halves. (1) The FS never did the volumetric raymarch — it just faded the quad radially, so the bright footprint ≈ the whole quad (sized by `scale`) instead of the inner ellipsoid (`0.82 * maximumSize`). (2) The instance buffer never carried `maximumSize` (vec3) at all — only `scale.xy` + `slice` — so even a correct FS had no ellipsoid extent to march. The renderer also defaulted `scale` to 50/30 and `slice` to 0.0, both wrong vs `CumulusCloud` (20/12, -1.0).

**Fix:** ported the full volumetric FS into `CLOUD_WGSL` — ray-vs-ellipsoid intersection (unit-sphere transform, optional `slice` plane), Gardner (1985) analytic texture `T()`, `I()` diffuse/specular/texture shading, and 3-channel worley-FBM erosion (`TR = ndDot^3 - W`, eroded by W2/W3). The worley is an inline port of `CloudNoiseFS.glsl`'s `worleyNoise`/`worleyFBMNoise` (cells from `random3`, internal `p*freq`), normalized by cloud radius (~4 cells across) — substituting WebGL's baked 3D-packed-2D noise texture (bindings 1/2 retained for the BGL + a future exact-texture pass). Wired `maximumSize` through: instance stride 56→68 (+`@location(5)` float32x3 at offset 56), velocity instance + prev strides and all `*56`/`56-byte` sentinels bumped to 68, `buildInstanceBuffer` writes `maximumSize` (default `(sx, sy, min(sx,sy)/1.5)`) and uses correct scale/slice defaults.

**Verification (probe-cloud-volumetric-parity.mjs, NEW — renders the same single cloud on BOTH backends, measures bright-pixel bbox):** baseline reproduced the bug exactly (WebGL 63x53, WebGPU 282x184, area 15.5x — matching the DEFERRED_WORK measurement). After: WebGPU 103x78, **area 2.41x**. Both PNGs READ — smooth ellipse blob → lumpy worley-eroded cumulus puff. Tuning note: np frequency ×10 measured WORSE (2.94x — high-freq specks balloon the bbox); ×4 kept. **Didn't-break:** probe-cloud-property-edit PASS (68-byte stride rebuild + dirty-gate intact), probe-collections-regression PASS (cloud 131 px > 100 gate, no re-baseline needed), 0 console errors throughout.

**Residual (tracked):** NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-WORLEY-TEXTURE-PARITY — the inline worley leaves the cloud ~1.6x linear larger + denser/less grainy than WebGL's baked-texture worley; porting the exact `CloudNoiseFS` texture is a ~1-session follow-up.

**Files:** `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts` only. **Probes:** `probe-cloud-volumetric-parity.mjs` (NEW), `probe-cloud-property-edit.mjs` + `probe-collections-regression.mjs` (didn't-break).

## Batch 362 — WebGPU CV/morph vertical exaggeration + the skirt-wall fix (MORPH-EXAG-SKIRTS) (2026-06-23)

**Item:** MORPH-EXAG-SKIRTS (QUEUE Tier-3). Vertical exaggeration was dropped in COLUMBUS_VIEW + MORPHING on WebGPU (`GlobeTerrain.wgsl` gated the exaggeration to `sceneMode > 2.5` and fed the planar legs raw height) → CV terrain rendered FLAT. A naive ungate (Batch 216, reverted) shattered skirts into vertical walls.

**Root cause of the skirt walls (now understood):** skirt vertices (tile-edge geometry extruded down to hide LOD cracks) carry a REDUCED height ATTRIBUTE (`heightSample -= skirtHeight`, `HeightmapTessellator.js:399`) AND an extruded-down geometric position. The Batch-216 attempt exaggerated `length(position3D) - radius` (the GEOMETRIC height), which pushed the already-low skirts much further down as visible walls. WebGL (`GlobeVS.glsl:245-258`) instead exaggerates the height ATTRIBUTE (`newHeight = (height - rel)*exag + rel`) and feeds `newHeight` to the planar `getPositionPlanarEarth` — so the skirt's planar X stays consistent with its edge and the taller skirt remains occluded behind the adjacent tile.

**Fix:** mirror WebGL exactly. Compute `resolvedHeight` from the RAW (un-exaggerated) position; `exaggeratedHeight = (resolvedHeight - rel)*exag + rel` (clamped to `-radius`); feed it to `computePlanarPosition` for CV + the morph planar leg; offset the 3D position along the geodetic ellipsoid normal by `(exaggeratedHeight - resolvedHeight)` for SCENE3D + the morph 3D leg — UN-gated from `sceneMode > 2.5` so all modes exaggerate consistently (no morph pop). `verticalExaggeration == 1.0` → byte-identical to the pre-fix path.

**Two verification lessons:**
1. **The "blue water streaks" were a red herring — baseline-isolate before blaming your change.** After the fix, WebGPU CV (and 3D) showed thin bright-blue streaks WebGL lacked. They LOOKED like a skirt/exaggeration artifact. Stashing the one-file `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` change + rebuilding + re-probing 3D exaggeration showed the streaks were ALREADY there pre-fix → a PRE-EXISTING water/lake-color parity gap (NEW-WEBGPU-EXAG-WATER-STREAKS) that exaggeration merely amplifies by deepening valleys. The fix is clean; the streaks are a separate item.
2. **Changing a working path (the SCENE3D offset, length-based → attribute-based) needs its own didn't-break probe** (`probe-exaggeration-3d.mjs`, NEW) PLUS the exag==1.0 byte-identity check (camera-track meanDiff 1.557% == baseline).

**Files:** `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` only. **Probes:** `probe-exaggeration-cv.mjs` (CV flat → matching WebGL relief), `probe-exaggeration-3d.mjs` (NEW, 3D didn't-break), `probe-camera-track.mjs` (exag==1.0 byte-identity).

## Batch 360 — WebGPU globe terrain picking, opt-in (DP-H44) (2026-06-23)

**Item:** DP-H44 (QUEUE Tier-1 #6). Globe surface emitted no pick-ID on WebGPU → terrain invisible to `scene.pick`.

**Investigation correction (critical):** the WebGL globe `DrawCommand` ALSO carries no `pickId` (`GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1771-1782`); `GlobeSurfaceTileProvider.updateForPick` only re-pushes the *color* commands, so WebGL `scene.pick` ALSO returns `undefined` over the globe — the re-push exists purely to populate pick-FBO DEPTH for `scene.pickPosition`. So "return the globe from `scene.pick`" is a deliberate DIVERGENCE from WebGL parity. Surfaced this to the user, who chose to gate it behind a default-`false` `Globe.pickable` flag.

**Three non-obvious failure modes hit during bring-up (each cost a debug cycle — documented so the next session skips them):**

1. **Central pipeline cache silently never resolves single-target / `multisample:undefined` descriptors.** `selectPickPipeline` routed the pick descriptor through `resolveGlobePipelineEntry` → `WebGPURenderPipelineCache.getPipeline` (async). It returned `null` FOREVER with NO console error and NO validation error. Direct sync `device.createRenderPipeline(descriptorToGPU(pickDescriptor))` succeeded immediately with zero validation errors — proving the descriptor is valid and the async cache path is the culprit (the ellipsoid pick uses the same helper but a different target shape). **Fix:** create the globe pick pipeline synchronously (the documented cache-less fallback; the WGSL module is already compiled for the color pipeline, so it only assembles the pipeline object, once per variant).

2. **`updateForPick` re-pushes the empty WebGPU `_drawCommands`.** `QuadtreePrimitive.render` only builds globe commands under `passes.render`; during pick it calls `tileProvider.updateForPick`, which re-pushes the WebGL `_drawCommands` array — empty on WebGPU (the WebGPU globe pushes inline command objects straight to `frameState.commandList`). So the WebGPU globe was ENTIRELY ABSENT from the pick pass — the pick command's `execute` never ran. **Fix:** `updateWebGPUForPick` REBUILDS fresh commands (with the pick command attached) for the selected tiles in the pick frame's ring page; re-pushing render-frame commands is unsafe because the camera UB is ring-allocated (slice recycled by pick time).

3. **"depth always" was unnecessary AND caused a foreground-occlusion regression.** Initial design always-attached the globe pick command (write depth even when `!pickable`) on the theory that `pickPosition` needs pick-FBO globe depth. But `pickPosition` worked on WebGPU BEFORE this change (it reads the MAIN-pass globe-depth texture, not the pick FBO). Always-writing globe depth made the globe occlude a foreground Point in the pick pass (multi-frustum depth) → the point became unpickable. **Fix:** gate the globe out of the pick pass entirely when `!pickable` — default behavior identical to pre-change (foreground picking intact, `scene.pick` undefined over globe, `pickPosition` unaffected).

**Implementation:** `pickColor: vec4` at the camera-UB TAIL (`GlobeTerrain.wgsl` after `logDepth`, `CAMERA_UNIFORM_FLOATS` 144→148, packed in `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts`); `@fragment fn fragmentPickMain → camera.pickColor`; `selectPickPipeline` (sync); `Globe.pickable` + `createPickId` in `Globe.beginFrame`; `updateWebGPUForPick` pick-frame rebuild.

**Files:** `GlobeTerrain.wgsl`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTypes.ts`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts`, `Scene/Globe.js`, `Scene/GlobeSurfaceTileProvider.js`, `Scene/GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js`. **Probe:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-globe-pick-h44.mjs`. Render regression `probe-camera-track.mjs` meanDiff 1.55% (== baseline).
