## Batch 261 — Phase 3 Slice 1: per-frustum camera-UB resolver for collections (NEW-COLLECTIONS-PER-FRUSTUM-CAMERA-UB) (2026-06-13)

**Context (Phase 3 — 2D/CV/morph for collections).** Collections render in 3D but vanish/misplace in SCENE2D + COLUMBUS_VIEW. Baseline `probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs` (recorded this batch): **3D** bb=56 pt=267 pl=259 lbl=125 (renders); **2D** bb=0 pt=0 pl=6 lbl=0 (broken); **CV** bb=0 pt=0 pl=0 lbl=128 (broken). Slice 1's mandate is the FOUNDATION — a per-frustum camera-UB resolver — not the 2D/CV fix itself (that is Slices 2-3). It MUST NOT regress 3D.

**Root cause of the 2D/CV hole (diagnosis).** Each collection FR packs its camera UB ONCE per frame at `update()` from `uniformState.projection`/`.view` and builds ONE `WebGPUDrawCommand` whose `mvpRelativeToEye` is baked from that single projection. The WebGPU multi-frustum loop (`WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop`) re-executes that same command once per depth slice its bounding volume overlaps; between slices it calls `_updateFrustumUniforms` → `uniformState.updateFrustum(...)`, recomputing `uniformState.projection` for that slice. The collection command carries only the single baked MVP, so it cannot pick up a slice's projection. In 2D/CV (orthographic/planar, per-band C-R8-SCENE2D-JITTER camera-Z shift, clip-z must land in WebGPU [0,1]) the single bake is wrong for most slices and the geometry clips out.

**Slice-1 deliverable.** New shared helper `WebGPUCollectionCameraUB.js` (+ co-located `.d.ts` for the `.ts` cloud FR) owns a per-collection pool of DISTINCT per-slice GPU camera buffers + bind groups, keyed by `uniformState._currentSliceIndex` (published by the frustum loop, Batch 173 plumbing). `makeResolver({bufferSize, bindGroupLayout, pack, extraEntries})` returns a `bindGroupResolvers[i]` closure that, at draw time, selects/uploads the current slice's buffer and returns its bind group. Wired into all five collection FRs at the camera group: Point + Polyline (dedicated camera group 0), Cloud (group 0 = UB + stable noise tex/sampler), Billboard + Label (group 0 = UB + per-frame-rotating atlas + globe-depth views — passed as `extraEntries`, with a generation token that rebuilds per-slice bind groups when those views rotate).

**The 3D-regression lesson (critical — caught probe-first, NOT shipped).** The first implementation had the resolver RE-PACK from live `uniformState.projection` at draw time. `probe-collections-far-camera.mjs` (mandatory gate, multi-frustum @220km log-depth) immediately regressed bb=7129→0 / pt=5286→0. Isolation probe confirmed: forcing the resolver to the static fallback restored 56/339; the active draw-time-repack path gave 0/0. Root cause: collections — like the globe (see `WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop` L162-171: globe packs against `scene.camera.frustum` at scene-update and REPLAYS UNCHANGED across slices) — must bake against the FULL camera frustum and replay; log-depth's `csm_updatePositionDepth` clip-z clamp makes that single bake correct in every slice. The multi-frustum loop slices `uniformState.projection` to a narrow per-band near/far (~5e5), so re-reading it at draw time packed each slice with the wrong narrow projection and clipped far geometry out of the near slices. **Fix:** the resolver captures the frame's reference snapshot ONCE at update time (== the static full-frustum bake) and merely COPIES it into each slice's own buffer. Result: 3D is byte-identical to the pre-resolver path; the distinct per-slice buffers/bind groups exist as the foundation Slices 2-3 build on (those introduce mode-gated per-slice DIVERGENCE for the 2D/CV band shift).

**Verification (probe-first per Principle 8).** `probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs` post-change: **3D byte-identical** to baseline (bb=56 pt=267 pl=259 lbl=125); **2D/CV unchanged** (still all-zero — Slices 2-3 fix those, as designed). Isolation: resolver-active == static-fallback (56/339) at the far camera, proving the snapshot-copy is a no-op in 3D. Internal verification probe confirmed the resolver reads a live non-zero `_currentSliceIndex` (=1, not the undefined→0 default) and allocates/binds the slice-keyed buffer. Standing gates ALL green: probe-collections-regression · probe-collections-far-camera (bb 7129 / pt 5286, == baseline) · probe-billboard-partial-write · probe-point-label-partial-write · probe-polyline-cloud-consume · probe-cloud-property-edit · probe-orbital-catalog · probe-compute-instance-generic · probe-globe-bindgroup-cache · probe-bloom-parity · probe-pickposition-webgpu (dH=4.1 m) · probe-taa-resolve · probe-pickmodel-instanced · probe-globe-default-limits · sandcastle-smoke (3/3) · upstream-regression-check 21/21 · `tsc --noEmit` clean · `gulp build` clean.

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCollectionCameraUB.js` (new shared helper), `WebGPUCollectionCameraUB.d.ts` (new co-located types), `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js`, `WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js`, `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js`, `WebGPULabelRenderer.js` (resolver wiring).

## Batch 264 — log-depth for the Mat/PBR/Basic geometry primitives (the bulk ~42 Primitive WGSL) (NEW-PRIMITIVE-MAT-LOG-DEPTH) (2026-06-13)

**Context.** Renderer-wide log depth has been LIVE since Batch 251 (master switch `_logDepthWriteEnabled` defaults TRUE — globe + depth plane + all five collections + ComputeInstance + Model PBR write log `@builtin(frag_depth)`), but among the geometry-Primitive pipelines ONLY the two lit Phong producers (`PrimitivePhongColor`/`PrimitivePhongTexturedColor`, Batch 188) wrote log depth. Every geometry primitive routed through a `Mat*`/`PBR*`/`Basic*` pipeline still wrote HYPERBOLIC NDC z into the SAME scene depth buffer the globe writes LOG depth into → a range-dependent z-fight. The log-depth re-audit measured a low slab ~2 km above terrain at a 220 km camera losing ~28% of its pixels (2913 of 4067) to terrain bleed-through purely from the mixed depth space.

**Fix — the established LOG-DEPTH RECIPE applied across 42 shaders.** Three structural families, each handled by a one-shot codegen pass (`Tools/apply-logdepth-{matlit,flatbasic,pbr}.mjs`):

- **Mat*Lit (19)** — `clipPosition` builtin + `FragOutput` struct return. Byte-identical to the PrimitivePhongColor template: `v_logDepth` varying (@location 7), `logDepth: vec4` on the LIT CameraUniforms tail, inline `csm_vertexLogDepth`/`csm_updatePositionDepth`/`csm_writeLogDepth` + `g_fragLogDepth` private, VS computes the varying + clamps clip-z, `@builtin(frag_depth)` added to `FragOutput`, FS writes it at the lone `return mrtOut;`.
- **PBR (2)** — `clipPosition` builtin but a bare `@location(0) vec4` return with many helper-fn returns ABOVE fragmentMain. Same VS treatment; the FS swaps to a `FragOut` struct (color + frag_depth) under `//>>ifdef LOG_DEPTH` and wraps the single fragmentMain `return finalColor;`.
- **Mat*Flat (19) + Basic (2)** — `position` builtin + bare-vec4 return. Same `FragOut`-swap return treatment (Basic has 2 fragmentMain return sites — the clipping-edge early-out + the final — both wrapped); v_logDepth sourced from `output.position`.

**Renderer plumbing (`WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js`).** (1) The FLAT camera UB gained the same 16-byte `logDepth` tail the LIT UB got in Batch 188: `FLAT_CAMERA_BYTES` 160→176, packed unconditionally by `writeRTEUniformsFlat`→`writeLogDepthTail` at floats 40-43 (inert until a shader reads it + the define is set). (2) `LOG_DEPTH` now ORs into BOTH command paths: the Phong/Basic path dropped the `isLit &&` restriction (`logDepthActive = isWebGPULogDepthActive(...)` — Basic uses the now-tailed FLAT UB); the material path threads a new `logDepthActive` arg into `createMaterialPipelineAndCache`, ORs it into `preprocessShaderSource`, and tracks `cache.logDepthEnabled` in the rebuild-invalidation comparison so the master-switch flip rebuilds the Mat pipeline (mirrors the Phong path's `logDepthChanged` guard). The `//>>else` branch keeps the historical hyperbolic path so LOG_DEPTH-off is byte-identical. Pick variants stay hyperbolic (pick FBO is self-consistent; never given the define).

**Drive-by bug fix (Batch-97 latent).** 18 of the 19 `Mat*Flat` shaders WRITE `output.eyePosition` in vertexMain and READ `input.eyePosition` in the FEAT-GAP-09 aerial-LUT fog block, but never DECLARE the varying in `VertexOutput` — they would fail `createShaderModule` the moment a `flat:true` material primitive rendered (only `PrimitiveMatColorFlat` got the declaration in Batch 97). Since the codegen pass already edits each `VertexOutput`, it restored the missing `eyePosition` declaration so the Flat path actually compiles and the log-depth `//>>else` branch is genuinely byte-identical-WORKING, not byte-identical-broken.

**Verification (probe-first per Principle 8).** New `Tools/visual-regression/probe-logdepth-zfight.mjs`: a green slab grid via `MaterialAppearance` (ColorMaterial → the Mat pipeline) near-coplanar with a solid globe at a 220 km nadir camera, + a magenta billboard reference grid (already log-depth). Results: Mat slab renders @220 km with log depth ON (39540 px), ON/OFF green ratio 0.988 (≥ 0.9 — the pre-fix mixed-depth bug was ~0.72), below-ground negative control stays occluded (0 px), flip-back-ON re-verifies, 0 console errors. The visual tell: the magenta markers render ONLY in the log-depth-ON leg (the all-hyperbolic OFF leg vanishes them at 220 km — the Batch-229 bug-2 signature) — confirming the Mat slab now composes in the same depth space as the globe + collections. Read both output PNGs: clean green slab rows, no z-fight speckle, markers present in ON / absent in OFF. Additional ad-hoc check: a material Polygon (PolygonGeometry + MaterialAppearance) renders 56073 px through the Mat pipeline with 0 errors. ALL standing gates green: probe-collections-regression · probe-collections-far-camera (bb 7129 / pt 5286) · probe-billboard-partial-write · probe-point-label-partial-write · probe-polyline-cloud-consume · probe-bloom-parity · probe-globe-bindgroup-cache · probe-pickposition-webgpu (dH 4.1 m — pick stays hyperbolic, unaffected) · sandcastle-smoke (3/3). Preprocessor cross-check: all 42 shaders preprocess balanced with LOG_DEPTH ON (frag_depth present) AND OFF (zero log-depth tokens — byte-identical). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx gulp build` clean (49 s).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` (FLAT UB logDepth tail + dual-path LOG_DEPTH gating); 19 `PrimitiveMat*Lit.wgsl` + 19 `PrimitiveMat*Flat.wgsl` + `PrimitiveBasicColor.wgsl` + `PrimitiveBasicTexturedColor.wgsl` + `PrimitivePBRSimple.wgsl` + `PrimitivePBRTextured.wgsl` (log-depth blocks; the Flat shaders also restore the `eyePosition` VertexOutput declaration); `Tools/apply-logdepth-{matlit,flatbasic,pbr}.mjs` (codegen passes); `Tools/visual-regression/probe-logdepth-zfight.mjs` (new gate). ## Batch 265 — log-depth for the experimental Buffer* collection family (BufferPoint/BufferPolyline/BufferPolygon) (NEW-BUFFER-LOG-DEPTH) (2026-06-13)

**Context.** Renderer-wide log depth has been LIVE since Batch 251 and Batch 264 closed the bulk Mat/PBR/Basic geometry-primitive producers, but the experimental Buffer* collections still wrote HYPERBOLIC NDC z. Their three WGSL shaders call `csm_vertexLogDepth` + `csm_writeLogDepth` via bare `#import` names, but `WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts` resolved those names from a hand-written `BUFFER_WGSL_CHUNKS` map to a 1-arg `csm_vertexLogDepth` STUB + an EMPTY `csm_writeLogDepth` no-op (lines 74-90) — so the family had no `@builtin(frag_depth)` output, never consulted `isWebGPULogDepthActive`, and was ALWAYS hyperbolic. The stub's own comment was actively wrong after Batch 251: it claimed "the WebGPU globe writes hyperbolic NDC depth" to justify the no-op — false since the globe writes LOG. Result: at a far nadir camera the Buffer fill sat in a different depth space than the log-depth globe and sank entirely behind terrain (verified below: the pre-fix build shows ZERO Buffer fill pixels while a co-located billboard reference renders fine).

**Fix — the established LOG-DEPTH RECIPE, reusing the canonical chunks (no bespoke math).** (1) `BUFFER_WGSL_CHUNKS` now maps `csm_vertexLogDepth`/`csm_writeLogDepth` to the SAME canonical 2-arg chunk `.js` modules the five collections + Model PBR use (`csm_vertexLogDepth.js` carries `csm_updatePositionDepth`; both chunks are leaf — no nested `#import` — so single-pass inlining is safe). The two old inline stub strings are deleted. (2) The three shaders gained `//>>ifdef LOG_DEPTH` blocks: a `v_logDepth` varying (reusing each `VertexOutput`'s existing free location), VS computes `v_logDepth = csm_vertexLogDepth(out.position, near)` + `out.position = csm_updatePositionDepth(out.position)` AFTER the quad-expand / extrusion / hide branch, and the FS swaps `fragmentMain` to a `FragOutput` struct (color + `@builtin(frag_depth)`) writing `csm_writeLogDepth(v_logDepth, factor)`. The `//>>else` keeps the historical bare-`@location(0) vec4` hyperbolic FS byte-identical. (3) The (near, far, factor) scalars ride in the reserved `.w` pad lanes of the SHARED 368-byte `CameraUniforms` struct that the Buffer family already binds — `encodedCameraPositionMCHigh.w` = frustum near, `cameraPosition.w` = `oneOverLog2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne` — packed unconditionally by `packCameraLogDepthLanes(out, 0, uniformState)` appended to `packCameraUniforms` (inert until a shader reads them; only fills previously-zero pads). (4) Each per-collection renderer (`WebGPUBufferPoint/Polyline/PolygonRenderer.ts`) computes `logDepthActive = isWebGPULogDepthActive(context, frameState)`, derives `defines = logDepthActive ? ShaderDefine.LOG_DEPTH : 0`, threads `defines` into `preprocessShader` + the module-cache `getOrCreate` key, and invalidates its `_webgpuCache` on a `_logDepthEnabled` flip (mirroring the existing `_pipelineFormatGeneration` HDR-toggle guard) so the module + pipelines rebuild when the master switch flips.

**Preprocessor wiring (`WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.preprocessShader`).** The function now takes a `defines` arg, runs the `//>>ifdef` preprocessor (`preprocess(source, defines)` from `WebGPUShaderPreprocessor`) AFTER `#import` inlining, and keys its `_processedShaderCache` by `(name, defines)` so LOG_DEPTH-on and -off cache distinct processed sources. Critically, `preprocess()` runs BEFORE the `PICK_FRAGMENT_SUFFIX` is appended — so the pick FS (`fragmentPickMain`) never sees the `FragOutput`/frag_depth swap and stays hyperbolic (the pick FBO is self-consistent; matches the recipe's "pick stays hyperbolic" rule).

**Verification (probe-first per Principle 8).** New `Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffer-logdepth-zfight.mjs`: a 6×6 cyan BufferPoint grid + a yellow BufferPolygon slab + a red BufferPolyline a few hundred meters above a solid globe at a 220 km nadir camera, with a magenta BillboardCollection grid co-located at the same 36 positions as a KNOWN-GOOD log-depth reference (billboards write log since Batch 250). The probe asserts (a) all three Buffer families render with floor pixels AND the billboard ref renders, (b) the cyan Buffer coverage is ≥ 40% of the magenta reference coverage (post-fix ratio ≈ 0.49-0.51 — both compose on the log globe), (c) an off→on master-switch flip rebuilds with NO validation error, (d) 0 console errors. **Against the pre-fix build the probe FAILS hard** (proving it catches the bug): cyan/yellow/red = 0/0/0 — every Buffer fill pixel eaten by the log-depth globe — while the magenta reference stays at ~6181. POST-fix: cyan=3009 yellow=9734 red=3221 magenta=6171, 0 errors. Read both output PNGs (pre-fix and post-fix): post-fix shows the yellow slab + red line + the overlapping cyan-circle/magenta-square grid sitting cleanly on the visible globe with no terrain bleed-through. **Note on the kill-switch OFF leg:** toggling `_logDepthWriteEnabled` mid-session (or building hyperbolic from frame 0) leaves the GLOBE pipelines half-rebuilt and blacks the globe — a PRE-EXISTING kill-switch limitation that affects the reference Mat/far-camera probes' OFF-dependent checks identically (confirmed by stashing this change and re-running: `probe-collections-far-camera` check 2 fails red=1455 at the pre-change baseline too). The Buffer slice does not regress it. **All standing gates green:** probe-collections-regression · probe-billboard-partial-write · probe-point-label-partial-write · probe-polyline-cloud-consume · probe-orbital-catalog · probe-compute-instance-generic · probe-globe-bindgroup-cache · probe-bloom-parity · probe-pickposition-webgpu (dH 4.1 m — pick unaffected) · sandcastle-smoke (3/3). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx gulp build` clean (49 s).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts` (canonical chunk map swap; `packCameraLogDepthLanes` in `packCameraUniforms`; `preprocessShader` `defines` arg + `//>>ifdef` resolution + `(name,defines)` cache key); `WebGPUBufferPoint/Polyline/PolygonRenderer.ts` (LOG_DEPTH gate + define threading + `_logDepthEnabled` flip-rebuild guard); `BufferPoint/Polyline/PolygonMaterial.wgsl` (gated log-depth blocks + `FragOutput` FS swap); `Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffer-logdepth-zfight.mjs` (new gate). Docs: DEFERRED_WORK NEW-LOG-DEPTH-REMAINING-PRODUCERS (Buffer* struck SHIPPED), FEATURE_INVENTORY log-depth producer list, DEBUGGING_GUIDE probe table.

## Batch 266 — log-depth for EllipsoidPrimitive + the Vector3DTile classifier family (NEW-ELLIPSOIDPRIM-LOG-DEPTH + NEW-CLASSIFIER-LOG-DEPTH) (2026-06-13)

**Context.** Renderer-wide log depth has been LIVE since Batch 251; Batches 264/265 closed the Mat/PBR/Basic and Buffer* producers. The remaining hyperbolic writers per NEW-LOG-DEPTH-REMAINING-PRODUCERS were EllipsoidPrimitive and the Vector3DTile classifier family. All four write into (or depth-TEST against) the shared scene depth, which the globe now LOG-encodes, so each was in the wrong depth space.

**The four cases (each a different depth-interaction shape — this was the analysis crux):**

1. **`WebGPUEllipsoidPrimitiveRenderer.ts` — ray-cast, `depthCompare: less-equal`, `depthWriteEnabled: true`.** Pre-fix the full-screen quad rasterized at the near plane (`output.position = vec4(input.position, 0, 1)` → clip z=0) and the FS wrote NO `frag_depth`, so the shell tested as on-top of everything (it ignored the globe). Fix: the camera UB grew `projection: mat4x4` + `logDepth: vec4` (240→320 B, 60→80 floats); the color FS recovers the eye-space hit's clip-space w via `positionCC = camera.projection * vec4(hit, 1)` and writes `csm_writeLogDepth(csm_vertexLogDepth(positionCC, near), factor)`. CONVENTION NOTE: WebGL's `EllipsoidFS.glsl` WRITE_DEPTH/LOG_DEPTH block uses `czm_writeLogDepth(1.0 + positionCC.w)` (no near subtraction — an idiosyncratic ray-cast form), but the WebGPU port deliberately uses the renderer-wide `csm_vertexLogDepth` = `(w - near) + 1` convention so the shell composes with the globe + collections, NOT with WebGL's variant. The `//>>else` (no frag_depth → historical near-plane z) keeps log-OFF byte-identical. Pick stays hyperbolic (`fragmentPickMain` emits a bare `@location(0)` — unaffected by the `FragOutput`-struct `//>>ifdef`).

2. **`WebGPUVector3DTilePrimitiveRenderer.js` — polygon classifier, `depthCompare: less-equal` vs shared scene depth.** Pre-fix the volume's hyperbolic z FAILED the `less-equal` test against the log globe → the entire volume was culled (the exact GroundPrimitive failure mode). Fix: the VS writes per-vertex log z (`o.pos.z = clamp(csm_writeLogDepth(csm_vertexLogDepth(o.pos, encNear), factor), 0, 1) * o.pos.w`) after `csm_depthClamp`, derived from the `logDepth` lane (floats 52-55). Shared by color/pick/stencil/velocity — pick is log-CONSISTENT on WebGPU because the globe writes log into the pick FBO too (GroundPrimitive's pick pipeline shares `colorVS` the same way; confirmed). No FS reverse needed: the FS only does `surfaceDepth == 0` sky-discard, it does NOT reconstruct eye-space.

3. **`WebGPUVector3DTilePolylinesRenderer.js` — non-clamped, `depthWriteEnabled: false`, `depthCompare: less-equal`, Pass.TRANSLUCENT.** Same root as #2 (tests `less-equal` even though it doesn't write depth). Fix: VS log-z write (color + velocity), `logDepth` lane at floats 60-63.

4. **`WebGPUVector3DTileClampedPolylinesRenderer.js` — terrain-clamped, `depthCompare: always`.** The hardware depth test is BYPASSED (all four pipelines use `always`), so NO VS log-z write is needed. But the FS reconstructs the eye-space surface point via `windowToEyeCoordinates(in.pos.xy, surfaceDepth)` where `surfaceDepth` is the sampled (now log-encoded) globe depth. Reconstructing with a plain inverse-projection gives a wildly-wrong eye point → the 5-plane swept-volume test discards every fragment. Fix: the FS gains a log branch (gated `logDepthActive ? … : ""`) mirroring GroundPrimitive's `windowToEye`: `depthFromCamera = csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance(depth, encNear, encFar)` (decode eye distance with the globe's ENCODE frustum) → re-encode to per-slice window z (`windowZ = sFar*(1 - sNear/depthFromCamera)/(sFar - sNear)`) → `invProj * vec4(ndc, windowZ, 1)` with the `q.w = 1/depthFromCamera` precision override. `logDepth` lane = (encNear, encFar, sliceNear, sliceFar) at floats 88-91. Single-frustum correct; per-slice multi-frustum refinement (a resolver like GroundPrimitive's FrustumState group) is deferred.

**Common plumbing.** Each renderer: imports `isWebGPULogDepthActive` + `ShaderDefine`, derives `logDepthActive`, passes `logDepthActive ? ShaderDefine.LOG_DEPTH : 0` as the module-cache key (the `code` string differs via `logDepthActive ? "…" : ""` concat, so the preprocessor sees no `//>>ifdef` to resolve — the define is purely the cache key, exactly the GroundPrimitive pattern), and adds a `_pipelineLogDepth` (Vector3DTile) / `_pipelineLogDepth` cache-guard flag (Ellipsoid) to the existing format-generation invalidation so the master-switch flip rebuilds the module + pipelines. The encode near/far prefers the stashed FULL-frustum `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` over the live per-slice `currentFrustum` (the Billboard packUniforms pattern) so producers encode against the SAME near/far the globe baked. New ambient type: `oneOverLog2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne` added to `CesiumUniformState` (cesium-js-types.d.ts) + `UniformState.d.ts` (real getter).

**Verification (probe-first per Principle 8).** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-ellipsoidprim-logdepth.mjs` (new): asserts the LOG_DEPTH pipeline builds, the flip-rebuild guard toggles `_pipelineLogDepth` across ON→OFF→ON, and 0 console / WebGPU validation errors — all PASS. It is a STRUCTURAL probe, NOT a pixel probe: the WebGPU EllipsoidPrimitive renderer produces NO visible output for a scene-placed ellipsoid (verified across radii 30 km..200 km / center via `center` OR `modelMatrix`, log ON and OFF both 0 lit pixels), a PRE-EXISTING bug orthogonal to log depth (the OFF leg is byte-identical to the pre-change shader). Two stacked causes filed as BUG-ELLIPSOIDPRIM-WEBGPU-INVISIBLE: (a) the renderer reads `primitive.modelMatrix` not the Scene's `_computedModelMatrix = modelMatrix*translate(center)`, dropping `center`; (b) the ray-cast quad emits no coverage even when placed via modelMatrix. The Vector3DTile classifiers are VERIFIED-BY-ANALYSIS + build-green + 0-validation-errors (they mirror the proven GroundPrimitive log-depth pattern exactly); a pixel-level e2e is blocked on the absence of `.vctr` test data — the only local vector assets (`Apps/SampleData/vector/*.glb`) are glTF tilesets that route through the Model pipeline, not these legacy renderers (same gap the Batch-178 2D/CV work documented). **Standing gates green:** probe-collections-regression · probe-pickposition-webgpu (dH 4.1 m, pick unaffected) · probe-bloom-parity · sandcastle-smoke (3/3). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx gulp build` clean (~51 s). (probe-classifier-logdepth-flip/settle remain in their pre-existing GroundPrimitive-Stripe `lit=0` state — unrelated to this slice's renderers — with 0 device errors.)

**Files:** `WebGPUEllipsoidPrimitiveRenderer.ts` (inline WGSL camera-UB `projection`+`logDepth` + FS log frag_depth; UBO 240→320 B; `packCameraUniforms` projection+logDepth lanes; `buildEllipsoidPipelineResources` `logDepthActive` param; `_pipelineLogDepth` flip guard); `WebGPUVector3DTilePrimitiveRenderer.js` + `WebGPUVector3DTilePolylinesRenderer.js` (VS log-z write color+velocity, `logDepth` UBO lane, define threading, flip guard); `WebGPUVector3DTileClampedPolylinesRenderer.js` (FS reverse-log `windowToEyeCoordinates`, `csm_reverseLogDepth` chunk import, `logDepth` UBO lane, flip guard); `cesium-js-types.d.ts` + `UniformState.d.ts` (`oneOverLog2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne`); `Tools/visual-regression/probe-ellipsoidprim-logdepth.mjs` (new). Docs: DEFERRED_WORK (NEW-LOG-DEPTH-REMAINING-PRODUCERS — EllipsoidPrimitive+Vector3DTile* struck SHIPPED; new BUG-ELLIPSOIDPRIM-WEBGPU-INVISIBLE), FEATURE_INVENTORY (log-depth producer list + 4 renderer lines).

## Batch 274 — WASM kernel actually loads + runs in the bundled build for all 7 Wasm*Bridge files (NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD) (2026-06-13)

**Context.** Since the WASM bridges were wired (Batches 270-273) the kernel only ever executed in the Node harness — in the BUNDLED build (`Build/CesiumUnminified/index.js`, the IIFE `Cesium.js`, and the variant bundles) the glue `import(".../ThirdParty/Workers/cesium_wasm.js")` in EVERY `Wasm*Bridge` 404'd, so every bridge silently used its byte-identical JS fallback. The whole engine WASM path (RTE, Cull, Sort, Heightmap, Matrix, PointCloud, QuantizedMesh) was dark in production. Rendering was correct (the JS twin is byte-exact) but the SIMD path never ran.

**Two failure shapes (both rooted in a glue specifier resolved relative to the EMITTED bundle, not the source file).** (a) The 5 bridges keeping `"../../ThirdParty/Workers/cesium_wasm.js"` external (RTE/Heightmap/Matrix/PointCloud/QuantizedMesh) had `../../` resolve from `/Build/CesiumUnminified/index.js` to `/Build/ThirdParty/Workers/…` → glue 404. (b) The 2 bridges (Cull/Sort) with a bare `import("../ThirdParty/…")` (no `webpackIgnore`) got the glue INLINED by esbuild; the inlined glue's `new URL("cesium_wasm_bg.wasm", import.meta.url)` then resolved against the bundle's own URL → `/Build/CesiumUnminified/cesium_wasm_bg.wasm` → binary 404. The glue + binary actually live at `/Build/<variant>/ThirdParty/Workers/`.

**Fix (bundle-wide, one resolver, all 7 bridges, all 3 formats).** New shared helper `packages/engine/Source/Scene/resolveWasmGlueUrl.js` returns `buildModuleUrl("ThirdParty/Workers/cesium_wasm.js")` — the canonical Cesium base-URL resolver `TaskProcessor` already uses for its worker + `wasmBinaryFile` paths. It yields a correct ABSOLUTE URL in every format: ESM (anchored at `index.js`'s `import.meta.url`), IIFE (anchored at the `Cesium.js` `<script>` via `getBaseUrlFromCesiumScript()` / `CESIUM_BASE_URL`), CJS, plus honoring a `CESIUM_BASE_URL` override. All 7 bridges now `import(/* webpackIgnore */ resolveWasmGlueUrl())`. Because the glue then loads as its OWN module, ITS `import.meta.url` is the real on-disk glue URL, so the sibling `new URL("cesium_wasm_bg.wasm", import.meta.url)` inside the glue also resolves correctly — one resolver fixes BOTH the glue 404 and the binary 404. Cull/Sort keep the import EXTERNAL (the `webpackIgnore` + non-literal specifier means esbuild can no longer inline it) so shape (b) is eliminated.

**Folded-in consistency fix (latent, all bridges).** The Batch-271 RTE memory-export fix is now applied bridge-wide: Matrix/QuantizedMesh/PointCloud/Heightmap stored `_wasmModule = module` (the glue NAMESPACE, which has no `.memory`) and read `_wasmModule.__wbindgen_export_0 ?? _wasmModule.memory` (always `undefined` — the wasm-bindgen glue never re-exports `memory`), so their WASM path would have caught + fallen back even once the glue loaded. They now capture `_wasmExports = await module.default()` (the instance exports object returned by `__wbg_init`, which carries `.memory`) and read it through a shared `_wasmMemory()` helper + an explicit `undefined` guard. Cull/Sort already stored the exports object in `_wasmModule` (correct); they gained a `wasmReady` getter (alias of `isAvailable`) so a single load-state probe works uniformly across all 7 bridges.

**Verification (probe-first; the kernel must ACTUALLY EXECUTE, no silent fallback).** New `Tools/visual-regression/probe-wasm-bundle-load.mjs` loads the REAL bundle in Edge and asserts, for all 7 bridges, `loadWasm()→true` + `wasmReady===true`; 0 `cesium_wasm*` 404s / failed requests (both glue + binary return HTTP 200); and a no-fallback trip-wire on the RTE kernel — `batchEncodeRange` on the WASM path (threshold=1, `_lastWasmUsed===true`) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the JS twin (threshold huge) and no "using JS fallback" warning fired. It runs in BOTH ESM mode AND `--iife` mode (against `Build/Cesium/Cesium.js`, exercising the `getBaseUrlFromCesiumScript`/`CESIUM_BASE_URL` branch) — ALL PASS in both. The node real-kernel check `Tools/wasm-subrange-encode-check.mjs` stays green (its resolve-hook loader matches the buildModuleUrl-produced specifier suffix `ThirdParty/Workers/cesium_wasm.js`). Build-system change → verified the BUNDLE: `npx gulp build` + `npx gulp buildAllVariants` green; the glue + binary are co-located under `ThirdParty/Workers/` in dual/webgpu-only/webgl-only outputs and NO bundle inlines the glue (`cesium_wasm_exports` count 0 in ESM/IIFE/CJS). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. **Standing gates green:** probe-collections-regression · probe-buffercoll-wasm-encode (now `kernel-ran=true`, 0 wasm 404s — the probe's stale "tracked separate blocker" / "excl. known 404" messaging updated to note Batch-274 fixed it) · probe-buffer-point-update · probe-logdepth-zfight · probe-buffer-logdepth-zfight · probe-collections-far-camera · probe-orbital-catalog · probe-compute-instance-generic · probe-globe-bindgroup-cache · probe-ellipsoidprim-logdepth · probe-pickposition-webgpu (dH 4.1 m) · probe-bloom-parity · probe-collections-2dcv-morph · sandcastle-smoke (3/3) · variant-smoke-test (dual/webgl-only/webgpu-only).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/resolveWasmGlueUrl.js` (new shared helper); `WasmRTEBridge.js` (import via resolver, drop stale 404 comment); `WasmMatrixBridge.js` / `WasmQuantizedMeshBridge.js` / `WasmPointCloudBridge.js` / `WasmHeightmapBridge.js` (resolver + `_wasmExports` capture + `_wasmMemory()` helper + guard); `WasmCullBridge.js` / `WasmSortBridge.js` (resolver + external import + `wasmReady` getter); `Tools/visual-regression/probe-wasm-bundle-load.mjs` (new, ESM + `--iife`); `Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffercoll-wasm-encode.mjs` (stale-messaging update). ## Batch 278 — near-earth SGP4 GPU df64 kernel: real TLEs propagated each frame on the GPU (NEW-ORBITAL-SGP4-KERNEL) (2026-06-13)

**Context.** The headline accuracy feature of Phase 5. The Batch-277 J2 stage shipped df64 (two-float, ~46-bit) helpers in the engine scaffold + a secular-J2 mean-element demo kernel. SGP4 is the real thing: the standard near-earth analytical propagator (Vallado "Revisiting Spacetrack Report #3", WGS-72) that turns a TLE into a position. The guardrail is that FP32 WGSL drifts badly vs FP64 SGP4, so the work splits FP64 CPU pre-conditioning from a GPU df64 per-frame update — and caps at NEAR-EARTH (defers SDP4 deep-space resonance), validated against python-sgp4 reference vectors. The engine stays orbital-agnostic: ALL SGP4 (init + kernel + element layout + TLE catalog) is demo/probe content riding the feature-agnostic `ComputeInstanceCollection`.

**Architecture (the two halves, per the SGP4 stage guardrail).**

1. **CPU FP64 pre-conditioning — `sgp4init()` (`Tools/visual-regression/sgp4-reference.mjs`, also inlined in the Sandcastle demo).** Parses the TLE columns (epoch, bstar assumed-decimal, inclo/nodeo/ecco/argpo/mo, no_kozai), de-Kozais the mean motion (recovers the Brouwer `no_unkozai` via the standard `del`/`adel` iteration), and computes EVERY time-independent SGP4 constant in JS double precision: the secular gravity rates (`mdot/argpdot/nodedot/nodecf`), the atmospheric-drag coefficients (`cc1/cc4/cc5/d2/d3/d4/t2cof/t3cof/t4cof/t5cof/omgcof/xmcof`, the SIMPLE-drag `isimp` switch under 220 km perigee, the `s`/`qzms24` perigee table), the periodic coefficients (`aycof/xlcof/eta/delmo/sinmao/con41/x1mth2/x7thm1`), and GMST at epoch (`gstime`). These upload ONCE as the 42-lane per-instance params; the three precision-critical secular RATES ship as **df64 (hi,lo) pairs** (`df64Split`) so `rate * tsince` keeps ~46 bits over a full day.

2. **GPU df64 per-frame update — `SGP4_KERNEL_WGSL` (`sgp4-kernel.mjs`, inlined in the demo).** Does ONLY the time-dependent SGP4 update, a 1:1 port of `sgp4()` from the validated JS FP64: secular mean-element advance (df64 angle accumulation for the fast/precise M/argp/node terms + drag corrections to a/e/M), long-period J3 periodics, the 10-iteration Kepler solve (`u = E + ω`), short-period periodics → TEME radius/orientation, and TEME→ECEF by −GMST(t) built component-wise in df64 so the RTE low part is real. `time` arrives as engine SECONDS-since-epoch; the kernel converts `tsince = time/60` (SGP4 works in minutes) — this one line keeps the demo + probe kernels byte-identical AND matched to the engine's `frameState.time − epoch` contract.

**Near-earth only (the deep-space guard).** `sgp4init` computes the orbital period `2π/no_unkozai` and flags `isDeepSpace` when ≥ 225 min. The demo + probe SKIP flagged objects — the GPU kernel NEVER sees a deep-space object, so it can never produce a silently-wrong dot. SDP4 (deep-space resonance + lunar-solar periodics) is deferred. A GPS/MEO TLE (period 718 min) is the negative test: it's flagged + counted-skipped, not drawn.

**Position-accuracy budget: < 2 km over a full day for near-earth SGP4** (SGP4 itself is a ~1 km-class model; the df64 GPU port adds only sub-meter numerical drift on top of the algorithm's own truncation). MEASURED worst: **55 m** (NOAA-19 @ 1440 min, near-polar sun-sync — the largest GMST lever arm) — 36× inside budget.

**Verification (probe-first per Principle 8; the math is checked against an AUTHORITATIVE reference, not self-consistency).** The JS FP64 `sgp4()` reference is first bit-validated against **python-sgp4 2.25** (the C++ Vallado port) to **0.0000 m** across ISS/NOAA-19/Starlink over 0–1440 min, with the deep-space GPS flagged — a dev gate (`validate-sgp4.mjs`). Then `Tools/visual-regression/probe-orbital-sgp4.mjs` (new standing gate): fetches the SHIPPED engine scaffold WGSL raw, composes prologue + scaffold + the SGP4 kernel exactly as `WebGPUComputeInstanceRenderer` does, dispatches on a probe-owned device for the near-earth catalog at five sample times across a full day, reads back the RTE high+low ECEF, and asserts (A) GPU ECEF vs the python-sgp4 reference (rotated TEME→ECEF via the validated path) worst **55 m** < 2 km, (B) the deep-space GPS is flagged + skipped while all near-earth sats are kept, (C) zero validation/compile/console errors, and (D) the demo's RUNTIME path — the REAL `ComputeInstanceCollection` + the engine seconds-since-epoch time contract + the instanced vertex-pull draw — renders + moves cyan points (142% mask change over ~45 sim-minutes). The reference vectors are EMBEDDED (generated by python-sgp4) so the probe is self-contained (no python at probe-run time). A camera screenshot of the demo confirms the catalog renders as distinct orbital shells by inclination (cyan ISS 51.6°, green NOAA-19 near-polar 99°, pale Starlink 53°).

**No engine code changed.** This is purely additive demo/probe/tooling content — the scaffold (`ComputeInstanceScaffold.wgsl`), renderer (`WebGPUComputeInstanceRenderer.ts`), and collection (`ComputeInstanceCollection.js`) are UNTOUCHED; the df64 helpers from Batch 277 were sufficient. **Standing gates green:** probe-orbital-sgp4 (new) · probe-orbital-catalog · probe-compute-instance-generic · probe-orbital-j2 (df64 15 m LEO, 145× win intact) · probe-collections-regression. `npx tsc --noEmit` unaffected (no .ts touched); no `gulp build` needed (no `Source/` engine change).

**Files (all new, demo/probe-owned):** `Apps/Sandcastle/gallery/WebGPU SGP4 Satellites.html` (real-TLE catalog: CPU sgp4init + GPU df64 kernel inlined, deep-space skipped, shells by inclination); `Tools/visual-regression/sgp4-reference.mjs` (JS FP64 SGP4 init+update+gstime+temeToEcef — the shared reference); `Tools/visual-regression/sgp4-kernel.mjs` (the GPU df64 kernel string + 42-lane packing); `Tools/visual-regression/probe-orbital-sgp4.mjs` (new standing gate); `Tools/visual-regression/validate-sgp4.mjs` (dev gate vs python-sgp4). Docs: DEFERRED_WORK (NEW-ORBITAL-SGP4-KERNEL struck SHIPPED), FEATURE_INVENTORY (compute-instance line + SGP4 demo).

## Batch 285 — pickMetadata/pickVoxelCoordinate read a stale pixel on WebGPU; readCenterPixel now arms a synchronized, guarded readback (NEW-PICK-METADATA-READBACK) (2026-06-15)

**Bug.** `scene.pickMetadata` and `scene.pickVoxel` (→ `Picking.pickMetadata` / `Picking.pickVoxelCoordinate`) read the center pixel of a freshly-rendered metadata/voxel pass via `PickFramebuffer.readCenterPixel`. On WebGPU that method (`WebGPUPickFramebuffer.readCenterPixel`) just did `_lastReadPixels.slice(...)` — but `_lastReadPixels` is only ever populated by the REGULAR `scene.pick()` color path (`end()`/`endAsync()`/`_startReadback`). So it returned a STALE pixel from a different pass, never the metadata/voxel pixel the caller just rendered. It also had NO re-entrancy guard, so a rapid re-pick could slice a half-written buffer.

**Root cause (two coupled issues).**
1. **No synchronized readback.** `readCenterPixel` never copied the current `_colorTexture` content — it depended on the color path having read the same texture, which it hadn't for the metadata/voxel pass.
2. **Submission order.** `Picking.pickMetadata`/`pickVoxelCoordinate` called `readCenterPixel` BEFORE `context.endFrame()`. On WebGPU `updateAndExecuteCommands` only records into `_currentCommandEncoder`; `endFrame()` submits it. So any readback armed inside `readCenterPixel` would be submitted to the queue ahead of the metadata/voxel render — the exact submission-order hazard `_pickAsyncWithMode` documents for `endAsync`.

**Fix (mirrors `PickDepth.getDepth`'s async-readback contract).**
- `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.readCenterPixel` now arms its OWN 1×1 `copyTextureToBuffer` readback of the current center pixel of `_colorTexture` (absolute coord = `_pickOriginX/Y + halfWidth/Height`), using a fresh per-readback staging buffer destroyed after unmap (never collides with the color-path `_stagingBuffer`). It returns a one-frame-stale cache keyed to `(centerX/Y ±2 px, _updateCount frame stamp ≤4 picks stale)`. Cold query → `[0,0,0,0]` (caller decodes "no metadata / no voxel") + arms readback; a re-pick at the same spot converges 1–2 frames later. `bgra8unorm` byte order normalized to `[R,G,B,A]` so the metadata/voxel decoders see WebGL's `readPixels` layout.
- New `_centerReadbackInFlight` guard prevents re-reading a half-written buffer (the metadata/voxel analogue of the color path's `_readbackInFlight`); cleared in the `.then()`/`.catch()` and on `destroy()`. `_updateCount` advances once per `begin()`.
- `Picking.pickMetadata` + `pickVoxelCoordinate` now call `context.endFrame()` BEFORE `readCenterPixel` so the render is submitted ahead of the readback copy. No-op on WebGL (endFrame only unbinds the default FBO; the pick FBO content persists and `readCenterPixel` re-binds it explicitly).

**Bonus fix surfaced by the probe — voxel COLOR pipeline MSAA bake.** Reproducing the voxel path exposed a separate pre-existing bug: `WebGPUVoxelRenderer`'s color pipeline descriptor had NO `multisample` field (defaulted to count:1), while the scene framebuffer render pass bakes `count = context._msaaSamples` (4 by default). WebGPU dropped every voxel color draw with "Attachment state of [Voxel color pipeline] is not compatible with [Scene Framebuffer Render Pass]". Added the `multisample: sampleCount > 1 ? { count } : undefined` bake (from `context._msaaSamples`) like every other scene-FB renderer, plus cache invalidation on sample-count change (pick + velocity pipelines stay single-sample — pick FBO and the velocity target are single-sample). The WebGPU Voxel Pick sandcastle now loads with 0 errors (was throwing the attachment-state validation error every frame). NOTE: full voxel-DATA rendering on WebGPU is still a SCAFFOLDED placeholder (FEATURE_INVENTORY §B — `VoxelPrimitive.update` returns early), so this only fixes the pipeline-state crash, not real voxel-data picking.

**Verification (probe-first, Principle 8).** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pick-metadata.mjs` (new standing gate). Because the WebGPU voxel renderer is a placeholder (so `scene.pickVoxel` can't reach `pickVoxelCoordinate`) and there is NO zero-dependency local `EXT_structural_metadata` asset (all metadata demos use ion tiles), the probe exercises the SHARED readback path directly against a known-pickable opaque Box's pick FBO: WebGPU `readCenterPixel` CONVERGES to the same non-zero pick color `[1,0,0,0]` WebGL reads synchronously (proving current-pass read, not stale), the `_centerReadbackInFlight` guard exists + clears after each readback, 0 validation/console errors across 20 rapid re-reads, and the converged RGB matches WebGL. Asset gaps (live voxel-coordinate parity blocked by the scaffolded voxel renderer / `C-R9-VOXEL-CELL-PICK`; full metadata-over-tileset decode) documented in-probe + DEFERRED_WORK, not papered over.

**Files modified:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts` (synchronized center-pixel readback + `_centerReadbackInFlight` guard + `_updateCount`), `packages/engine/Source/Scene/Picking.js` (endFrame-before-readCenterPixel in `pickMetadata` + `pickVoxelCoordinate`), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts` (color-pipeline MSAA bake + sample-count cache invalidation). New: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pick-metadata.mjs`. Docs: DEFERRED_WORK (NEW-PICK-METADATA-READBACK → SHIPPED), FEATURE_INVENTORY. **Standing gates green:** probe-pick-metadata (new) · collections-regression · pick-basic · pickposition-webgpu · compute-instance-pick · pickmodel-instanced · logdepth-zfight · sandcastle-smoke. `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `gulp build` green.

## Batch 286 — per-instance pickPosition for GPU-resident compute-instances on both backends (NEW-COMPUTE-INSTANCE-PICKPOSITION) (2026-06-15)

**Gap (not a regression — Phase-6 picking-parity follow-up to Batch 279).** `scene.pick` over a `ComputeInstanceCollection` instance returned `{collection, instanceIndex, primitive}` (Batch 279), but `scene.pickPosition` over the same dot did NOT return the instance's world position. Positions are produced by the user kernel and live ONLY in the GPU storage buffer (WebGPU) or are CPU-computed by the `cpuKernel` (WebGL2) — they're never in a form the ordinary depth-buffer pickPosition can reconstruct: a sub-pixel dot's center rarely coincides with the unprojected scene-depth sample, and on WebGPU the translucent dots don't even write depth.

**Fix — three layers, all routed through the FeatureRenderer seam (no Scene→Renderer/WebGPU import).**
1. **`Scene/Picking.js`** — `pickPositionWorldCoordinates` now object-picks at the cursor FIRST (`_pickComputeInstancePosition`). If the front record is a compute-instance — duck-typed: a `{collection, instanceIndex}` whose `collection` exposes a `getInstanceWorldPosition(index, result)` function (so Picking stays domain-agnostic; no `ComputeInstanceCollection` import) — it returns `collection.getInstanceWorldPosition(instanceIndex)` and caches it; otherwise it falls through to the EXISTING depth path unchanged. **Gated** on `context._pickableComputeInstanceFrame` (frame-stamped by `ComputeInstanceCollection.update` only when a pickable collection renders) so scenes with no compute-instances never run the extra pick pass. This gate is load-bearing: without it, the extra `this.pick` (pick render + `endFrame`) on every `pickPosition` query clobbered the shared depth state the globe's async `getDepth` readback depends on, and `probe-pickposition-webgpu` went all-undefined (caught + fixed during bring-up).
2. **`Scene/ComputeInstanceCollection.js`** — public `getInstanceWorldPosition(index, result)` delegates to the active backend's FR (new `getInstanceWorldPosition` slot on the `CesiumFeatureRenderer` interface), passing the context cached at the last `update`.
3. **WebGPU (`WebGPUComputeInstanceRenderer.ts`)** — `getWebGPUInstanceWorldPosition` reads the picked instance's ONE 64-byte `CsmInstanceRecord` slot (offset `index*64`) back from the LIVE ping-pong instance buffer via `copyBufferToBuffer` + `mapAsync`, summing `positionHigh` (f[0..2]) + `positionLow` (f[4..6], vec3 padded to 16 B) to recover the absolute ECEF position. **Same one-frame-stale sync-cache bridge as `PickDepth.getDepth`:** the FIRST query for an index returns undefined (caller falls back to depth — the SAFE pre-feature state) and arms the readback; subsequent queries for the SAME index converge once the map resolves. The cache is trusted only for the index it was armed for and within `POS_READBACK_MAX_STALE_FRAMES` (4) DISPATCHED frames (`posUpdateCount` advances per kernel dispatch, not wall time, so a paused/requestRenderMode scene keeps a valid cache). **The instance buffers gained `GPUBufferUsage.COPY_SRC`** (they were STORAGE-only) so the readback can copy from them — this was the actual bug behind the initial `(0,0,0)` readback (a missing COPY_SRC made the copy a silent no-op into a zero-initialized staging buffer). Staging buffer freed on teardown.
4. **WebGL2 (`WebGLComputeInstanceRenderer.js`)** — two parts: (a) `getWebGLInstanceWorldPosition` re-runs the `cpuKernel` for the picked index at the current sim time and returns `out.position` directly (synchronous, deterministic — the kernel is pure in index+time+params, so this is byte-identical to what the renderer packed this frame); (b) a NEW per-instance WebGL PICK path — previously WebGL compute-instances were UNPICKABLE (Batch 279 was WebGPU-only), so pickPosition had no instance to identify. Mirrors the WebGPU pick: one `context.createPickId({collection, instanceIndex, primitive})` per instance packed into a dedicated pick VAO's color slot (`ComputeInstanceWebGLPick{VS,FS}.glsl`, new — circle-discard matches the color FS so the pickable footprint matches the dot, byte-exact pick color via `BlendingState.DISABLED`, depth-write on so a nearer dot wins), pushed as a STANDALONE command on `frameState.passes.pick` (no `pickId` on the command → `SceneRenderer.executeCommand` runs it raw during the pick pass instead of deriving a uniform-pick variant). The pick VAO owns its OWN instance buffer (never shares the color VAO's instance buffer → no double-free); pick ids freed on count change + teardown.

**WebGPU index-1-picks-0 false alarm (probe, not engine).** During bring-up the probe's center dot kept resolving to instance 0. Root cause was the probe's convergence loop accepting the FIRST stable Cartesian3 — but on WebGPU both the pick FBO read AND the position readback are one-frame-stale, so the first read after moving to a new pixel can carry the PREVIOUS pixel's instance. Fixed in the probe with a per-pixel SETTLE phase (drive a few pickPosition frames at the new pixel before trusting a result) + require the position stable across two consecutive reads. Confirmed via a focused diagnostic (12-pick settle per pixel) that the engine picks 0→0,1→1,2→2 correctly with the WebGPU pick-Y mirror.

**Verification (probe-first, Principle 8).** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-compute-instance-pickposition.mjs` (new standing gate): 3 instances at fixed ECEF positions on BOTH `?renderer=webgl|webgpu`; `scene.pickPosition` over each converges to that instance's known position within 50 m (measured dist = **0.00 m** all six), empty space → undefined, never a Promise (sync contract), 0 console/validation errors. The WebGPU pick-Y mirror is applied per-backend in the probe (the same convention `probe-compute-instance-pick.mjs` documents — not a pickPosition quirk).

**Files modified:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/Picking.js` (`_pickComputeInstancePosition` + the gated hook in `pickPositionWorldCoordinates`), `packages/engine/Source/Scene/ComputeInstanceCollection.js` (public `getInstanceWorldPosition` + context cache + pickable frame-stamp), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUComputeInstanceRenderer.ts` (readback + cache fields + COPY_SRC on the instance buffers), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUFeatureRenderers.ts` (FR registration), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/cesium-js-types.d.ts` (`getInstanceWorldPosition` interface slot), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGLComputeInstanceRenderer.js` (CPU-kernel position + the WebGL per-instance pick path). New: `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/ComputeInstanceWebGLPick{VS,FS}.glsl`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-compute-instance-pickposition.mjs`. Docs: DEFERRED_WORK (NEW-COMPUTE-INSTANCE-PICKPOSITION → SHIPPED; NEW-ORBITAL-GPU-PICKING follow-up struck), FEATURE_INVENTORY (compute-instance line), CAMPAIGN_ROADMAP (Phase 6). **Standing gates green:** probe-compute-instance-pickposition (new) · compute-instance-pick · orbital-catalog · compute-instance-generic · compute-instance-webgl2 · compute-instance-webgl2-demos · pickposition-webgpu · pickmodel-instanced · collections-regression · sandcastle-smoke. `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `gulp build` green.

## Batch 289 — CSM soft-shadow PCF kernel on the receive side (NEW-CSM-SOFT-SHADOW-PCF); cast pass dispatches zero commands in viewer scenes (NEW-CSM-CAST-NO-DISPATCH-VIEWER) (2026-06-15) — PARTIAL (code shipped, visual-verify blocked)

**Gap (Phase 7 shading parity).** The WebGPU CSM receive path's `sampleOneCascade` did a single `textureSampleCompareLevel` tap → hard aliased cascade-shadow edges. WebGL's `czm_shadowVisibility` softens its shadow with a 9-tap (3x3) box PCF kernel under `USE_SOFT_SHADOWS` (`shadowVisibility.glsl:42-59`); the WebGPU CSM path had no equivalent.

**Fix (receive-side PCF — CODE SHIPPED).** An `effects.csmControl.y`-gated 3x3 PCF box kernel (summed over the 3x3 neighborhood, averaged ×1/9 — the exact WebGL kernel shape) added to `sampleOneCascade` in ALL 25 inlined receivers (`GlobeTerrain.wgsl`, `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`, every `PrimitivePhong*/PBR*/Mat*Lit.wgsl`) plus the canonical `Shadow/ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl` reference (which gained a `pcfRadius` param + threaded it through `sampleCascadeShadow` so it stays a faithful source of truth). The 25 inlined edits were applied by a one-shot codegen pass (`/tmp/csm_pcf_patch.mjs`) keyed on the stable `return textureSampleCompareLevel(cascadeDepthArray, shadowCompSampler, uv, i32(cascadeIdx), depth)` block (indentation-agnostic regex), since the inlined copies are byte-identical modulo whitespace.

- **Texel size** = `textureDimensions(cascadeDepthArray, 0)` — uniform across every receiver, no new UBO field. `textureSampleCompareLevel` (explicit LOD) is valid inside the non-uniform cascade-select branch (same pattern as the pre-existing `globeShadowPCF`).
- **`pcfRadius = 0`** keeps the original single tap bit-exact (hard fallback).
- **JS plumbing:** `WebGPUCSMRenderer` config gains `softShadows` (default true) + `pcfRadius` (default `DEFAULT_CSM_PCF_RADIUS = 1.5`, mirroring the single-shadow-map `shadowMap.softShadows ? 1.5` convention) + `softShadows`/`pcfRadius` getters; `WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js` writes `ud[CSM_CONTROL_OFFSET + 1] = csm.pcfRadius`; the three csmBinding sites (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUModelRenderer.js`, `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js`) forward `csmCandidate.pcfRadius`. New Scene option `cascadedShadowMapSoftShadows` (default true) → `WebGPUContext._initCSMRenderer` (+ `cesium-js-types.d.ts` scene slot).

**Visual verification BLOCKED — root-caused to a separate cast-side gap.** Per Principle 8 I built `Tools/visual-regression/probe-csm-soft-shadow.mjs` (3-cell matrix: WebGPU CSM hard vs WebGPU CSM soft vs WebGL soft reference; uniform bright base-color flat-ellipsoid receiver, box/model caster, top-down framing). The kernel IS compiled into the bundle (`CSM-PCF-SOFT` ×26 in `Build/CesiumUnminified/index.js`) and the radius reaches the runtime (`csmRenderer.pcfRadius` reads **0** in the hard cell, **1.5** in the soft cell). BUT the A-vs-B (hard-vs-soft) masked pixel diff is **0.000%** — because the WebGPU CSM **cast pass dispatches ZERO commands** in every CesiumViewer scene tried: `csmRenderer._castDispatches === 0` with an in-view enabled shadowMap (4 passes), `viewer.shadows = true`, `useCascadedShadowMaps = true`, and shadow-casting appearance-primitive AND glTF-model casters added. `renderCSMCastPass` early-returns only on `castCommands.length === 0`, so the Scene-side cast list (`shadowState.shadowMaps[0].passes[].commandList`, populated by `ShadowMap.createCastDerivedCommand`) is empty when the CSM pass runs — though the SAME scene casts + softens correctly on WebGL (probe cell C: real cast shadow, ~600 penumbra px). Both the CSM AND the single (non-CSM) WebGPU shadow map showed 0% shadow in the cast region for the appearance primitive → this is a broader WebGPU globe-terrain cast/receive plumbing gap in viewer scenes, NOT CSM-specific and NOT caused by this change. Tracked as `NEW-CSM-CAST-NO-DISPATCH-VIEWER` (HIGH) in DEFERRED_WORK; the probe is committed and will go green once that lands with no probe changes.

**Not done (deferred, lower value than the kernel):** the `czm_private_shadowVisibility` normal-shading-smooth clamp in `computeShadowFactorCSM`; VSM/rg32float variance soft shadows (CSM_DESIGN Slice 3 stretch goal).

**Files modified:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts` (`softShadows`/`pcfRadius` config + getters + `DEFAULT_CSM_PCF_RADIUS`), `WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js` (`csmControl.y` = pcfRadius + JSDoc), `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts` + `WebGPUModelRenderer.js` + `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` (forward `csmCandidate.pcfRadius`), `WebGPUContext.ts` (`_initCSMRenderer` softShadows arg), `cesium-js-types.d.ts` (`cascadedShadowMapSoftShadows` scene slot), `Scene/Scene.js` (`cascadedShadowMapSoftShadows` option), and the WGSL PCF kernel in `Shaders/WebGPU/Globe/GlobeTerrain.wgsl` + `Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` + `Shadow/ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl` + all 23 `Primitive/Primitive{Phong*,PBR*,Mat*Lit}.wgsl`. New: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-csm-soft-shadow.mjs`. Docs: DEFERRED_WORK (NEW-CSM-SOFT-SHADOW-PCF → code SHIPPED; NEW-CSM-CAST-NO-DISPATCH-VIEWER added), CSM_DESIGN, FEATURE_INVENTORY. **Standing gates green:** collections-regression · sandcastle-smoke · logdepth-zfight · bloom-parity. `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `gulp build` green.

## Batch 293 — PointCloudLOD slot-255 full-occupancy corruption (NEW-POINTCLOUDLOD-SLOT255-OFFBYONE) + bounded eviction for the post-process bind-group cache (NEW-BINDGROUPCACHE-EVICTION) (2026-06-15)

**Bug 293.1 (correctness) — PointCloudLOD slot-255 clobber at full workgroup occupancy.** `Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/PointCloudLOD.wgsl`'s per-workgroup compaction reserves a contiguous output range via one `atomicAdd(&visibleCount, localCount)` on lane 0, then must broadcast that base offset to the other 255 lanes. It did so by parking the value in `sharedVisible[255]` ("safe because localCount < 256"). That assumption is false: at LOD 0 every point is kept (`shouldKeepAtLOD` returns true) and when all 256 lanes of a workgroup also pass the frustum + distance test, `localCount == 256`, so `sharedVisible[255]` already holds the 256th compacted point index. Overwriting it with the base offset corrupted that point — the read phase (`visibleIndices[baseOffset + lid.x] = sharedVisible[lid.x]`) then wrote the base-offset value (0 for the first workgroup) where the index 255 should have been → the output contained a DUPLICATE of index 0 and was MISSING index 255. The subgroup-accelerated entry point (`computeMainSubgroups`) had the byte-identical clobber.

- **Root cause:** data/broadcast aliasing — a live compaction slot was reused as a scratch broadcast register.
- **Fix:** a dedicated `var<workgroup> sharedGlobalOffset: u32` scalar carries the broadcast in BOTH entry points; `sharedVisible[255]` is now only ever a real index slot. No size change to `sharedVisible` (256 slots still suffice — slot 255's sole consumer is the legitimate 256th point).
- **Why it only bit at exactly n=256:** at n≤255 the highest assigned local slot is ≤254, so slot 255 was free scratch and the old code happened to work; the corruption is strictly a full-occupancy boundary artifact. The diagnostic confirmed clean output at n=250/254/255 and corruption only at n=256.
- **Verification (probe-first, Principle 8 — the LOD processor has no Scene wiring yet, so this is a direct-dispatch compute probe, not a rendered scene):** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pointcloud-lod.mjs` (NEW) fetches the generated WGSL and runs the real compute on an Edge WebGPU device. One fully-occupied 256-point workgroup → output is the exact permutation {0..255} (count=256, unique=256, 0 dup, 0 missing, index 255 present) for BOTH entry points, 0 validation errors. Negative control: against the pre-fix shader the subgroup variant reports `missing=[255] has255=false` (the dropped point) — non-vacuous.
- **Dev-server cache gotcha (cost ~2 build cycles):** `node server.js` caches file contents in memory at startup, so after rebuilding the WGSL the probe kept fetching the STALE pre-fix shader (curl confirmed the served bytes lacked `sharedGlobalOffset` while the on-disk `Build/CesiumUnminified` copy had it). Restarting the dev server fixed it. **Lesson: after a `gulp build` that changes a served shader/asset, restart `server.js` before running a probe that fetches that asset by URL** (probes that `import("/Build/.../index.js")` are unaffected — the bundle hash changes — but raw `fetch()` of a fixed-path `.wgsl` hits the stale in-memory cache).

**Bug 293.2 (resource leak) — unbounded growth of the generic post-process bind-group cache.** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBindGroupCache` (Bloom/SSAO/DoF/GodRays/AutoExposure) stored bind groups in an unbounded `Map<string, GPUBindGroup>` evicted only by explicit `invalidateAll()`. In the "0% hit rate" failure mode its own docstring warns about (input texture views recreated each frame without a matching invalidate), the key set grew by one per frame for the whole session, leaking a `GPUBindGroup` (≈150-300 B driver state) every frame.

- **Fix:** bounded LRU + optional age eviction. The Map's insertion order is maintained as a recency list (every hit re-inserts at the tail), so the first key is the LRU → O(1) `_evictLRU()` on any over-cap miss (`maxEntries` default 1024 — far above any effect's single-digit stable key set). New `beginFrame()` advances a frame clock and, when `maxIdleFrames > 0` (default 0 = LRU-only), drops entries idle past the window. Optional `BindGroupCacheOptions { maxEntries, maxIdleFrames }` constructor arg; all six existing no-arg callers are unaffected. `getStats()` gains `evictions`.
- **Verification:** `WebGPUBindGroupCacheSpec.js` +7 tests (30/30) — cap never exceeded, LRU touch protects a recently-hit entry, 500 frames of per-frame identity churn stays bounded at ≤16 (was +1/frame unbounded pre-fix), age eviction drops/keeps by window, `maxIdleFrames=0` does no age eviction. `probe-bloom-parity` (live post-process cache path) PASS.
- **Companion IDs assessed, left open:** `NEW-RENDERBUNDLE-AGING-DECOUPLE` — `WebGPURenderBundleManager` ALREADY has bounded LRU (`_maxCacheSize`/`_evictOldest`) + age eviction (`_maxIdleFrames`/`_evictStale`) via `beginFrame()`, so it is not an unbounded-growth gap (the ID is only the aging-from-tick decouple). `NEW-RESOURCEMANAGER-KEY-EVICTION` — `WebGPUResourceManager`'s sampler/BGL caches key on `JSON.stringify(descriptor)`; both key spaces are naturally finite, so growth is bounded — lower value.

**Files modified:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/PointCloudLOD.wgsl` (slot-255 → `sharedGlobalOffset`, both entry points), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBindGroupCache.ts` (bounded LRU + age eviction + `BindGroupCacheOptions` + `evictions` stat). Specs: `packages/engine/Specs/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBindGroupCacheSpec.js` (+7 eviction tests). New: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pointcloud-lod.mjs`. Docs: DEFERRED_WORK (both IDs → SHIPPED), FEATURE_INVENTORY, CAMPAIGN_ROADMAP. **Standing gates green:** probe-pointcloud-lod (new) · collections-regression · globe-bindgroup-cache · bloom-parity · sandcastle-smoke. PointCloudLODProcessorSpec 7/7, WebGPUBindGroupCacheSpec 30/30. `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `gulp build` green.

## Batch 302 — shared collection-renderer base + the three permanent collection sentinels (NEW-COLLECTION-RENDERER-BASE partial, NEW-COLLECTIONS-ERROR-SENTINELS) (2026-06-15)

**Refactor (Phase 11) — fold the duplicated collection per-frame scaffolding into a shared base.** The five WebGPU collection feature renderers each re-implemented the same per-frame plumbing around `WebGPUResidentInstanceBuffer`. New `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCollectionRendererBase.ts` (188 non-comment LOC) extracts six sub-flows (shader-module-cache WeakMap accessor, scene-format-generation pipeline invalidation, settled-2D/CV coplanar-depth flag + pipeline-key fold, resident-instance-manager lazy create, the capture→sync→consume ORDERING as one structural call, grow-on-demand pick buffer + write). Billboard + Point migrated with zero behavior change (collections-regression upload-gate stays 0/0/0; billboard partial=1×176 B / point 1×112 B byte-identical). −131 non-comment lines of duplicated scaffolding across the two renderers. Three permanent sentinels (re-entry guard, null-target guard, size-validation/overflow clamp) added to the base hot paths per CLAUDE.md.

**Bug 302.1 (sentinel false-positive caught by probe-first) — async-bracketed re-entry guard false-trips under rapid re-render.** First cut wrapped the billboard `update` as `async function update() { begin(); try { await inner(); } finally { end(); } }`. `probe-collections-far-camera` then reported `Billboard collection update re-entered (depth 2)` and, after the threshold was raised to a "sane limit" of 16, `depth 17`.

- **Root cause:** `_updateWebGPUBillboardsInner` contains NO real `await` — the whole command-list build is synchronous — but bracketing the depth across the wrapper's `await` defers every `endCollectionFrame` to a microtask. The scene calls the collection's `update()` multiple times per frame (per frustum slice / pass) in a tight synchronous loop, so all those `end()` microtasks queue behind the synchronous work and the depth climbs to "calls this frame" before any `finally` runs. The guard was therefore measuring *suspended async overlap*, not synchronous recursion — the wrong signal for an infinite-loop sentinel.
- **Fix:** make the begin/end bracket the SYNCHRONOUS inner build directly — `function update() { begin(); try { inner(); } finally { end(); } return Promise.resolve(); }`. `_updateWebGPUBillboardsInner` is now a plain (non-async) synchronous function; the wrapper still returns a thenable so the feature-renderer `update` contract is unchanged. With synchronous bracketing the legitimate depth is exactly 1; only true stack recursion can exceed the sane limit. (Point's update was already synchronous, so its wrapper needed no special handling.)
- **Verification (probe-first, Principle 8):** rebuild → `probe-collections-far-camera` 0 console errors (was 2); the sentinel is exercised non-vacuously by a standalone unit test (esbuild-transpile the base, drive forced bad input): re-entry depth 17 logs, null buffer with 5 visible logs + returns skip, a 5-instance payload into a 3-capacity pick buffer clamps to 3 + logs — 10/10 assertions, silent on good input.
- **Lesson:** a re-entry / infinite-loop sentinel must bracket the SYNCHRONOUS work whose recursion it guards. Do NOT span an `await` (even a no-op one) — that turns the depth counter into a count of in-flight async calls, which is legitimately > 1 and frame-rate-dependent.

**Files modified:** new `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCollectionRendererBase.ts`; `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js` (sync wrapper + base-helper calls, `async`→sync inner); `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js` (wrapper + base-helper calls). Docs: DEFERRED_WORK (NEW-COLLECTION-RENDERER-BASE → PARTIAL, NEW-COLLECTIONS-ERROR-SENTINELS → SHIPPED, P1-T6 close note), FEATURE_INVENTORY, CAMPAIGN_ROADMAP. **Standing gates green:** collections-regression · billboard-partial-write · point-label-partial-write · polyline-cloud-consume · collections-far-camera · collections-2dcv-morph · entity-bulk · upstream-regression-check (26/26) · sandcastle-smoke. Sentinel unit test 10/10. `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `gulp build` green.

## Batch 303 — Phase 11: capability-getter sweep + index-wgsl churn close + doc-currency sweep (NEW-CAPABILITY-GETTER-CODIFY, NEW-INDEXWGSL-CHURN) (2026-06-15)

**Not a bug fix — an architecture-hygiene + doc-currency batch (Phase 11 of CAMPAIGN_ROADMAP).** Three tracked items.

**1. NEW-CAPABILITY-GETTER-CODIFY (architecture rule sweep).** Grepped `Source/Scene` + non-renderer code for residual `isWebGPU` / `rendererType===` branches in RENDERING logic (CLAUDE.md §2 forbids them — Scene must branch on `context.supportsX` capability getters, never the backend). Now the build output is byte-identical to the committed prettier copy, so `git diff packages/engine/index-wgsl.js` is clean after any `gulp build` (verified `prettier --check` passes + `git diff --quiet` clean post-build). **Lesson:** when a generated+tracked file churns, making the two producers (build emitter ↔ commit-hook formatter) AGREE is the only stable fix; `.prettierignore` + committing one side's form is defeated by the lint-staged stash/restore.
