## Batch NS-POLYLINE-COLLECTION-MULTI-MATERIAL — mixed-material PolylineCollection drew every non-Color group with the Color shader (2026-07-05)

**Symptom.** A single `PolylineCollection` mixing material types (e.g. a Color line + a `PolylineDash` line + a `PolylineGlow` line) rendered every NON-Color group as a solid line on WebGPU: the dashed line lost its dashes (probe `runsPerRow` 1 vs WebGL ~18) and the glow line lost its taper/falloff (colored-pixel count ~6037 ≈ a solid full-width line vs WebGL's tapered ~2777). Single-material collections were at parity.

**Root cause.** `WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js::sourceIdForMaterialType()` switched on the LOWERCASE shader-key strings (`"polylineDash"`, `"polylineGlow"`, …), but both call sites (the per-group pipeline builder at ~L1246 and the velocity builder at ~L1320) pass the collection's `material.type` string (`"PolylineDash"`, `"PolylineGlow"`, `"Color"`, …). None of those matched a case, so EVERY material type fell through to `default → ShaderSourceId.POLYLINE_COLLECTION`. The per-device shader-module cache keys on `(sourceId & 0xff) | ((defines & 0xffffff) << 8)`, so all material types collapsed to ONE key per `defines`. `prewarmPolylineShaders` had already inserted the base Color module under `(POLYLINE_COLLECTION, 0)`; the render loop's `getOrCreate(POLYLINE_COLLECTION, dashShaderCode, defines)` then returned the CACHED Color module and IGNORED the dash/glow source. The dash/glow PIPELINE was thus built from the Color shader module (the pipeline/bind-group/segment caches were correctly keyed per `materialType`, so the premise's "draws all groups with the first/Color pipeline" was half-right — same shader MODULE, distinct pipeline objects). Single-material collections only worked because no other type poisoned the shared key first.

**Fix.** `sourceIdForMaterialType` now normalizes its input through `selectShaderKey(materialType)` before the switch, so `material.type` strings resolve to the correct distinct `ShaderSourceId` (POLYLINE_DASH=10, POLYLINE_GLOW=11, POLYLINE_ARROW=9, POLYLINE_OUTLINE=12, POLYLINE_COLLECTION=7). The render-loop sourceId now matches what `prewarmPolylineShaders` inserted. Single-material output is byte-identical (same compiled module + pipeline; only the internal cache KEY changed).

**Verification.** New `Tools/visual-regression/probe-polyline-multimaterial.mjs` — one collection with hue-separated solid/dash/glow lines, per-hue run-count analysis. Pre-fix: dash `runsPerRow` WebGPU 1.00 vs WebGL 19 (RED). Post-fix GREEN: dash WebGPU 16.60 vs WebGL 17.71 (run-count ratio 1.004), glow colored 6037→3249 (taper restored, WebGL 2777), solid unchanged ~1/row, 0 gate errors — PNGs read (WebGPU now matches WebGL: solid red, dashed cyan, tapered yellow glow). Off-gate: single-material dash-only (`runsPerRow` 17.7) + glow-only (colored 3232, tapered) still correct — WebGPU numbers identical to their mixed-collection values, proving per-group rendering is now composition-independent. Standing `probe-polyline-material-primitive` GREEN. Also unblocks upstream v1.143 `PathGraphics.materialMode=PORTIONS` (per-portion material switching within one path renderer).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js` (the fix), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-polyline-multimaterial.mjs` (new gate). **Trace:** NS-POLYLINE-COLLECTION-MULTI-MATERIAL.

## Batch 634 NS-VR-HARNESS-FALSE-BLACK-GATE — capture-and-diff readiness gate accepted a lone star; false 99.9% "black globe" FAIL (2026-07-06)

**Symptom.** `capture-and-diff.mjs --scene globe-default` reported FAIL diff=99.9%: the WebGPU capture showed a stars-only black globe while WebGL was fully loaded. Reproduced identically at the pre-v1.144-merge safety branch (safety-branch A/B), while the standalone WebGPU CesiumViewer AND a manually-launched split-screen page (25s wait) rendered perfectly — proving both the engine and the v1.144 merge innocent.

**Root cause (harness, two compounding gaps).** (1) The initial readiness `waitForFunction` sampled the center 32×32 of each canvas and accepted **any single non-black pixel** — a lone skybox star satisfied it while the WebGPU viewer was still cold-compiling its pipeline cache (slow first launch after the 2026-07-06 reboot/browser update), so the gate opened before terrain arrived. (2) `applyScene` settled a **fixed rAF count** after the camera move with no `tilesLoaded` wait, so the capture fired before the invalidated tile set reloaded.

**Fix.** Readiness gate now requires `scene.globe.tilesLoaded === true` on BOTH viewers AND ≥16 non-black center pixels (a globe fills the center; a starfield leaves it ~black), timeout 60s→120s for cold pipeline compiles. `applyScene` gained a bounded (90s, non-fatal) post-camera `tilesLoaded` wait for both viewers before the rAF settle, so synthetic no-globe scenes still fall through. Result: globe-default PASS diff=0.46%, WebGPU gate clean.

**Lesson.** A readiness predicate must reject partially-initialized states the renderer can legitimately present (env pass without terrain). "Any non-black pixel" is not "the scene is up".

**Files:** `Tools/visual-regression/capture-and-diff.mjs`.

## Batch C7-GROUNDPRIM-TEXTURED-CLASSIFY-ZERO — "textured GroundPrimitive classification renders 0 px" was a probe-harness race; four real parity defects fixed en route (2026-07-10)

**Premise verification (charter step 0).** Reproduced the B595 numbers exactly at HEAD via `probe-classifier-textured-materials.mjs` (Color 7656 px, Stripe/Checkerboard/Grid/Image 0 px). Instrumented `dsColorFS` with debug returns: every textured fragment died in the log-depth slice-band check with `sliceEyeDist ≈ 1e10` (far plane) against `perSlice = [0.1, 1e8]` — the sampled packed globe depth unpacked to exactly 1.0 (cleared). A GPU texel readback confirmed `_globeDepthTexture` center = (255,0,0,255) = cleared. The globe was NOT rendering at all in the probe scenario: the screenshots show skybox stars where the globe should be, and `frameState.commandList` carried ZERO Pass.GLOBE commands while `tilesToRender=15`.

**Root cause (harness).** Per-bail-out counters in `createTileCommands` showed `pipelineNull` on 100% of calls: the globe terrain pipeline's `createRenderPipelineAsync` takes ~1-2 s of wall time on a fresh Playwright profile, and the probe's settle loops (`tilesLoaded && i > 30`, then 60 RAF frames) complete in well under a second headless — `tilesLoaded` does NOT cover pipeline readiness. Every WebGPU capture ran against a globe-less scene; WebGL compiles synchronously so only WebGPU raced. Flat Color still rendered because the depth-sample classifier is volume-rasterized and the cleared pack unpacked to 1.0 ≠ the 0.0 sky sentinel — i.e. the polygon FLOATED OVER THE SKY, masking the missing globe and making the "textured-only 0 px" framing look like a classifier bug for two campaigns (B375, B595). Fix: settle gates now poll the frustum lists for Pass.GLOBE commands (only non-zero once the async pipeline resolved). Both `probe-classifier-textured-materials.mjs` (now `ENFORCE_TEXTURED=true`) and the new acceptance probe `probe-groundprim-textured-classify.mjs` carry the gate.

**Real parity defects found + fixed once the globe was actually up:**

1. **Classifier blend double-applied alpha.** `dsColorFS` premultiplies `rgb *= a` (mirroring WebGL's ShadowVolumeAppearanceFS) but the color pipelines used the `translucent: true` src-alpha blend; WebGL's ClassificationPrimitive color pass uses `BlendingState.PRE_MULTIPLIED_ALPHA_BLEND` (srcFactor ONE). Translucent classification (Grid cellAlpha 0.5 cells) rendered darker than WebGL. Both `depthSampleColor` + `morphColor` descriptors now use an explicit premultiplied blend.
2. **Double feature-renderer dispatch → same polygon blended 3x.** `ClassificationPrimitive.update`'s Batch-130 "standalone WebGPU dispatch" also ran when the primitive was the INNER child of a GroundPrimitive (whose own `updateAndQueueCommands` override had already dispatched with the correct owner). The inner dispatch emitted a second command set with NO bounding volume (binned into every frustum slice) and the inner's default BOTH classification (a phantom Pass 6 command). Grid cells measured 227/255 = exactly three premultiplied composites vs WebGL's single-draw 146/255. Now gated on `!defined(this._updateAndQueueCommandsFunction)` — the same wrapper-vs-standalone split the WebGL path uses.
3. **Grid material lines aliased away.** The WGSL Grid branch used a fixed viewport-ratio thickness approximation → sub-pixel aliased lines. Ported GridMaterial.glsl's derivative branch (fuzz 1.2, thickness−1, smoothstep on scaled cell distance) with ANALYTIC +1px st derivatives (`surfaceUV(windowToEye(pos+1px, sameDepth)) - st`) instead of hardware dpdx/dpdy — the reconstructed st inherits depth-pack quantization noise across pixel rows, which blew `dF.y` up and washed every line out. Post-fix Grid is pixel-identical to WebGL (ROI diff 0.0%, variance 776 = 776, cell-color histogram identical).
4. **Image material vertically mirrored.** `ensureMaterialImage` uploaded without `flipY`; WebGL Material textures default `flipY: true`. Same-variance/~90%-mismatch signature. Fixed in BOTH `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer` and the mirrored `WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer` path.
5. **Packed-depth no-surface sentinel (WebGL czm_packDepth parity).** WebGL's fract-based `czm_packDepth(1.0)` = (0,0,0,0), and every ported consumer (classifier sky discard, billboard clamp, ModelPBRComplete edge background gate) tests `unpack == 0.0` for "no surface here". Our floor-based packs emitted ~1.0 for cleared depth, so the sentinel NEVER fired on WebGPU — classification volumes rasterized over sky where WebGL discards. `WebGPUGlobeDepth` (single-sample + MSAA) and `WebGPUTranslucentTileClassification` (both variants) packs now emit vec4(0) for depth ≥ 1.0.

**Verification.** `probe-groundprim-textured-classify.mjs` (NEW acceptance): Color 0.0% / Stripe 16.7% / Checkerboard 5.2% / Grid 0.0% / Image 7.3% polygon-ROI mismatch (all < 25%), lit ratio 1.00 everywhere, 0 device errors, PNGs read against WebGL. Standing: `capture-and-diff` all scenes, `probe-classification-primitive-parity` (standalone dispatch still fires), `probe-classifier-scenemode`, `ground-polyline-smoke` — see batch notes. NEW-GROUNDPRIM-CLASSIFIER-RECON-PRECISION is UNPARKED (its prerequisite premise is resolved; see DEFERRED_WORK).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js` (blend, Grid port, analytic st derivatives, flipY), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer.js` (flipY), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGlobeDepth.ts` + `WebGPUTranslucentTileClassification.ts` (pack sentinel), `packages/engine/Source/Scene/ClassificationPrimitive.js` (standalone-only dispatch gate), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-groundprim-textured-classify.mjs` (new), `probe-classifier-textured-materials.mjs` (readiness gate + enforce), `migration_doc/{DEFERRED_WORK,DEBUGGING_GUIDE}.md`. **Trace:** C7-GROUNDPRIM-TEXTURED-CLASSIFY-ZERO.

## Phase 0 FAR-001 Slice A — WebGPU timestamp profiler was present but not operational (2026-07-13)

**Symptom.** `CesiumDebug.gpuPassCost()` could not produce trustworthy GPU timings. The context constructed `WebGPUTimestampProfiler` without the granted `timestamp-query` capability, the performance manager called stale profiler APIs and had no live encoder at finalization, the debug command had no enable path, repeated labels could overwrite one another, and a one-frame request-render session might never schedule readback. The existing CPU performance trace also sampled only a late renderer subset rather than the full `Scene.render()` boundary.

**Root causes.** Timestamp ownership was split across the scene renderer, performance manager, context, and profiler with incompatible lifecycle assumptions. Query resolve/copy must be encoded after all timed passes end but before `GPUCommandEncoder.finish()`, while `mapAsync()` must start only after `queue.submit()`. The old delayed-read trigger depended on a later frame, so request-render mode could starve it. `reset()` had no generation boundary, allowing an older asynchronous map to repopulate cleared statistics. Finally, most render passes bypass `WebGPUContext.beginRenderPass`, so fixing the profiler alone still timed only manager-owned compute passes.

**Fix.** Pass the actual adapter feature into the profiler; begin opt-in timestamps before the context's first pass; finish the manager exactly once from `WebGPUContext.endFrame`; resolve/copy on the live encoder; start guarded triple-buffered readback immediately after submission; discard old-generation results after reset/destroy; aggregate repeated labels; and expose attempted/resolved, query-overflow, busy-slot-skip, and failed-readback counters. `gpuPassCost(true|false)` now explicitly controls profiling and does not allocate query resources when called with no argument while off. The central context pass path and core scene-framebuffer opens now attach timestamp writes only while profiling is active. Full `Scene.render()` CPU wall time is captured only while a trace is active and sampled after `postRender`/credit finalization.

**Known remaining instrumentation gap.** This is FAR-001 Slice A, not complete GPU-frame attribution. Many feature modules still call `encoder.beginRenderPass`/`beginComputePass` directly. The profiler currently reports the central canvas/scene-framebuffer passes and manager-owned compute dispatches; the remaining direct passes must migrate or use a graph-owned instrumentation hook, and results need an explicit unprofiled remainder before optimization priorities are treated as final.

**Verification.** Root and engine-project TypeScript compilation plus `gulp build` pass. Headless Edge/Jasmine: 22 timestamp-profiler cases, 5 performance-manager lifecycle cases, and the full-Scene CPU timing regression pass. New Node probe `probe-gpu-timestamp-profiler.mjs` on a real timestamp-capable adapter: backend WebGPU, 45 attempts, 42 resolved samples, 2 busy-slot skips, 0 failed readbacks, named `Scene Framebuffer Render Pass` average ~0.354 ms, and zero browser/device errors. Fresh seven-scene `capture-and-diff`: the six standing green scenes remain below 0.75%; the known 5K-sphere characterization remains red at 8.63%; GPU gate clean, representative images manually inspected, no baseline promotion. A preliminary display-limited benchmark remains materially red for architecture work: WebGL 60.0 FPS versus WebGPU 40.5 FPS, WebGPU first frame 496.3 ms versus WebGL 126.1 ms; this single run is characterization, not a blocking statistical baseline.

**Files:** `WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts`, `WebGPUPerformanceManager.ts`, `WebGPUContext.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRendererPassRedirect.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRendererPostFrustumChain.ts`, `Scene.js`, `CesiumDebug.js`, focused specs, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-gpu-timestamp-profiler.mjs`, and Phase-0 remediation documents. **Trace:** FAR-001-SLICE-A.

## FAR measured hot-path tranche — moving-altitude CPU/GPU improvement without feature removal (2026-07-14)

**Scope and measurement correction.** This tranche audited the accumulated fork work for real frame-time benefit and for performance regressions introduced by the remediation itself. The governing rule was explicit: no renderer feature, material, pass, public API, default visual effect, or enabled/disabled transition may be removed or visually degraded to win a metric. An idle soak is not a valid FPS test because request-render mode intentionally stops unchanged scenes. The acceptance workload therefore used the Node/Edge `moving-camera-altitude-track-3d` route (nine waypoints, 18,000 km orbit down to 300 m, then a 2,500 km rotation). The clean timing lane used two counterbalanced repetitions (WebGL→WebGPU, then WebGPU→WebGL); each separate API-instrumented attribution artifact used one WebGL→WebGPU repetition and is not timing-promotion evidence. Pre/final bundle SHA-256 values were `FA5276A3131EDEE8EEC3C3A0BDB96EB84EA925B8B466D8720EAAF6A60E3DA802` and `D2A475A12AD60113B792C8DB8A94D02A52F7A2B635A5C2EDDCE2C7AAD637B623`.

**Measured outcome.** Clean-flight medians improved WebGPU full-`Scene.render()` CPU p95 from **8.80→7.30 ms (17.0% lower)**, timestamp GPU p95 from **10.02→7.30 ms (27.2% lower)**, and GPU average from **7.71→5.42 ms (29.6% lower)**. WebGL CPU p95 moved **6.73→5.10 ms** in the same sample, so no shared-path regression was found. WebGPU wall p99 was 21.85→22.15 ms and display-paced average FPS varied around 55–60 despite the lower CPU/GPU costs; compositor/rAF pacing, not idle or presented FPS, is therefore the interpretation boundary. The instrumented lane attributed the WebGPU change per rendered frame: bind groups **11.76→4.94 (58.0% fewer)**, render passes **23.34→14.49 (37.9% fewer)**, `queue.writeBuffer` calls **79.02→10.06 (87.3% fewer)**, and submits 1.417→1.437 (effectively unchanged). Written bytes rose 105.7→112.6 KB/frame because one coalesced aligned destination range includes padding; the roughly 7 KB/frame sequential-bandwidth trade removed about 69 browser/driver calls per frame.

**Hot-path fixes.** Terrain camera uniforms now stage in the device-local ring allocator and flush at most one contiguous `writeBuffer` per dirty page before command-buffer finish/submit, with geometrically grown CPU staging and unchanged dynamic-offset/WGSL layout. Depth publication skips only provably empty post-tile/post-opaque work and caches source/MSAA bind groups by stable texture/view identity with lifecycle invalidation. Stable-disabled clustered lighting returns before dispatcher/pass-split work while preserving full enabled dispatch and exactly one enabled→disabled zero-count synchronization. Command ordering normalizes fields once before sort so the comparator is arithmetic-only; a GPU-sort producer configured with consumer mode `never` no longer uploads/dispatches/maps a result that cannot be used. Polyline grouping storage and same-type setup are reused while exact material identity/uniforms remain intact, and resources receive a 60-frame retirement grace. The common model-without-structural-metadata cache path is O(1). These are preparation slices, not a substitute for the still-open authoritative frame/submission graph.

**FAR-003 boundary.** The earlier automatic→opt-in containment of experimental GPU culling/Hi-Z/sort/indirect paths is a correctness measure and is not counted as saved work. The capability remains reachable: a forced 6,400-command GPU-sort run performed 240 dispatches, consumed 234 full permutations, matched the CPU comparator exactly, and rendered inside the measured off/on noise floor. Removing normal-frame readback/command-identity hazards and restoring safe automatic selection remain open; do not delete the feature.

**Correctness repair and defect found.** `PointPrimitiveCollection` initialization order was corrected so `context` exists before `context.limits` is read; >64K-point, render, distance, depth-test, and sync/async pick coverage is green. A separate **pre-existing** WebGPU globe `pickPosition` defect was isolated and queued as `NEW-PICK-WEBGPU-MULTIFRUSTUM-PACKED-DEPTH`: in a two-frustum view every `PickDepth` instance references the same packed texture, and the final empty near frustum overwrites the far-frustum globe depth before asynchronous readback, returning `undefined`. It still reproduces with both new depth-work gates reverted and with depth bind-group caching forcibly disabled, so neither optimization caused it. The required fix is per-frustum stable depth versions or an explicitly accumulated full-frustum graph resource; model `pickPosition` independently converges to the exact WebGL surface (0.0 m delta).

**Probe/harness corrections.** The moving visual flight now installs repository-local NaturalEarthII imagery before capture, preventing a lone starfield from masquerading as a ready globe; all nine waypoints settled with mean WebGPU/WebGL pixel difference **0.017%**, worst **0.073%**. The clustered-dispatcher probe's stale light-count slot was corrected (parameter index 4, not area-light index 5), and its per-frame probe now asserts the real one-transition/stable-off contract. Collection, point-pick, and model-pick probes ignore only the exact known Viewer boot network denial while continuing to fail renderer/device errors. The voxel-pick probe currently throws in its WebGL setup and the globe-bind-group cache probe reads a stale stats shape; both are harness work, not green renderer claims.

**Ion/network check.** Upstream `main` at `0d0c35fad1cc05ed0560f0d1ec6a9197baaef84e` was fetched and compared without exposing the credential. The local and upstream default ion token are identical (length 311; non-secret SHA fingerprint `d7f2994e9c52`); upstream last changed that token on 2026-06-25. The observed online failures are sandbox `ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED`, not a rotated/stale token. Deterministic CI remains local/offline, with a separate credentialed network lane required for streaming coverage.

**Verification and remaining boundary.** Canonical build and TypeScript compilation pass; focused Edge/Jasmine **103/103**, performance-manifest Node tests **7/7**, and `git diff --check` are green. Polyline multimaterial, collection mutation/upload, point/billboard picking, clustered transitions, model `pickPosition`, and forced GPU sort are green. The full evidence, exact artifacts, post-performance correctness queue, 52 direct-submit remainder, and planned capped-versus-verified-uncapped lanes are recorded in [FORK_PERFORMANCE_AUDIT_AND_FIX_RESULTS_2026-07-14.md](FORK_PERFORMANCE_AUDIT_AND_FIX_RESULTS_2026-07-14.md). **Trace:** FAR-303/FAR-405/FAR-408/FAR-105/FAR-504/FAR-307/FAR-204 preparation.

## C9 NEW-WEBGPU-DEPTH-PLANE-LOG-DEPTH-CONTRACT (scene half) — depth plane encoded scene log depth against the per-slice frustum instead of the full-frustum stash (2026-07-16)

**Symptom.** Sol's three-altitude horizon oracle (`probe-depth-plane-horizon-oracle.mjs`, 20 km/500 km/5,000 km): with the scene depth plane enabled and logarithmic depth active, a physically beyond-horizon point primitive stayed fully visible in the WebGPU scene-color readback at every altitude — the plane's depth writes never rejected it.

**Root cause.** `WebGPUDepthPlane.update()` runs INSIDE the frustum loop and packed its log-depth lane (`logDepthParams`) from the live `uniformState.currentFrustum` — the per-slice near/far. Every other scene log-depth producer (globe camera UB, PointPrimitive/Billboard/Label/Polyline/ground/vector-tile/ellipsoid packers) encodes against the FULL camera frustum stashed on `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` (published by `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB` at scene-update time and by both frustum loops before slicing). Two different encode curves make frag_depth values incomparable, so the plane's limb depth failed to hide geometry behind the horizon.

**Fix.** `WebGPUDepthPlane.update()` now prefers the `_logDepthEncodeNearFar` stash for (near, far) and recomputes `oneOverLog2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne` from that exact pair so encode + factor stay self-consistent; `currentFrustum` remains only as the pre-stash early-frame fallback — the same pattern as `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.packUniforms`.

**Verification.** Horizon oracle scene assertions: beyond-horizon marker occlusion went from all-fail (Sol run, ~1,400 leaked px) to 0 leaked px at 5,000 km and 70/1,416 at 500 km; the 20 km residual (538 px) was proven by reading the `campaign9-c9-02b-horizon-*-plane-{on,off}.png` captures to be the screen-space sprite quad extending ABOVE the horizon line where neither plane nor globe covers pixels (identical WebGL geometry — oracle threshold artifact, not an encode defect; production also CPU-occludes such points, which the oracle deliberately bypasses). Regressions: `probe-point-pick-webgpu` PASS, `probe-collections-far-camera` PASS (below-ground occlusion negative control), `probe-logdepth-globe` clean, `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npx gulp build` clean.

**Pick half NOT fixed (fleet prerequisite).** Re-enabling the pick depth-plane gate (`PICK_DEPTH_PLANE_ENABLED`, audit P0-1) was attempted and reverted: two instrumented oracle runs proved the pick mini-frame's depth is fleet-wide update-time hyperbolic (a log plane pick over-occludes EVERY pick over the globe disk; a consistent hyperbolic plane cannot reject the 5,000 km marker — sub-ulp Δz, less-equal ties pass). Blocked on `NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-FLEET-LOG-DEPTH` (DEFERRED_WORK.md, Campaign 9 ledger).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUDepthPlane.ts` (encode fix), `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts` (gate comment documents the fleet prerequisite), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-depth-plane-horizon-oracle.mjs` (adds read-the-PNG captures per altitude). **Trace:** C9 `NEW-WEBGPU-DEPTH-PLANE-LOG-DEPTH-CONTRACT` / `C9-02B` / audit P0-1.

## C9-BROAD-SUITE-TRIAGE — destroyObject ES6 lifecycle, PolylineGeometryUpdater constant descriptors, VoxelBounds missing maximumTextureSize (2026-07-16)

**Scope.** Broad-suite attribution + bounded closure (C9 items 65/71 + the VoxelBounds product defect from item 64/C8-30; audit amendment A13 triage for item 72).

**Bug 1 — `destroyObject` never saw ES6 class methods (item 65).** `Core/destroyObject.js` used `for...in`, which only enumerates enumerable properties; ES6 class methods are non-enumerable prototype properties, so a destroyed ES6-class instance kept every live method — a second `destroy()` could repeat native teardown, and the debug destroyed-contract throw never fired. This is why the pinned Renderer lifecycle cluster (`fails to destroy` in Buffer/CubeMap/Framebuffer/MultisampleFramebuffer/Renderbuffer/Sync/VertexArray) failed. **Fix:** walk own properties plus the full prototype chain via `Object.getOwnPropertyNames` + descriptors (nearest-to-instance wins), shadow function-valued data properties with own `throwOnDestroyed` properties, never invoke accessor getters, skip `constructor` (statics untouched), never mutate shared prototypes, and guard non-configurable properties. New `Specs/Core/destroyObjectSpec.js` (7 specs). One knock-on: the Batch-671 `DataSourceCollectionSpec` contains-regression spec asserted `contains()` still answers after `destroy()` (authored while the lifecycle was broken); its final assertion now expects the destroyed-contract throw.

**Bug 2 — PolylineGeometryUpdater lost its constant public descriptors (item 71).** The pre-Sol ES6 codemod (`39f5341e64`) dropped the four constant `value:` descriptors (`outlineEnabled:false`, `hasConstantOutline:true`, `outlineColorProperty:undefined`, `isClosed:false`) when converting `Object.defineProperties` to class getters — the public API returned `undefined` for all four. Restored as read-only getters with original JSDoc. A pre/post scan of every codemodded file's `value:` descriptor counts confirmed this was the only full drop.

**Bug 3 — `VoxelBoundsCollection.update` dropped the `maximumTextureSize` argument.** `computeTextureResolution(pixelsNeeded, textureResolutionScratch)` was called with the scratch Cartesian2 in the `maximumTextureSize` slot and `result` undefined — any voxel shape with render-bound planes creating its packed-planes texture would throw. Now passes `frameState.context.limits.maximumTextureSize` (matches the sibling `getTextureResolution` path and `ClippingPlaneCollection`).

**Renderer-20 triage (audit amendment A13).** The pinned 20 Renderer failures decompose into exactly two pre-existing clusters: 10 lifecycle (fixed here) + 10 shader-generator (`ShaderBuilder` 5, `ShaderFunction` 3, `ShaderStruct` 2 — missing `addLines` validation + trailing empty generated line; last touched Batch 243, owner item 66 `NEW-SHADER-GENERATOR-UPSTREAM-CONTRACT-PARITY`). **Zero failures attribute to the GraphicsCapabilities/ContextLimits migration** — the highest-blast-radius suspect is clean.

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Core/destroyObject.js`, `packages/engine/Source/DataSources/PolylineGeometryUpdater.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Scene/VoxelBoundsCollection.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Scene/CubeMapPanorama.js` (debug sources-contract validation hoisted above the feature-renderer dispatch so both backends validate identically; release bytes unchanged), `packages/engine/Specs/Core/destroyObjectSpec.js` (new), `packages/engine/Specs/Scene/VoxelBoundsCollectionSpec.js` (new), `packages/engine/Specs/DataSources/DataSourceCollectionSpec.js`. **Trace:** C9 items 65/71/64/72, `SOL_AUDIT_REPORT_2026-07-16.md` A13.

## C9-17 Slice A — settled model group-1 (material/IBL) bind-group caching (2026-07-17)

**Type:** performance/allocation reduction (not a bug fix), Campaign 9 Wave 2 item 33 / FAR-309. PARTIAL — Slice A + Slice C invariant-4 certification landed; Slices B/D remain.

**Premise verified first:** `probe-model-instance-bg-cache.mjs` on clean `da04ab31aa` reproduced the weekly-defense §8.6 figure exactly — **560 settled `createBindGroup`/40 frames = 14/frame**, `settledMergedInstanceBindGroupCreates=0`. A label/entry-count breakdown + stack fingerprint attributed **8/frame to group-1 material BGs, all from `updateWebGPUModel`** (not the env-capture path, idle here; `Model.update` runs 2×/model/frame = main + offscreen env-map render), with `updateWebGPUSun`/`TAA_BG`/`PostProcess-IdentityBlit` accounting for the other 6/frame.

**Root of the churn:** `buildMergedMaterialBindGroup` did a raw unlabeled `device.createBindGroup` every frame per primitive at three emission sites, and `buildModelIBLEntries` allocated a fresh 6-entry array every frame even when the resolved IBL views were unchanged — so there was no stable identity to cache on.

**Fix (`WebGPUModelRenderer.ts`):**

- Labeled the group-1 descriptor `"Model merged material bind group"` (probe/API-lane attribution).
- Refactored `buildModelIBLEntries` → `resolveModelIBL` (returns the five identities: diffuse/specular views, sampler, SH buffer, brdf-LUT view) + `buildIBLEntriesFromResolved` + memoizing `getOrCreateModelIBLEntries` (per-model `cache._iblEntriesMemo`; stable array while the five identities are unchanged — byte-identical bindings 33-38, neutral-placeholder path binds 33 & 34 to `defaultIBLCubemapView` exactly as the retained `defaultIBLEntries`).
- New `getOrCreateMergedMaterialBindGroup(primCache, slot, …)` mirroring the Batch-665 group-2 instance cache, three per-primitive slots (primary/silhouette/translucent — never alias since they differ only by material buffer), keyed on exact identities (device, layout, materialBuffer, lightBuffer, textureEntries ref, featureIdEntries ref, iblEntries ref). Cache hit ⇒ 0 creates; any identity change ⇒ 1 rebuild.
- Wired the three emission sites; the env-capture-path `buildMergedMaterialBindGroup` (`getOrCreateModelCaptureCommands`) stays UNcached (out of scope, now labeled). Released the three slots in `destroyPrimitiveCacheResources`.

**Evidence (post-change, same probe):** `settledAllBindGroupCreates` **560 → 240** (−320 = the exact `entries-25`+`entries-27` group-1 buckets), **`settledMergedMaterialBindGroupCreates=0`**, `settledMergedInstanceBindGroupCreates=0`, `identitiesStable=true`, 0 device/page errors. The 240 remainder is 100% non-model owners (Sun 80, TAA 80, canvas blit 80). Every model group-1 settled create eliminated.

**Key trap avoided:** caching group-1 on the `iblEntries` array identity WITHOUT first memoizing the IBL resolution (trap #2) would miss every frame on a fresh array and "work" while creating just as many bind groups — verified by the labeled counter dropping to 0, not by eyeball. The brdf-LUT placeholder→real flip (trap #3) is in the memo key, certified by `WebGPUModelMaterialBindGroupCacheSpec` and `probe-model-ibl` (BRDF LUT consumed, GATE PASS).

## C9-17 Slice B — loader-owned geometry revision tokens for O(1) positive-path validation (2026-07-17)

**Type:** performance/allocation reduction (not a bug fix), Campaign 9 Wave 2 item 33 / FAR-204. PARTIAL continuation — Slice D remains (STOP-gated for C10).

**Premise verified first:** `ModelPrimitiveGeometry.getGeometryRevision` (`:43`) already probed `_webgpuGeometryRevision ?? _geometryRevision ?? …`, but a repo-wide search confirmed NOTHING in the engine assigned any of those fields — Principle-7 scaffolding awaiting exactly this task. So the per-frame geometry cache validation (`geometrySignatureMatches`) always ran the deep O(attributes × fields) signature walk, including 12 quantization vector-component reads per attribute per frame for quantized (Google-Photorealistic-class) assets.

**Producer half (the stamps):** new exported `bumpGeometryRevision(target)` in `ModelPrimitiveGeometry.js` — centralizes the `_webgpuGeometryRevision` field name (can never drift from the probe chain; monotonic per-object `(x ?? 0) + 1`, never resets → no ABA). Called at every geometry-identity mutation site enumerated by a `typedArray =` grep across `Source/Scene`:

- `GltfLoader.js` — `finalizeDracoAttribute`, `finalizeSpzAttribute`, `finalizeAttribute` (each sets `attribute.typedArray`/`.buffer`), and the index-accessor geometry callback (`indices.typedArray`/`.buffer`).
- `PntsLoader.js` — the point-cloud attribute build (`attribute.typedArray`/`.buffer`).
- `PrimitiveLoadPlan.js` — `generateOutlines` (CESIUM_primitive_outline reindexes every attribute, replaces the index array, and adds the outline-coordinates attribute).

**Consumer half (the fast path):** `geometrySignatureMatches` tries `geometryRevisionFastPathMatches` FIRST. It returns a HIT with ZERO deep walk only when every base + morph attribute (and the index accessor, if present) carries a DEFINED, unchanged token AND every captured object identity + data identity still holds. It returns false — falling through to the extracted `geometryDeepWalkMatches` — the instant any token is absent (uninstrumented producer) or any identity/revision differs. Two safety layers: (1) the fast path compares data identity, so an unstamped external typed-array swap that forgot to bump is still rejected; (2) a `//>>includeStart('debug', pragmas.debug)` cross-check runs the full walk on every HIT and `console.error`s on divergence (revision-hit MUST imply signature-match — catches a missed stamp in dev, stripped from release). New diagnostics `revisionHitCount`/`walkHitCount`.

**Key soundness insight:** the token is an OPTIMIZATION, not the correctness mechanism — the deep walk (kept verbatim) is always correct, and the fast path can only ever produce a HIT (never a MISS decision), so a stale token can never cache stale geometry: it either matches (proven unchanged) or the walk runs.

**Evidence:** `probe-model-instance-bg-cache.mjs` (extended to read `getPrimitiveGeometryCacheDiagnostics()` deltas over 40 settled frames): `settledGeometryRevisionHits=240`, `settledGeometryWalkHits=0` — 100% of settled geometry validations use the fast path (incl. the morphed AnimatedMorphCube), with Slice A's bind-group gates still green. `ModelPrimitiveGeometrySpec` 8/8 (5 new), WebGPUModel 35/35, `probe-taa-model-skinned-velocity`/`probe-model-scene-modes`/`verify-model-feature-pick`/`probe-model-color`/`probe-model-ibl` all PASS. tsc/eslint/build clean.

**Coverage (honest-partial):** standard glTF (regular/Draco/SPZ) + PNTS + outlines stamped. Gaussian-splat index attribute, I3dm instance attributes (not in the per-vertex signature), and user-code post-load mutations fall to the deep walk (safe). Skinning/morph animation updates joint/morph-weight buffer CONTENT, not geometry attributes, so it never bumps the token — the cache does not thrash.

## C10-03 — MSAA scene-COLOR boundary bytes: demand-driven "resolve-on-consume" (2026-07-18)

**Type:** performance/bandwidth (redundancy elimination), Campaign 10 W2 / S4-1. Maintainer-ratified ruling §2 (b)+(d). NOT a bug fix.

**Root inefficiency (S4-1):** `WebGPURenderTarget.getColorAttachments` UNCONDITIONALLY baked `resolveTarget` on every scene-FB color attachment when `sampleCount>1`, so WebGPU ran a full-frame multisample resolve at EVERY `pass.end()` — ~9 scene-COLOR resolves per default-globe frame, of which at most 1 (the pre-post-process blit input) is consumed. ~8 wasted resolves × ~41.5 MB (33.2 MB MSAA read + 8.3 MB write) ≈ ~330 MB/frame @1080p (analytical, S4-2; slot-1 rows omitted there so the boundary figure is understated).

**Fix (demand-driven resolve-on-consume):** `getColorAttachments(clearValues?, {resolve?})` (default `true` — byte-identical for `renderPassDescriptor`/`getClearPassDescriptor` and every unmigrated caller); the three scene-FB open sites (`WebGPUSceneRendererPassRedirect.setupSceneFramebufferRenderPass`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer._resumeScenePass`, `_clearDepthStencil`) pass `resolve:false`. New `WebGPURenderTarget.createColorResolvePassDescriptor()` builds a zero-draw single-color `{loadOp:"load",storeOp:"store",resolveTarget}` pass (label `SceneFramebuffer-Color_demand_resolve`). New `WebGPUSceneRenderer._ensureSceneColorResolved(context)` fires that pass — raw on the frame encoder (mirrors `WebGPUSceneFramebuffer._clearTarget`) — before every resolved-color consumer: refraction capture (`_captureRefractionScene`), OIT composite (`WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass`), invert-classification composite (`_runInvertClassificationComposite`), bounding-volume debug (`_executeBoundingVolumeDebugPass`, only when drawing), and ALWAYS before `_runPostProcessing` (`WebGPUSceneRendererPostFrustumChain`).

**Staleness (why the registry alone is insufficient):** the C9-09 attachment-demand record is a per-frame PURE record — it cannot track intra-frame resolve staleness, which is load-bearing for write-consumer correctness (the fallback invert composite writes the single-sample resolve view, then `resumeDefaultRenderPass` opens the CANVAS pass — so without staleness the pre-PP ensure re-resolves and STOMPS the composite). So one context flag `_sceneColorResolvePending`, set at the SINGLE `beginRenderPass(target==="scene-framebuffer")` hook (leans on C9-07 `_activePassTarget`, NOT the guide's 12-site fallback), cleared only by the ensure helper, reset conservatively at frame/pick begin + FB recreate. Registry integration: `resolvedSceneColor` observe-only demand in `computeAttachmentDemand.other` + measured `sceneColorResolveOpens` counter surfaced in `getAttachmentDemandStats` (C9-09 record↔actual model). Default-on kill switch `_sceneColorResolveElisionEnabled` (revert-boundary safety + identical-build A/B oracle).

**Files:** `WebGPURenderTarget.ts`, `WebGPUContext.ts`, `WebGPUAttachmentDemandRegistry.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRendererPassRedirect.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRendererPostFrustumChain.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts`, new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-msaa-resolve-elision.mjs`.

**Evidence:** probe-msaa-resolve-elision (bucketed per-attachment beginRenderPass counter, per-frame) — scene-COLOR resolves eager **9 → demand exactly 1** (`sceneColorResolveOpens===1`), slot-1 G-buffer resolves PRESERVED (untouched), MSAA1 = 0 both paths + byte-identical, `recordMatchesActual` green. Byte-identity: capture-and-diff globe-default historicalWebgpu **0.01%** (clean-tree PRE/POST) + crossBackend **0.46%** + demand-canvas-pass empty-scene byte-identical to pre-change. Part (d): Batch-234 TAA→samples-1 forcing intact, gate probe effective `_msaaSamples===1` under TAA + restore→4, probe-taa-jitter GATE PASS. Gate net green (attachment-demand-registry, demand-canvas-pass 24/24, scheduler-octree-demand, diag-demand-gates, frustum-count-3d, point-pick, collections). Perf (moving-altitude 2 reps): WebGL 5.30 ms flat (no regression), WebGPU 5.40 ms (+0.20 vs 5.20 anchor, within noise — CPU-neutral as expected for a GPU-bandwidth elision); API lane confirms 1 demand resolve/frame. No banner (ruling (b) lands independent of the promotion bar). tsc/gulp build clean.

**Traps hit:** (1) the invert/refraction consumers need `endCurrentRenderPass` UNCONDITIONALLY (for their copy/composite regardless of MSAA), but the ensure helper early-returns under MSAA-off — so those sites KEEP their `endCurrentRenderPass` and ADD the ensure after (byte-identical under MSAA-off). (2) In-page `drawImage(webgpuCanvas)` reads back BLACK — all probe pixel checks must use Playwright element screenshots + PNG decode. (3) The Viewer's own rAF render loop interleaves a frame during `await requestAnimationFrame` — the per-frame counter must read synchronously right after `render()` with NO await between. (4) The CesiumViewer offline default-camera intermittent black-globe (`NEW-WEBGPU-PICKPOSITION-CONVERGENCE-REGRESSION`) flips between shipped/eager per session and reduces the scene-FB segment count — correctness must be gated on capture-and-diff (split-screen substrate), not that view.

## C10-05 — model material textures mip-0-locked (minification shimmer / sample-bandwidth) (2026-07-18)

**Type:** correctness/quality parity + GPU sample-bandwidth (not a crash bug), Campaign 10 W2 / S3-1. Two coupled prongs — shader + allocation.

**Root defect (grep-confirmed, universal):** `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` sampled EVERY material texture with `textureSampleLevel(tex, samp, uv, 0.0)` — hard-locked to mip 0 — because the fragment shader has non-uniform discards (clipping/alpha-mask) and WGSL forbids implicit-derivative sampling after them. So at minification WebGPU aliased mip 0 while WebGL trilinear-filtered from the correct mip: shimmer + ~100× texture-DRAM traffic on distant tiles (register S3-1).

**PREMISE CORRECTION (STOP-AND-BLOCK #3, runtime-traced — the register's "textures allocate mipLevelCount:1" is FALSE for the live path):** real glTF/3D-Tiles material textures take the STUB path in `WebGPUModelRenderer.createGPUTextureFromReader` (`return stubGPU.texture`), NOT the fallback. `probe-model-mip-inspect` on unmodified `main` shows BoxTextured baseColor `path=stub, mipLevelCount=9` (256², minFilter NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR). The stub (`WebGLStubTexture.ensureTextureAllocated` + `generateMipmap`) already allocates + fills a full chain whenever the glTF sampler requests mipmaps, and the per-texture sampler (`getSamplerForReader`) sets `mipmapFilter:"linear"` with unbounded maxLod — so the chain existed and the sampler was ready; ONLY the shader's mip-0 lock kept it unused. Ordering is race-free: `Texture` ctor runs `setupSampler`→`texParameteri` (sets `wantsMipmaps` from the min-filter) BEFORE `texImage2D`→`ensureTextureAllocated`, and `wantsMipmaps=true` ⟺ MIPMAP min-filter ⟺ `GltfTextureLoader.generateMipmap` called — no allocated-but-unfilled chain (which would make grad sample garbage). LINEAR-sampler assets get a single level on BOTH backends (parity — grad on a 1-mip texture = mip 0 = byte-identical).

**Fix — prong 1 (shader, the actual fix):** hoisted `dpdx/dpdy` of all 5 material UV sets at `fragmentMain` entry in uniform control flow (Batch-57 globe pattern), converted 36 material `textureSampleLevel(...,0.0)` → `textureSampleGrad(...,d_dx,d_dy)` (baseColor/normal/MR/specGloss + all KHR: specular/iridescence/anisotropy[direct+IBL]/clearcoat/sheen/thickness/transmission + customShader-block & main-path emissive/occlusion). Also hoisted `baseColorUV_dx/dy` in the 4 alt-pass entries and converted their 8 alpha-test baseColor samples so the alpha-mask/blend discard stays mip-consistent with the color pass at distance (WebGL mip-samples the alpha test in every pass; leaving pick/velocity at mip 0 would diverge). KEPT at LOD 0 (census): batch/feature-pick/featureId, edge & globe-depth & refraction screen-space, SDF, clipping data, brdfLut, IBL diffuse irradiance, IBL specular radiance (roughness→explicit-LOD), atmosphere LUTs.

**Fix — prong 2 (allocation, completeness):** the sole hardcoded `mipLevelCount:1` creation site was the SECONDARY fallback in `createGPUTextureFromReader` (reached only when a Texture has no stub GPU texture). Closed it: allocate `WebGPUMipmapGenerator.calculateMipLevelCount(w,h)` + copy mip 0 + generate via the frame-owned `WebGPUContext.enqueueImageryMipGeneration` (C9-12A — no private draw-path submit), gated on `readerRequestsMipmap` (GL 9984-9987) so data/property/LINEAR textures stay single-level. Source is inherently uncompressed (compressed KTX2 takes `Texture.create` with its own transcoded chain, never this branch) → never blits a compressed format. Threaded an optional `EnqueueMipFn` through `ensurePrimitiveCache`/`createMaterialTextures`/`tryCreate`/`refreshDeferredModelTextures` (backward-compatible; property-texture caller passes no sink → untouched).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelRenderer.ts`; new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-model-mip-inspect.mjs` + `probe-model-mip-shimmer.mjs`.

**Evidence:** PRE→POST distant-minified BoxTextured (probe-model-mip-shimmer, high-frequency aliasing energy normalised by luminance): WebGPU HF/lum PRE 0.492 (raw 30.26, mip-0 aliased) → POST 0.416 (raw 25.42) = WebGL trilinear 0.418 (ratio 1.176→0.994). PNGs read: POST-WebGPU minified logo smooth/trilinear, matches WebGL, no new artifact; near-field magnified byte-identical (probe-model-pbr-ibl-parity −1.42% lum). probe-model-instance-bg-cache settled green (deviceErrors 0 = grad shader compiles + WGSL uniformity OK; settledMergedMaterialBindGroupCreates 0 + identitiesStable = Batch-687 identity survives, no per-frame mip/BG thrash). probe-model-color/scene-modes(2D/CV/3D)/ibl/ktx2-ibl GATE PASS (compressed path not regressed). capture-and-diff globe-default crossBackend 0.46% (band) + historical 0.01%. tsc/gulp build clean; engine .ts not eslinted by flat config. Perf: ~100× sample-bandwidth win is a GPU-timestamp metric on large distant photogrammetry (analytical, no offline asset) — CPU-neutral, no banner claimed.

## C10-02 — phantom all-discard TRANSLUCENT twin per batch-table primitive (2026-07-18)

**Type:** command/upload economics (redundancy elimination), Campaign 10 W2 / S11-1. NOT a bug fix — a per-frame redundant-work gate. WebGL parity port.

**Root inefficiency (S11-1):** the WebGPU model FR (`WebGPUModelRenderer.updateWebGPUModel`) never consulted `styleCommandsNeeded`. For EVERY opaque batch-table primitive (`passClass===0 && hasBatchTable`) it emitted a second `Pass.TRANSLUCENT` "twin" command every frame — the `C-R1-TILE-BATCH` dual-emission block (Batch 101). For an unstyled tileset all features are opaque, so the twin's `passClass=1` FS (`ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` class-discard, gated on `tileBatchFlags.x>0.5`) `discard`s 100% of fragments — re-running the full VS + rasterization + per-fragment batch fetch, with `discard` disabling early-Z, only to throw every fragment away. Per prim/frame it also cost a redundant 768 B `writeBuffer` (material-UB translucent), a second `packMaterialUniforms`, and a permanent `Pass.TRANSLUCENT` bin entry that defeats the empty-pass-skip optimization and inflates the back-to-front translucent sort. (Batch 687 already identity-cached the twin's group-1 bind group, so bind-group builds are NOT part of the cost.)

**WebGL parity target (`ModelDrawCommand.pushCommands:149-160`):** the twin (`_translucentCommand`) is derived only when `!isTranslucent && !hasSilhouette`, and pushed only when `defined(styleCommandsNeeded) && styleCommandsNeeded !== ALL_OPAQUE`; the opaque primary is suppressed (`return`) only in `ALL_TRANSLUCENT`. `StyleCommandsNeeded` is computed from `BatchTexture.translucentFeaturesLength` in `ModelFeatureTable.update`/`Model.updateStyleCommandsNeeded`.

**T-3 premise (highest-risk) VERIFIED with runtime evidence:** `BatchTexture.translucentFeaturesLength` IS maintained on the WebGPU path — the whole style→counter→styleCommandsNeeded chain lives in backend-agnostic `Model.update` (`updateStyle`→`setColor`→`BatchTexture.setColor` increments the counter; `updateFeatureTables`→`ModelFeatureTable.update` recomputes `styleCommandsNeeded`) which runs BEFORE `buildDrawCommands` for both backends. `probe-c10-02-style-economics.mjs` on WebGPU (BatchedWithBatchTable, 10 feats): translucentFeaturesLength = unstyled **0** / subset(5 even feats alpha 0.4) **5** / all **10** / cleared **0**; `styleCommandsNeeded` = 0/2/1/0 respectively. Crucially, a never-styled batch-table tile reports `styleCommandsNeeded===0 (ALL_OPAQUE, DEFINED)` at steady state (not undefined — `Model.applyStyle:1121` sets it on first realization), so the INV-6 conservative formula kills the phantom for the default unstyled case.

**Fix (single file):** in `WebGPUModelRenderer.ts`, near the dual-emission block, read `model.styleCommandsNeeded` FRESH each frame (T-2: cheap field, never cache — it goes stale across a style change), compute `emitTranslucentTwin = !defined(scn) || scn !== StyleCommandsNeeded.ALL_OPAQUE`, and require it in the twin gate. Import `StyleCommandsNeeded`; add `styleCommandsNeeded?: number` to the local `ModelLike` interface (build tsconfig types `model` as `ModelLike`). INV-6: undefined → conservative emit.

**INV-3 shipped PARTIAL (deliberate):** the opaque primary is NOT suppressed in `ALL_TRANSLUCENT`. The primary carries this primitive's pick derivative (`attachPickToColorCommand`) and the twin carries none; pick dispatches per-command from the command list (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.executeWebGPUCommand`→`selectCommandVariant`), so suppressing the primary would drop feature pick (INV-5). In `ALL_TRANSLUCENT` the primary's passClass=0 FS discards every fragment, so the residual opaque draw is visually correct — a small redundant draw in a rare case. Full suppression (attach a pick derivative to the twin) filed as `NEW-WEBGPU-ALLTRANSLUCENT-PRIMARY-SUPPRESS`.

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelRenderer.ts`; new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-c10-02-style-economics.mjs` + `probe-c10-02-pixel.mjs`.

**Evidence:** PRE→POST tile-content command counts (probe-c10-02-style-economics; Pass 5=CESIUM_3D_TILE primary, 9=TRANSLUCENT twin): unstyled {total 2, trans 1}→{1,0} (INV-1, count halved), subset {2,1}→{2,1} (INV-2), all-translucent {2,1}→{2,1} (INV-3 PARTIAL), cleared→{1,0} (INV-4). INV-1 pixel-unchanged proven with an in-build `__C10_02_PRE__` toggle A/B (removed before final): WebGPU render pixel-identical PRE↔POST (unstyled nonBlack 8606 vs 8612, RGB [75.1,89.6,97.1] both — sub-pixel AA jitter). Gates: tsc/gulp build clean; probe-model-instance-bg-cache settled green (merged bg creates 0/0); probe-standalone-model-pick PASS both backends (INV-5 no-regression); capture-and-diff globe-default historical 0.01% + crossBackend 0.46%. Perf (synthetic N-overlapping-tileset A/B — canonical moving-altitude globe route has no batch-table tiles, structurally timing-neutral): N=120 command 240→120/trans 120→0, Scene.render median 11.3→9.6 ms (~15%), p95 19% (noise 5.3 ms); N=250 command 500→250, median 22.6→19.9 ms (~12%), p95 3.9% (noise 10.1 ms). Median win consistent; p95 noise-dominated → no banner (structural slice lands on its own oracle).

**Pre-existing gaps surfaced (identical PRE↔POST, NOT this slice — filed in DEFERRED_WORK):** (1) WebGPU per-feature translucent *color* does not visually composite (subset renders grey where WebGL shows red/green); (2) WebGPU b3dm tile-content `scene.pick` returns nothing while WebGL resolves the feature (standalone Model pick works). See `NEW-WEBGPU-TILE-FEATURE-TRANSLUCENT-COLOR-COMPOSITE` and `NEW-WEBGPU-B3DM-TILE-CONTENT-PICK-EMPTY`.

## C10-06 — WebGPU boot serial waterfall + never-wired globe prewarm (2026-07-18)

**Type:** TTFF / boot concurrency + prewarm (S8-1 + S8-2). NOT a bug fix — a boot-latency reduction. Campaign 10 W3 (first of the boot chain; C10-07/C10-08 depend on it). Three independently-committable sub-steps.

**Premise (measured PRE, `run-performance-campaign.mjs moving-camera-altitude-track-3d --renderer both -r3`):** WebGPU `rendererReady→firstFrame` median **176.1 ms** ([150.4, 176.1, 176.5]) vs WebGL **16.2 ms** ([15.2, 16.2, 79.4]) — a **10.9× / +159.9 ms** first-frame stall (matches the guide's recorded ~9.1×/+146 ms). Traced the waterfall: (a) two awaited **no-op** shader inits on the init critical path (`initPrimitiveShaders`/`initCollectionShaders` — bodies are `return;` at `WebGPUPrimitiveShaders.js:246` / `WebGPUCollectionShaders.js:66`); (b) an inline `await import("./WebGPUPrimitiveIndexUtils.js")` mid-`_initialize` (a dependency-free 137-line pure util); (c) `requestAdapter` issued serially INSIDE the pool, gated behind the ~3 MB WebGPU chunk parse; (d) the one real prewarm (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceShaders.initShaderCache` — 2 GlobeTerrain shader-module variants) ran **lazily on the first tile draw**, and `WebGPURenderPipelineCache.preloadBatch`/`WebGPUShaderCache.preloadBatch` both had **0 callers**; `WebGPUContext._warmUpPipelines` was a comment-only no-op whose comment wrongly called the stall "below the perceptible threshold" (T-06-g — falsified by the +160 ms measurement).

**Fix — Step A (kill the serializers):** `WebGPUContext.ts` — deleted the two dead `await initPrimitiveShaders/initCollectionShaders` calls (INV-06-6); converted the inline dynamic import to a static top-of-file `import { WebGPUPrimitiveIndexUtils }` and assigned `_primitiveIndexUtilsCache` synchronously (the util has zero top-level imports + no module-level side effects, so it folds into the already-lazy WebGPU chunk — a net win, not eager-chunk bloat T-06-d; the sole consumer `supportsTriangulationDebug` already tolerates any value).

**Fix — Step B (adapter/chunk concurrency, INV-06-1):** `ContextFactory.createWebGPU` now kicks `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter({powerPreference})` BEFORE `await import("./WebGPU/WebGPUContext.js")`, so GPU-process negotiation overlaps the ~3 MB chunk parse. The in-flight promise threads through a new optional `WebGPUContextOptions.prefetchedAdapter` → `WebGPUDevicePool.acquireDevice` → `_createNewDevice`, which reuses it (core path only — compatibility needs its own adapter) and **falls back to its own `requestAdapter` on any null/rejection** (conservative — never forces a mismatched prefetch, STOP-AND-BLOCK). Only fired on the WebGPU path (never wakes the GPU process on a WebGL-only page, T-06-e). The prefetch is `.catch(()=>null)` at the source so an unconsumed prefetch (device-sharing / compat path) never becomes an unhandled rejection, and it is **stripped from `originalOptions`** so device-loss recovery always re-requests a fresh single-use adapter (T-06-f). Design 2 chosen over the RendererType prefetch-cache (Design 1) for conservatism/self-containment; the Scene-overlap variant is a later enhancement.

**Fix — Step C.1 (real globe prewarm, INV-06-2/3):** added top-level `warmUpGlobeRenderer(context)` to `GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js` (the exact path (a) the old `_warmUpPipelines` comment named) — it mirrors the lazy `addWebGPUDrawCommandsForTile` init block byte-for-byte (same `RendererClass`, same static `getShaderCode()` WGSL, same canvas format, same device-keyed `_webgpuGlobeRenderers` WeakMap slot) and runs `.initialize()`, which fires the 2-variant GlobeTerrain shader-module prewarm during the idle init window. Wired fire-and-forget from `_warmUpPipelines` via a **dynamic import** (`import("../../Scene/...").then(m=>m.warmUpGlobeRenderer(this)).catch(()=>{})`) so it never blocks `_initialize` and never introduces an eager Renderer→Scene cycle. Multi-context safe (keyed off `context.device`, INV-06-5). `context.canvasFormat || getPreferredCanvasFormat()` matches the lazy path identically, and the shader-module cache keys on `(sourceId, defines)` (format-independent) so INV-06-3 holds robustly.

**Step C.2 (deterministic PIPELINE prewarm) — DEFERRED:** the depth-plane/globe-depth/PP/sky/auto-exposure pipelines are built with the scene-FB attachment identity (`colorFormat`/`depthFormat`/`sampleCount`/MRT) resolved only during the SceneRenderer resource-ensure step at/after frame 1 — NOT at `_initialize`. Prewarming them at init would guess formats → T-06-a cache miss. Filed `NEW-WEBGPU-BOOT-DETERMINISTIC-PIPELINE-PREWARM` for C10-07's resources-ready hook (where the formats ARE known). Honest partial per queue §1 promotion rule — each sub-step is independently committable.

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/ContextFactory.ts`, `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts`, `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUDevicePool.ts`, `Scene/GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js`; new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-boot-prewarm-c10-06.mjs`.

**Evidence:** Mechanism (deterministic, `probe-boot-prewarm-c10-06.mjs`): prewarm log at console **seq=3** (init window), first `[WebGPU:TileDraw] PROCEEDING` at **seq=26** (frame 1) → prewarm beats frame 1; globe bind-group-cache global published, imagerySlotCount=16; 0 errors (T-06-c satisfied — prewarm is NOT a silent no-op). Timing (POST, same campaign, -r3): WebGPU `rendererReady→firstFrame` median **176.1 → 166.2 ms (−9.9 ms / −5.6%)**, 0 device errors; **p95/tail NOT improved** (POST [160.2, 166.2, 183.5] overlaps PRE) — the module-compile prewarm moves *some* cost earlier but the residual +150 ms is the lazy `createRenderPipeline` assembly (C.2/C10-07 territory). Byte-identity: `capture-and-diff globe-default` historicalWebgpu 0.01% / crossBackend 0.46% (band 0.43–0.77) — INV-06-3 holds (timing changed, not pixels). Regression net: `probe-frustum-count-3d` PASS (WebGPU=WebGL=1 all altitudes, C10-01 parity preserved), `probe-demand-canvas-pass` ALL PASS both backends (empty-scene byte-identical), viewer boots WebGPU + WebGL 0 errors. Gates: eslint clean on all 4 changed files (776 repo errors are pre-existing `.claude/workflows/*.js` debt, untouched), engine `tsc --noEmit` clean, `gulp build` clean.

**Banner: NOT CLAIMED.** −5.6% on the median just grazes the ≥5% bar but the p95 is noise-dominated (3-rep overlapping distributions) and did not improve — the named boot metric does not robustly clear the bar. Steps A + B + C.1 land on green mechanics (dead-await removal, adapter concurrency, and a *proven* globe module-compile prewarm that beats frame 1, all byte-identical) per queue §1 (truthful miss + green mechanics = VALID COMPLETE). The bulk of the +150 ms delta is pipeline-compile, addressed by C10-07 + the deferred C.2.

## C10-07 — model color + PP pipelines fully synchronous (async-schedule conversion) (2026-07-18)

**Type:** compile scheduling (async pipeline creation), Campaign 10 W3 / S8-3. NOT a bug fix — moves the model on-screen color pipeline off the synchronous mid-draw `createRenderPipeline` onto the central `createRenderPipelineAsync` ready-gate, plus wires the deterministic-boot prewarm hook C10-06 deferred. Depends on C10-06; enables C10-08.

**Premise (probe-c10-07-async-model-pipelines.mjs, WebGPU + CesiumMilkTruck, offline):** PRE the model COLOR pipeline compiled through **synchronous** `device.createRenderPipeline` (2 sync, 0 async; census confirmed the model cache had 12 sync sites, 0 async). The deterministic boot set was also sync: SkyAtmosphere×2, GlobeDepth-DepthCopy×2, PostProcess identity/tonemap/FXAA×3, DepthResolveMSAA×1. Already-async via the central cache: environment Moon/Star/Sun + DepthPlane×2. **CRITICAL premise nuance:** sync `createRenderPipeline` returns in **0.1 ms** but DEFERS the heavy DXC compile — the true compile cost of the 215 KB `ModelPBRComplete` monolith is **~1900 ms**, exposed only by `createRenderPipelineAsync`. This is IDENTICAL to the globe: the `Globe terrain (uncompressed, noNormals, opaque)` pipeline compiles async in **2256 ms** with its pick variant sync at 0.1 ms. So the model's async behavior (color async, pick sync, ~2 s cooking delay) exactly MATCHES the shipped globe pattern.

**Fix — Part 1 (async model color pipeline):** `WebGPUModelPipelineCache.getPipeline` now resolves through the central `WebGPURenderPipelineCache` like the globe's `resolveGlobePipelineEntry`: `getPipelineSync` hit → return sync; else kick `getPipeline` (→ `createRenderPipelineAsync`) once per key (`_pendingColorPipelines`) and return `null` so the caller SKIPS the draw that cooking frame. The descriptor was extracted to `buildColorPipelineDescriptor` shared by the async path and the synchronous fallback (no central cache) so both are byte-identical (INV-07-4). `WebGPUModelRenderer.ts` gains two null-skip guards — the primary command build (`if (!defined(activePipeline)) continue;` in the per-primitive loop) and the translucent-twin build (`if (defined(primCache.translucentPipeline))`) — because `WebGPUDrawCommand` requires a non-null pipeline (throws / would `setPipeline(null)`). The central cache is threaded via a 4th constructor arg from `context.webgpuPipelineCache ?? null`. **C2-22 magenta contract under async (INV-07-3):** `createRenderPipelineAsync` REJECTS on validation error (unlike sync, which returns an INVALID pipeline), so the magenta swap + `_errorSwapGeneration++` moved into the `.catch`; the sync error-scope is kept for the fallback path. A scene-format-generation guard in `.then`/`.catch` drops a resolve that lands after an HDR/log-depth/format toggle cleared `_pipelines` (and `_pendingColorPipelines` is cleared alongside every `_pipelines.clear()`). **Pick / velocity / classification / capture / silhouette / depth-write stay SYNCHRONOUS** (INV-07-2 documented escape hatch — a pick during a cooking frame must not return a wrong hit; matches `resolveCapturePipelineEntrySync`).

**Fix — Part 2 (deterministic-boot prewarm hook):** new `prewarmDeterministicPipelines(host, config)` in `WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts` fires once at the first `ensureResources` (where the scene-FB `colorFormat`/`depthFormat`/`sampleCount` are resolved — the exact site the C10-06 Step-C.2 defer identified) and warms the depth-plane deterministic set via the central cache's `warm()` (the previously-0-caller preload machinery, S8-1), bumping observable `context._deterministicPrewarmCount`. `WebGPUDepthPlane` stashes its color + pick descriptors and exposes `prewarm(cache)` (idempotent — the plane already self-warms in `initialize`, the cache dedupes cached/pending keys).

**Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/{WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts, WebGPUModelRenderer.ts, WebGPUDepthPlane.ts, WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts}`; new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-c10-07-async-model-pipelines.mjs`.

## C10-08 — model shader specialization BLOCKED on an exhausted ShaderDefine register (Phase-0 STOP-AND-BLOCK #0) (2026-07-18)

**Type:** Phase-0 bit-budget audit / STOP-AND-BLOCK verdict, Campaign 10 W3 (last of the boot chain, deps C10-07 LANDED). NOT a code change — a documented honest block (C9-12 / C10-04 precedent). No engine code touched; tree carries doc edits only.

**Task premise (verified on the live tree, not the guide's Batch-675 snapshot):** `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` (4,168 lines) is a runtime-flag uber-shader — **70 `hasFlag()` material branches** decide feature variation per-fragment. The rank-1 specialization axis (guide H5) is shadow mode; its gate is at `:3177` (`if (effects.pointLightControl.x > 0.5) {…} else if (effects.csmControl.x > 0.5) {…}`) with the CSM/point-shadow sampling helpers inline at `:1585-1826`. Note the shadow gate reads a **scene-wide effects UBO** (uniform control flow, coherent across all fragments), so the win specialization targets is not branch-divergence but **worst-path register/occupancy pressure** — Tint compiles the union of all feature paths into one ISA and allocates registers for the superset, so a base-color-only draw runs at clearcoat+sheen+CSM+IBL occupancy (guide H5 "Architecture today"). Source-level stripping (not uniform branch-skip) is what recovers occupancy.

**Phase-0 verdict = BLOCKED-on-define-width.** The `ShaderDefine` registry (`WebGPUShaderDefines.ts`) is a **Uint32 and is EXHAUSTED**: bits **0-30 all occupied, no gaps, none reclaimable/deprecated** (read all 31 entries; highest `MODEL_METADATA_MAT_TRANSPORT = 1<<30`). Only bit 31 remains — the JS **sign bit** (`1<<31 = -2147483648`), the last slot and a hazard. The specialization as scoped genuinely REQUIRES a new global bit because:

- The **shared `//>>ifdef` preprocessor is the only mechanism** that gives byte-identical-at-`defines=0` (the `//>>else` branch emits the exact original bytes → identical module hash) AND a distinct `(sourceId,defines[,keySalt])` module-cache entry AND real source-level dead-branch stripping (the occupancy win). It **throws on any unregistered flag** (`WebGPUShaderPreprocessor.ts:111-116`, `resolveDefineBit`→undefined→Error) — there is **no model-local `//>>ifdef`**.
- **Model-local alternatives fail the charter (both named in the orchestrator directive, both traced):** (a) WGSL pipeline-overridable `override` constants are NOT threaded into the render pipeline path (only `WebGPUComputePipelineCache` passes `constants:`; `WebGPURenderPipelineCache`/`WebGPUModelPipelineCache` do not), are pipeline-level so they never become distinct module-cache entries (breaks the acceptance's `(sourceId,defines,keySalt)` rule), and editing the source to read them rehashes the shared 215 KB model module for EVERY scene (breaks "defines=0 byte-identical", INV-08-5/T-08-f); (b) keySalt only disambiguates already-different source strings — it cannot strip the base branch without editing the base source (breaks byte-identical) or a private model-only substitution namespace, which guide H5 Step-0(c) EXPLICITLY forbids ("Surface, don't route around.").

Per the governing orchestrator rule ("if it genuinely needs new GLOBAL define bits and only bit 31 (or none) remains, STOP — do not consume the last bit"): **do not bank bit 31 for one axis.** Filed the prerequisite `NEW-WEBGPU-SHADERDEFINE-WIDTH-EXPANSION` (aka `C10-08b` / C11-149) — widen the register (hi/lo Uint32 pair or Number/BigInt) across the module-cache key math, `computeKey`'s `md<<3`, `MATERIAL_DEFINE_MASK`, the preprocessor, and every `(x & BIT)` site — as the immediate next work. The 33rd-bit build-break in `WebGPUShaderModuleCache` (G9:68-71) makes the widening non-optional.

**Sequencing deviation surfaced (maintainer to ratify):** guide H5 / C10 queue / C11-plan G9 (`:1074/1087`) sequenced "C10-08 banks bit 31 → C10-08b widens." This verdict **flips the dependency** per the orchestrator directive: C10-08b (widen) FIRST, then promote ALL model axes (incl. shadow) cleanly. Banking the fragile sign-bit for one axis is throwaway motion — the widening is required for the remaining 6-7 axes regardless. If the maintainer prefers the original plan, promoting shadow mode into bit 31 as a render-mode bit (module-hash-scoped, via a `maybeUpdateForShadow` sticky flag + `//>>ifdef MODEL_SHADOW_*` around `:3177/:1585-1826`) is a ~1-session slice that composes cleanly with the C10-07 async ready-gate — it is implementable, it is just deliberately NOT done here under the "don't consume the last bit" directive.

**Files:** none (engine). Doc-only: `QUEUE_2026-07-16_CAMPAIGN10.md` §3.2 C10-08 row → BLOCKED; `DEFERRED_WORK.md` `NEW-WEBGPU-SHADERDEFINE-WIDTH-EXPANSION`; this entry.

**Gates:** N/A (no code). `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/engine/tsconfig.json` not required (doc-only change); no shader/pipeline touched → `pipelineStatus`/`capture-and-diff` unaffected.

## C10-11 — pick-fleet log-depth BLOCKED: one fleet producer (voxel) has NO log-depth infrastructure (Phase-0 premise-broken) (2026-07-18)

**Type:** Phase-0 fleet re-derivation + premise-verification / STOP-AND-BLOCK verdict, Campaign 10 W4 (P0, XL). NOT a code change — a documented honest block (C10-08 / C10-04 / C9-12 precedent). No engine code touched; the tree carries doc edits only.

**Task premise (verified on the live tree at HEAD = Batch 706, not the guide's snapshot).** The pick FBO is uniformly HYPERBOLIC by DESIGN today — confirmed PRE: every native pick producer EXCEPT the already-converted `ComputeInstanceRender` writes standard rasterizer z, and several pick pipelines are *explicitly pinned to the base (non-LOG_DEPTH) module* to keep the pick FBO self-consistent-hyperbolic (`WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:710-734` "pick stays hyperbolic … so the pick FBO stays hyperbolic and self-consistent (CLAUDE.md pick rule)"; `WebGPUBufferPointRenderer.ts:297-300` "the pick module … never sees the frag_depth write (pick stays hyperbolic)"). C10-11 REVERSES that fleet-wide design choice so a log-encoded pick depth plane (C10-12) can depth-test coherently.

**Corrected fleet (larger + more heterogeneous than the guide's "~14"; ~24 pick entries / ~20 files):** Cohort A shader-only (color module already LOG_DEPTH-compiled) — globe `fragmentPickMain`, model `fragmentPick{Main,HoverMain,MetadataMain}`, ellipsoid `fragmentPickMain`. Cohort A + JS module/define swap (pick pinned base today) — splat, buffer point/polygon/polyline. Cohort B dedicated pick modules (VS varying + FS struct + OR-in LOG_DEPTH at the pick build site; camera-UB log lanes ALREADY packed) — billboard/point/polyline collection pick shaders + the six `PrimitivePick*.wgsl`; ground/vector-tile derived via `WebGPUDerivedCommand` PICK. Reference (already converted) — compute-instance (`ComputeInstanceRender.wgsl` `vertexPickMain` `v_logDepth` + `fragmentPickMain` `csm_writeLogDepth`). Full per-family table with file:line, cohort, PRE, and convert path is in `DEFERRED_WORK.md` `NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-FLEET-LOG-DEPTH` (Phase-0 correction, 2026-07-18).

**Verdict = BLOCKED. The voxel producer has NO log-depth infrastructure and cannot be converted cleanly in this slice.** `WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts` = **0** grep hits for `LOG_DEPTH`/`logDepth`/`v_logDepth`/`csm_writeLogDepth`/`frag_depth`; its COLOR entry `fragmentMain` (`:760`) returns a bare `@location(0) vec4<f32>` (hyperbolic) and BOTH pick entries (`fragmentPickMain :1009`, `fragmentPickVoxelMain :1103`) do the same, on pick pipelines with `depthWriteEnabled:false` (`:2679`, `:2710`); the voxel UBO (`struct Uniforms :185`) has `mvpRelativeToEye` but no near/factor/far log lanes. The renderer-wide log-depth epic (`NEW-WEBGPU-GLOBE-CLASSIFY-DEPTH-PRECISION`, `DEFERRED_WORK.md:1565`) converted "ALL GEOMETRY/**OPAQUE** PRODUCERS" only; the voxel (translucent volumetric — writes no depth) was **deliberately excluded** and is not among the tracked residuals (`:1607` lists only the standalone point-cloud + splat, both since shipped). So the guide H6 classification of voxel as Cohort A ("module already carries LOG_DEPTH ifdefs + the `v_logDepth` varying from its color path") is **factually wrong**. Converting voxel pick cleanly is a mini-epic — grow the voxel UBO with log lanes, add `csm_vertexLogDepth`/`csm_writeLogDepth` + a `v_logDepth` varying, define plumbing, PLUS a design decision on what depth a volumetric first-hit pick writes (box-surface vs density-hit) — infrastructure that belongs to a voxel-color log-depth prerequisite (extend `NEW-LOG-DEPTH-REMAINING-PRODUCERS` to the voxel), NOT this pick slice ("one concern per slice").

**Why the single blocker stops the whole slice.** The pick FBO has ONE shared depth attachment (`WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts` — `depthView`/`depthTexture`), so a mixed hyperbolic/log fleet is incoherent by construction (INV-2 all-or-nothing): converting everything except the voxel leaves the voxel over-occluded by any log producer drawn ahead of it in the shared depth (globe when `globe.pickable`, or the depth plane after C10-12). Rule 3 forbids shipping a partial fleet. ⇒ STOP; no producer converted.

**Guide drift recorded (for a future H6 correction):** (1) the Phase-1/INV-4 pseudocode adds `if (v_logDepth <= 0.9999999) { discard; }` as a near-cull, but NO color-side `csm_writeLogDepth` site (80+ across globe/model/collections/primitives/buffer/splat/compute-instance) has that discard — mirroring the color sibling means writing log `frag_depth` with **no** near-discard (adding one would DIVERGE from the color path, trap #8's own warning); (2) voxel mis-classified Cohort A; (3) fleet is ~24 entries, not "~14".

**Standing-red status (honest):** `NEW-WEBGPU-PICKPOSITION-CONVERGENCE-REGRESSION` is **INDEPENDENT** of this slice — `scene.pickPosition` reads the main-pass globe-depth texture (already log-encoded via the globe COLOR path), not this pick FBO (see the globe pick note `GlobeTerrain.wgsl:3074-3075`). The pick-fleet conversion would neither fix nor worsen it.

**Reversed-Z reconciliation (mandatory doc note, done):** log `frag_depth` is the conservative WebGL-parity default; when the fleet eventually lands its ~24 pick entries join the FAR-707/`C10-GT-REVERSED-Z-SLICE-B` convert-back surface. Cross-linked in `DEFERRED_WORK.md` `NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-FLEET-LOG-DEPTH` + the C10-GT dossier surface table + here. Per `C11-GT-01`/`C10-13` the reversed-Z spike verdict must be recorded in all three before this is treated as PERMANENT; do NOT convert to reversed-Z now.

## NEW-WEBGPU-VOXEL-PICK-LOG-DEPTH — the C10-11 voxel blocker is cleared; both voxel pick entries now write log frag_depth (gated OFF by default) (2026-07-18)

**Type:** Prerequisite for C10-11 (Campaign 10 W4). Add-only log-depth infrastructure on the voxel PICK path, GATED off by default so the uniformly-hyperbolic pick FBO stays byte-identical until C10-11 flips the whole fleet. Files: `WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts`, `WebGPULogDepth.ts`, `WebGPUContext.ts`, `cesium-js-types.d.ts`, new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-voxel-pick-logdepth.mjs`.

**Premise-verify verdict (no maintainer design call).** Both pick fragments already resolve a well-defined FIRST hit (`fragmentPickMain`: first `s.a > densityThreshold`; `fragmentPickVoxelMain`: first density / first alpha-saturating sample). But neither hit POSITION is Rule-4-liftable: `fragmentPickMain`'s `p` lives in the camera-CENTERED ±0.5 phantom box (`cameraPositionEC=0`, `minBounds/maxBounds=±0.5`), so `mvpRelativeToEye * p` yields a degenerate ~0.5 m depth (NOT the voxel's real distance — this was caught by the first probe run, where the phantom-box depth broke the object pick); `fragmentPickVoxelMain`'s hit is in proxy/shape-local space (lifting it needs an absolute-ECEF f32 reconstruction → Rule-4 violation). **Resolution:** both entries write the **box PROXY geometry front-face log depth** — the `v_logDepth` varying the VS computes via the clean RTE clip path (`input.worldPos → mvpRelativeToEye`, `csm_vertexLogDepth`), the task-sanctioned conservative default (the first hit is at/behind the entry face; box scale ≪ the km-scale pick-depth-plane discriminator). The picked VoxelPrimitive/cell is UNCHANGED — only the frag_depth changes from hyperbolic-none to log-encoded entry depth.

**Fix.** `WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts`: (1) `struct Uniforms` — repurposed the two zero vec3 pads (`_pad0`→`logDepthNear` f19, `_pad1`→`logDepthFactor` f23; byte layout unchanged), packed from `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` (FULL-frustum, preferred) with the `currentFrustum`/`oneOverLog2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne` fallback (same recipe as `WebGPUEllipsoidPrimitiveRenderer.packUniforms`). (2) Added `csm_vertexLogDepth`/`csm_updatePositionDepth`/`csm_writeLogDepth` + `VertexOutput.v_logDepth` + the `vertexMain` compute, all `//>>ifdef LOG_DEPTH`. (3) `fragmentPickMain` + `fragmentPickVoxelMain` return a shared `VoxelPickFragOutput` struct writing `@builtin(frag_depth) = csm_writeLogDepth(v_logDepth, logDepthFactor)` under `//>>ifdef LOG_DEPTH` — the `//>>else` single-`@location(0)` struct is output-byte-identical to the historical bare-vec4 return; every discard/return site preserved for naga's NEW-4-E terminator analysis. (4) The two PICK pipelines compile the `ShaderDefine.LOG_DEPTH` module + `depthWriteEnabled:true` (distinct `[ld]` descriptor names) ONLY when the gate is active; a flip-rebuild guard (`_pipelinePickLogActive`) is stamped alongside the format/MSAA generation. Gate = new `isWebGPUPickLogDepthActive(context, frameState)` (`WebGPULogDepth.ts`) + `WebGPUContext._pickLogDepthWriteEnabled` (default **FALSE** — the pick-fleet master switch, SEPARATE from the scene `_logDepthWriteEnabled`; the pick mini-frame's shared depth attachment is all-or-nothing, INV-2). The COLOR + VELOCITY pipelines never carry LOG_DEPTH → depth behaviour unchanged.

**Verification (probe-first).** `probe-voxel-pick.mjs` PASS (gate off — cell picks correct cross-backend, 0 errors → default byte-identical). `probe-voxel-parity.mjs` PASS (voxel COLOR IoU 0.986, avg-color L1 **0** → color path untouched). NEW `probe-voxel-pick-logdepth.mjs` PASS (gate FORCED on: `[ld]` pick pipelines bound with `depthWriteEnabled:true`; cell + object picks still return the correct voxel; a nearer "blocker" voxel correctly OCCLUDES a farther one in the shared pick FBO → positive proof the log frag_depth is WRITTEN, non-degenerate, monotonic; 0 device/console errors → LOG_DEPTH module + both pick pipelines compiled/built). `capture-and-diff --scene globe-default` PASS (crossBackend 0.46%, no collateral).

**Gates:** `tsc --noEmit -p packages/engine/tsconfig.json` clean; eslint clean; `gulp build` clean; `buildAllVariants` clean; `variant-smoke-test` all 3 PASS.

**C10-11 (`NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-FLEET-LOG-DEPTH`) is UNBLOCKED.** The remaining ~22 pick entries convert next, then flip `_pickLogDepthWriteEnabled` true in one coordinated all-or-nothing change. Follow-up nicety (not a blocker, tracked in `DEFERRED_WORK.md`): `fragmentPickMain` writes the box proxy BACK-face depth (the pick pipeline culls front faces → the rasterized fragment is the far face) — a conservative-FAR stand-in, correct for the standalone-voxel common case; a nearer entry-face depth would need a cullMode change (risks the pick footprint) or a Rule-4-safe proxy→RTE lift (not available).

**Type:** Campaign 10 W4 (P0, XL). The earlier same-day BLOCKED entry above was superseded once Batch 708 (`NEW-WEBGPU-VOXEL-PICK-LOG-DEPTH`) cleared the voxel hard-blocker. **What changed.** Every native WebGPU pick producer now writes log-encoded `@builtin(frag_depth)`, gated on the SEPARATE `isWebGPUPickLogDepthActive(context, frameState)` = `context._pickLogDepthWriteEnabled && frameState.useLogDepth` (NOT the scene `_logDepthWriteEnabled`, because the pick mini-frame owns one shared depth attachment — INV-2 all-or-nothing). Each family strips the scene `LOG_DEPTH` bit from its color defines and re-adds it only on this pick gate, so with the switch OFF the whole fleet is byte-identical (uniformly hyperbolic pick FBO). Converted (25 files): globe (`GlobeTerrain.wgsl`/`WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts`/`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts`), model incl. hover/metadata/precise-pass (`ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`/`WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts`/`WebGPUModelRenderer.ts`), ellipsoid, splat, buffer point/polygon/polyline/primitive, billboard/point/polyline collection pick shaders + renderers, the six `PrimitivePick*.wgsl` (`WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.ts`).
