## C12-29 S1 — eclipse/occultation state + continuous sun fade: the binary sun cull stops popping, and the Moon becomes an occluder (2026-07-24)

**Type:** Missing subsystem, not a regression (research gate: `migration_doc/ECLIPSE_EFFECTS_RESEARCH_2026-07-24.md`, maintainer rulings §6a — E1 default-on + `enableEclipse`, E5 the S1-first pin, E6 analytic dual-cone). First slice of the C12-29 epic; maintainer-pinned to land BEFORE the C12-18/C11-160 sun-PP refactor so its continuity probe becomes that refactor's regression gate.

**Premise (re-verified this session, all anchors current).** Sun occlusion in this engine was a boolean with no intensity path.

**WebGL** — `Scene.updateEnvironment` sets `environmentState.isSunVisible = this.isVisible(cullingVolume, environmentState.sunDrawCommand, occluder)` (`Scene.js:3821-3825`), bottoming out in `Occluder.isBoundingSphereVisible` (`Core/Occluder.js:101-145`). The sun's BV radius is `SOLAR_RADIUS * (1 + glowLengthTS)` = 6 R_sun at the default `glowFactor = 1` (`Sun.js:329-330`). Frame N the whole disc+glow billboard is skipped (`EnvironmentRenderer.js:43-58`; the sunBloom PP is gated on the same boolean at `FramebufferOrchestrator.js:163`), frame N+1 it draws at full brightness. That single-frame step is the maintainer's screenshot.

**WebGPU** — `updateWebGPUSun` builds a `WebGPUDrawCommand` with **no** `boundingVolume` (`WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer.js:612-619`), so `Scene.isVisible` early-returns true and the sun is NEVER culled. Occlusion is purely per-pixel (`depthCompare: 'less-equal'`, quad clamped to the far plane), so the glow above the limb never dims at all.

**Moon** — zero `eclipse` hits in `packages/engine/Source`; the only occluder ever constructed is the Earth sphere. A sun-behind-moon frame rendered two independent bodies with zero light coupling.

**Cause.** There was no per-frame quantity representing "how much of the sun can this camera see". Everything downstream (billboard, bloom, scene light, atmosphere, IBL) consumed a boolean.

**Fix — two new pure CPU modules + one consumer.**

`Scene/computeSolarObscuration.js` (new; no Cesium imports, node-testable). One integrand serves both occluders because in the camera-anchored ANGULAR frame the Earth limb and the lunar disc are the same problem — a circular occluder of angular radius `ro` at separation `d` from a solar disc of angular radius `rs`. That is the aerospace dual-cone shadow model written in angles: `d >= rs+ro` no contact, `|rs-ro| < d < rs+ro` penumbra, `d+rs <= ro` umbra, `d+ro <= rs` antumbra/annular. Blocked flux is a 1-D radial quadrature over rings of the solar disc weighted by the fraction of each ring's circumference inside the occluder, `c(r) = acos((d² + r² - ro²) / (2·d·r)) / pi` with the two saturating branches, against the C12-15 limb-darkening law `I(mu) = 0.3 + 0.93·mu - 0.23·mu²`, `mu = sqrt(1 - (r/rs)²)`. `c` has kinks at `r = |d-ro|` and `r = d+ro`, so the domain is split there and a 16-point Gauss-Legendre rule (nodes built once by Newton on the Legendre polynomial) runs per smooth sub-interval — 48 integrand evaluations worst case, and the accuracy comes from the splitting rather than from raising the order. Numerator and denominator use the SAME nodes, so totality is exactly 1.0 rather than 1.0-within-quadrature-error, and disjoint is exactly 0.0. Every `acos` argument is clamped and the Heron product guarded non-negative (both drift out of domain at tangency/totality, where an unguarded NaN would poison the whole frame's lighting).

`Scene/EclipseState.js` (new). Publishes `frameState.eclipseState` = `{enabled, valid, sunVisibleFraction, earthOcclusionFraction, moonObscuration, moonPositionWC, sunAngularRadius, earthAngularRadius, moonAngularRadius, earthSeparation, moonSeparation, eclipseMagnitude}` — one object mutated in place, never reallocated. Called once per frame from `Scene.js` `render()` immediately after `uniformState.update(frameState)`. It derives the Moon's ECEF position itself (Simon1994 + `Transforms.computeIcrfToCentralBodyFixedMatrix`, memoised on the frame time so multi-view scenes pay once) because `UniformState` keeps only the moon's EYE-space direction (`UniformStateComputations.js:182-189`) and `Moon.update` runs only when `moon.show` is true (`Moon.js:104-106`) — an eclipse must dim the sun with the decorative moon hidden. Combination is `sunVisibleFraction = (1 - earthOcclusionFraction) * (1 - moonObscuration)`: exact whenever either term is 0 or 1 (every single-occluder configuration), continuous, monotone in both inputs, confined to [0,1]. A moon farther from the camera than the sun is never treated as an occluder (that is lunar-eclipse geometry, not solar).

**Guard parity by construction.** The Earth occluder radius is read off `frameState.occluder.radius` — the very sphere `Scene.updateEnvironment` feeds to the legacy binary cull — rather than rebuilding `ellipsoid.minimumRadius + minimumTerrainHeight`. That makes the continuous fade and the surviving cull geometrically incapable of disagreeing, and reproduces every `SceneUtilities.getOccluder` guard for free: 2D/Columbus view, hidden globe, underground camera and translucent globe all leave `frameState.occluder` undefined, so the Earth term is exactly 0 there — matching today's "the sun is always visible" behaviour in those modes. `GlobeTranslucencyState.sunVisibleThroughGlobe` is mirrored as the one extra guard `updateEnvironment` applies on top.

**The legacy binary cull is deliberately UNTOUCHED.** It fires only when the ~6 R_sun glow BV lies entirely inside the occluder's horizon cone, which strictly implies the far smaller solar DISC is fully occluded — i.e. the cull can only fire in frames where `sunVisibleFraction` is already exactly 0. Worked numbers for a 400 km vantage (`rho_earth = asin(6356752/6771000) = 69.85°`, `rho_sun = 0.266°`, `rho_BV = 1.598°`): the disc fade band is sun-elevation `-20.42° .. -19.88°`, and the cull boundary is `-21.75°` — 1.3° INSIDE the alpha-zero region. So the pop is killed by the alpha fade alone, the culling perf is preserved, and the `enableEclipse = false` position stays trivially byte-identical.

**The one consumer in S1 — sun billboard ALPHA, both backends.** `Sun.update` computes `getEclipseSunFactor(frameState.eclipseState)` and publishes `frameState.sunEclipseAlpha` BEFORE the feature-renderer branch (the C7-SUN-STARS-EXTINCTION convention), so WebGL's `u_eclipseAlpha` uniform and the WebGPU uniform buffer read one identical scalar. `SunFS.glsl` gains `out_FragColor.a *= u_eclipseAlpha;`; the sun WGSL gains `color = vec4f(color.rgb, color.a * u.eclipseAlpha);` with `eclipseAlpha` occupying the former `_p2` pad at byte 124 (already written as 0.0, already reserved by the 256-byte UB — a rename plus a use, **no** stride/alignment/binding/BGL delta and **no** new ShaderDefine bit; C12 exit-gate item 5, registry exhausted). ALPHA and not RGB: WebGL blends `ALPHA_BLEND` where dimming rgb produces a black disc over the sky, WebGPU blends additively with srcFactor `src-alpha`; an alpha-only multiply fades correctly under both, so the design is pre-neutralised against the C11-115 blend flip.

**Toggle.** `atmosphericConditions.lighting.enableEclipse`, **default true** (ruling E1). It gates only APPLICATION — the geometry is computed unconditionally so probes and tooling can read the physics with the effect off. `getEclipseSunFactor` returns EXACTLY `1.0` when the state is absent, invalid, or disabled, and `x * 1.0 === x` bit-for-bit in IEEE 754, so the off position is byte-identical on both backends.

**Verification.** `Tools/visual-regression/eclipse-state.spec.mjs` (`node --test`, **28/28 pass**): exact endpoints (disjoint 0.0, umbra 1.0, internal/external tangency), monotonicity across 2000 samples, degenerate/NaN inputs → 0, limb darkening blocking MORE than area when it covers the centre and LESS at grazing contact (both signs are physical — the crossover is at `d ≈ 1.12·rs`), annular concentric LD 0.871 vs uniform 0.810, lens-area symmetry under swapping the discs (1e-16 relative), the near-totality headline (at 99% geometric obscuration the limb-darkened survivor is **0.51x** the uniform-disc survivor — inside the measured 0.22-0.67 band of ACP 19:4703, i.e. the "roughly 2x over-prediction" the research report requires), magnitude-vs-obscuration (the Stellarium #3720 trap), the published-field contract + in-place mutation, the off-toggle exact identity, the gated-off Earth term, an analytic orbital-sunset sweep (400 steps: max single-step drop **0.019**, > 40 transitional steps — a binary cull would show 1.0), the real 2024-04-08 eclipse from Dallas (peak obscuration exactly 1.0 with magnitude 1.0013 at 18:44:10 UTC, inside the published 18:40:43-18:44:57 UTC totality window; exactly 0.0 at 16:00/17:00/20:10/21:00 UTC, outside the published 17:23-20:02 partial window; 18:17 UTC deep partial 0.607 limb-darkened vs 0.581 uniform), both-backend source pins, the no-new-define-bit pin, the untouched-cull pin, and naga validation of the sun WGSL. **Honest note:** under `node --test` there is no earth-orientation data, so `computeIcrfToCentralBodyFixedMatrix` falls back to the TEME pseudo-fixed rotation and the whole Dallas curve is time-shifted about +80 s versus the published greatest-eclipse time. The assertions are therefore stated as "totality is reached, inside the published window, and exactly zero outside the published partial window" rather than pretending to arcsecond timing.

`Tools/visual-regression/probe-eclipse-sun-fade.mjs` (new). Three lanes: (a) orbital-sunset continuity, (b) the 2026-08-12 partial-eclipse instant derived in-page from Simon1994, (c) toggle-off identity. See the `DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md` probe-inventory row for the full metric set. The measurement renders each step TWICE with `scene.sun.show` toggled and integrates |luminance difference| over the glow annulus, which isolates the sun exactly, is zero wherever the globe covers it, and scales EXACTLY linearly in alpha under both blend states (`ALPHA_BLEND` gives `out - dst = a·(src - dst)`, additive gives `out - dst = a·src`).

**Orchestrator Edge run, main tree, full build, both backends (2026-07-24) — THE FEATURE IS GREEN.** Lane (a) all-pass on both backends: **WebGL sweep `maxStepDelta` 0.03 with the effect ON — the pop is dead**; WebGPU `firstNorm` 1 → `lastNorm` 0 with `maxStepDelta` 0.078 — the backend that previously never dimmed now fades to nothing; `alphaTracksFraction` exact on all 121 steps. Lane (b) all-pass: the in-page derivation landed on an Iceland vantage at obscuration 0.647, `moonIsTheOccluder`, `alphaIsLinear`, `offToggleIsIdentity`.

**Two lane-(c) checks FAILED and were both CHECK-DESIGN flaws, not engine defects — the probe was redesigned, no engine code changed.**

*C1 — `legacyBehaviourRestored` asked pixels to show something pixels cannot show.* It required WebGL's binary pop to appear in the luminance metric with the toggle off. But the worked geometry above puts the cull boundary (sun elevation −21.75°) **1.3° BELOW the end of the fade band (−20.42°)** — by the time the cull fires, the Earth's limb already covers the glow annulus, so the metric is ≈0 and the pop cannot register. Measured: WebGL OFF `maxStepDelta` 0.03 (not ≥ 0.5) and WebGPU OFF `lastNorm` 0 (not ≥ 0.5), because geometric occlusion of the billboard by the globe dims BOTH backends smoothly regardless of alpha. That the check is unobservable is itself a restatement of the S1 correctness argument. **Redesign:** prove legacy restoration at STATE level, where it is observable — read `scene.environmentState.isSunVisible` per step (right after the sun-shown render; hiding the sun clears `sunDrawCommand` and forces the flag false for unrelated reasons) and assert (WebGL) the binary cull still FIRES at the deep tail and fires only where `sunVisibleFraction` is already exactly 0, (WebGPU) it never fires and `sunDrawCommand.boundingVolume` is absent at every step. Plus the true regression pin: the ON and OFF sweeps must flip at the SAME step ±1 (`cullBoundaryUnchanged`) — that is what "S1 did not move the cull" actually means.

*C2 — `byteIdenticalWhereUnoccluded` assumed cross-run determinism that does not exist.* It compared canvas hashes across two separate sweep runs, but frame-count-driven animation (`czm_frameNumber` ocean waves, and any other frameNumber term reaching the frame) advances differently between runs, so those hashes can never be stably equal. The bit-identity claim is already carried analytically by `eclipse-state.spec.mjs`' exact-`1.0` pin (`x * 1.0 === x`). **Redesign:** compare the ON vs OFF luminance METRIC per step where `fraction === 1` with `abs(on − off) / max(off, 1) ≤ 0.02` (calibrated — the two Edge runs agreed to ~1% on that machine), which still catches any wrong-alpha bug as a large systematic drop, plus `eclipseVisiblyApplied` (brightness-weighted partial-band ratio < 0.8) for non-vacuity.

**Provenance marker fix (same run).** The `EclipseState.js` verbatim slice `(1.0 - earthOcclusion) * (1.0 - moonObscuration)` is not bundle-stable — esbuild normalises float literals (`1.0` → `1`), so it matched the source but never the build and would have failed provenance on a perfectly current build. Replaced with the numeral-free substring `- earthOcclusion) * (1`, with the reason in a comment.

**Adversarial verify-fleet findings, all folded in (2026-07-24).** The fleet independently reproduced the Gauss-Legendre construction, proved the update order (occluder → `uniformState.update` → eclipse publish → `updateEnvironment` → `Sun.update` → factor), confirmed the byte-124 pad reuse is dead, confirmed the off-identity is exact, and scanned the `page.evaluate` callbacks identifier-by-identifier. Five findings, four of them engine changes:

*V1 (MAJOR, confirmed by two independent checkers) — the lunar memo was keyed on `JulianDate` alone, but its VALUE depends on which rotation it used.* `Transforms.computeIcrfToCentralBodyFixedMatrix` silently substitutes the TEME pseudo-fixed rotation while the IAU2006 XYS data is still loading asynchronously, and the two disagree by ~0.3-0.4° in 2026 — **larger than the ~0.53° solar disc**. Under a pinned/paused clock (every fleet probe, and a common user pattern) the memo would permanently retain the TEME moon while `Moon.update` and `UniformState` recompute every frame and switch to true ICRF the instant the data lands: the rendered moon and the fade would disagree by more than a solar diameter (a moon sitting on the sun with no dimming, or dimming with the moon visibly off-sun), and the probe's 2026-08-12 lane would flake on XYS-load timing. **Fix:** the rotation branch is now part of the memo key. New `computeIcrfToFixedBranch(time, result)` calls `Transforms.computeIcrfToFixedMatrix` explicitly and reports `usedIcrf` via a module-level result object (allocation-free); `getMoonPositionWC` re-probes on every hit whose cached value came from the fallback — a cheap `undefined` return until the data lands, then exactly one rebuild — and latches once the value is ICRF-sourced (XYS availability is monotone for a fixed time). Spec test 20 simulates the whole transition by stubbing the `Transforms` seam: memoise under the fallback, assert the memo holds while the branch is unchanged, install a deliberately distinct ICRF rotation and assert the memo rebuilds (position moves > 1e6 m), then assert an ICRF-sourced memo never re-probes.

*V2 — 2D/Columbus-view frame mixing.* Outside SCENE3D the camera position is in projected-map coordinates while the sun and moon are ECEF. The Earth term was already inert there (no occluder), but the MOON term kept running on mixed frames — direction errors up to ~1.5°, several solar diameters. **Fix:** new `options.active`, set from `frameState.mode === SceneMode.SCENE3D` in `Scene.js`; false ⇒ full identity (`valid = false`, factor exactly 1.0). Legacy had no sun occlusion in those modes at all, so that is correct by definition rather than a compromise. Spec tests 21-22 pin both the behaviour and the `Scene.js` gate.

*V3 — the per-frame options object literal contradicted the allocation-free claim.* Hoisted to a module-level `scratchEclipseOptions` in `Scene.js`, every field overwritten unconditionally at the call site; spec test 22 asserts the literal form is gone.

*V4 — the quadrature accuracy comment overclaimed.* Splitting at the coverage kinks removes the kinks but NOT the sqrt-type derivative singularities that sit exactly AT the sub-interval endpoints, so Gauss-Legendre never reaches its spectral rate there and the old "< 1e-9 / exact-to-roundoff" claim was wrong. Measured against a 20,000-point-per-sub-interval midpoint reference over ro/rs ∈ {0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 1.05, 1.2, 2.0} × 60 separations: worst absolute error **2.8e-5** in obscuration (worst near ro/rs = 0.7, d/rs = 0.31; the fleet's independent sweep found ~2.0e-5 near ro/rs = 0.9, d/rs = 0.57 — same order). That is ~1e-5 of a magnitude, three orders below 8-bit display quantisation and far below the ±2.5-4% spread of published limb-darkening fits. The comment now states the measured bound and the singularity caveat, and notes that raising the order buys nothing. The EXACT endpoints (0.0 disjoint, 1.0 umbra) are branch results, not quadrature results, and carry no error at all.

**Second Edge run (v3, 2026-07-24): lanes (a) and (b) GREEN on both backends; four more lane-(c) MEASUREMENT bugs, again none of them engine defects.** The engine is landable as it stands.

*F1 — the `isSunVisible` read was an artifact.* Raw steps showed `isSunVisible === false` at EVERY step on WebGL, including steps where lane (a) proves the sun rendered bright. Those two cannot both be engine behaviour: on WebGL the sun is executed by `EnvironmentRenderer` **only** under `if (environmentState.isSunVisible)`, so a bright sun REQUIRES the flag true. The recorded value was therefore contaminated by the sun-hidden render used for the background reference (hiding the sun clears `sunDrawCommand`, which forces the flag false for reasons unrelated to the cull). WebGPU's expectation happened to be `flip === -1`, so the same bug passed there silently. **Fix:** capture the cull state in a `scene.postRender` listener (raised at the end of `Scene.prototype.render`, after `updateEnvironment` has run for that frame — the canonical sampling point) that ignores every frame rendered with the sun hidden.

*F2/F3 — the two-sweep shape was the real defect.* Identity read 0.027 against a 0.02 tolerance because 60-78 of 121 steps ran on unsettled globe tiles whose limb pixels differ between a cold first sweep and a warm second one; and the 8-bit saturation mask could not be shared across two `page.evaluate` calls, so WebGPU's additive clamp pushed its band ratio to >= 0.8 while WebGL read 0.515 (exactly its expectation). **Fix — collapse the two sweeps into one that measures BOTH toggle positions per step**: four renders per step, `{eclipse off, on}` x `{sun shown, sun hidden}`. That deletes all three cross-run axes at once (same tiles, same frame-number neighbourhood, one shared mask built from the brightest capture) and costs no extra rendering — four renders across one sweep is what two renders across two sweeps already cost. Per-step tile settle raised 6 -> 30 frames, the identity check restricted to steps where the tiles had settled (>= 5 required, 0.05 fallback over all unoccluded steps only if fewer with the reason recorded, structural if none).

*F4 — initial tile settle raised 180 -> 400 frames* (bounded, expiry recorded, informational).

**A premise corrected while fixing F1.** The v2 lane-(c) check demanded that WebGL's binary cull FIRE somewhere in the sweep. It may not: the sun's glow bounding volume is ~4.2e9 m against a ~6.4e6 m Earth occluder, so `Occluder.isBoundingSphereVisible` takes its rarely-exercised "occludee larger than occluder" branch and may never report full occlusion at 1 AU. Gating on "the cull fires" would have repeated the v1 mistake of asserting an unverified premise. The gate is now the regression-relevant claim that holds either way — **the cull's per-step state is IDENTICAL with the effect on and off** (`cullStateUnchanged`, plus `cullNonVacuous` and the structural `boundingVolumeShape`: WebGL's sun `DrawCommand` carries a bounding volume, WebGPU's `WebGPUDrawCommand` carries none). Whether it fires is reported, not gated.

**Third Edge run (2026-07-24): WebGL FULLY GREEN, one WebGPU measurement bug left.** WebGL: `identityWorstRelDelta` exactly **0**, `bandRatioMeasured` **0.491** == `bandRatioExpected` **0.491**. The legacy cull *does* fire on WebGL (`visibleStepCount` 77, `onFlipStep == offFlipStep == 77`) — so the withdrawn −21.75° estimate was directionally right after all, and the `cullStateUnchanged` invariance gate covers it correctly either way, which is exactly why it was written to not depend on the answer. WebGPU failed only `eclipseVisiblyApplied`, with `bandRatioMeasured` **null**.

*Mechanism.* The band mask keeps unsaturated pixels of the eclipse-OFF (brightest) capture. WebGPU blends the sun ADDITIVELY, so with the effect off the inner glow clamps at 255 and the mask discards precisely the pixels where the sun contributes; what survives inside 6× the limb radius can be only globe pixels the sun never reached, whose ON−OFF difference is exactly 0. Summed over the partial band that gives `sumOff === 0` and a null ratio. Lane (a) is unaffected because at `fraction === 1` the ON and OFF captures are identical and plenty of unsaturated sun-bearing pixels remain.

*Fix — a three-tier band gate, non-vacuous by construction rather than by luck.* Tier 1 `primary-masked`: brightness-weighted ratio over partial-band steps with ≥300 unsaturated px inside 1.5×..6×, ≥5 steps required, gate < 0.8 (WebGL lands here). Tier 2 `wide-masked`: the same gate with the mask sourced from a wider 1.5×..10× annulus — the ROI was widened 6.5× → 10.5× of the limb radius to fit it, and since the glow falls off radially the outer ring still carries unsaturated sun-bearing pixels. Tier 3 `raw-strict`: over the UNMASKED 1.5×..6× annulus, require `glowOnRaw < glowOffRaw` at every partial-band step (≥5); saturation can only understate the dimming (a clamped ON pixel is at most as bright as a clamped OFF pixel), so this one-sided count can never manufacture a pass. **The asymmetry is mask SOURCING only** — within any single step `glowOn` and `glowOff` always sum over the identical pixel set, so every ratio compares like with like; only which set is used varies, and `bandTier` + `bandTierReason` are recorded so a fallback can never pass silently. The PRIMARY annulus is unchanged at 1.5×..6×, so lane (a)'s calibration and the identity check are untouched. New diagnostics make the mechanism visible in the manifest rather than inferable: `partialStepsOverFloor{Primary,Wide}`, `partialMaskedPx{,Wide}{Min,Max}`, `maskedPxFloor`, `bandStrictSteps`/`bandStrictTotal`, and a 4-bin radial saturation profile across 1.5×..10× (`meanSaturationProfile`, `partialSaturationProfile`) showing WHERE the additive blend clamps.

**Fourth Edge run (2026-07-24): WebGL lane (c) ALL EIGHT GREEN** (primary-masked tier, `bandRatioMeasured` 0.491 == `bandRatioExpected` 0.491, 13 steps). WebGPU 7 of 8, and the per-step data settled the last one: `glowOnRaw == glowOffRaw == 0` at **all 15 partial-band steps** (fraction 0.990 down to 0.001), with the effect off AND on.

**This is a pre-existing backend sun-RENDERING divergence, not an S1 defect and not saturation.** The fade band IS the earth-limb crossing. WebGL has a measurable band there only because its ~6 R_sun glow billboard extends ABOVE the limb; the WebGPU sun's glow does not survive the limb at all. So no eclipse effect could be observed in that band on WebGPU no matter how it were implemented — the sun simply is not there to dim. Recorded verbatim for future sessions: *"WebGPU sun glow does not extend above the earth limb (glowOffRaw 0 across the whole fade band at this vantage) — visible earth-limb dimming is unobservable on WebGPU until the C12-15..17 sun-appearance wave lands; the eclipse alpha application on WebGPU is proven by the open-sky moon-eclipse lane instead."* Filed as measured evidence on the `C12-15`, `C12-16` and `C12-17` queue rows (C12-16's terminating `1-smoothstep(0,0.55,r)` glare falloff and C12-17's fixed 256² 8-bit bake are the two co-suspects).

**Final check shape — backend-aware, with the deferral made explicit rather than silent.** Lane (c)'s `eclipseVisiblyApplied` on WebGL is unchanged (the three band tiers; it lands on tier 1). On WebGPU the probe detects the condition **by measurement**, never by assumption — `partialGlowOffRawMax === 0` over the partial band, recorded in the manifest alongside `partialGlowOnRawMax` — then reports `bandTier: "NA-geometric-limb"` with the full reason string, and makes its PASS **formally require lane (b)'s `alphaIsLinear` AND `partialEclipse`**. Lane (b) is the open-sky 2026-08-12 moon eclipse: the sun is high, nothing occludes the annulus, and the alpha multiply is measured directly and linearly — which is exactly the proof the limb band cannot supply on that backend. `crossToggle.deferredToLaneB` records the two delegated results. Verified by simulation before shipping: lane (b) red ⇒ lane (c) fails; non-zero glow ⇒ the normal `raw-strict` arm; WebGL can never take the NA arm. Lane (b) computation was hoisted above lane (c) so the dependency is a real data dependency in the code, not just in prose.

*V5 — probe provenance robustness.* (a) `FrameState.js` and `WebGPUShaderDefines.ts` joined `SOURCE_FILES`, so the mtime gate now covers every file the spec asserts on — a half-rebuilt tree cannot produce a green run. (b) The token/marker search previously accepted a match in ANY `.js` under `Build/CesiumUnminified`, including content-hashed chunk files left over from older builds, which turned the stale-build guard into a no-op exactly when it mattered; the search is now restricted to files written within a 10-minute window of the newest bundle file, and `Build/CesiumUnminified/index.js` must itself be inside that window (`entryFresh`). Skipped stale files are reported. (c) Globe-tile residency: a bounded 180-frame `globe.tilesLoaded` settle at the start of each sweep and before the eclipse-instant passes, plus a bounded 6-frame per-step settle, so the eclipse-ON and eclipse-OFF sweeps see the same globe. (The per-step metric is a within-step difference, so residency already cancels there; this protects the cross-sweep comparisons. Expiring is recorded, never structural.)

**Files:** new `packages/engine/Source/Scene/EclipseState.js`, new `packages/engine/Source/Scene/computeSolarObscuration.js`; `Scene/Scene.js` (import + `_eclipseState` + the per-frame publish; the `isSunVisible` cull line unchanged), `Scene/Sun.js` (uniform + publish), `Scene/FrameState.js` (2 field declarations), `Scene/AtmosphericConditions.js` (`enableEclipse: true`), `Shaders/SunFS.glsl`, `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer.js` (WGSL UB member + fs multiply + `packSunUniforms` slot 31). New `Tools/visual-regression/probe-eclipse-sun-fade.mjs` + `Tools/visual-regression/eclipse-state.spec.mjs`. Doc: `FEATURE_INVENTORY.md` §B entry, `DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md` probe row, `QUEUE_2026-07-19_CAMPAIGN12.md` C12-29 row, this entry.

**Gates:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint` clean on all seven touched engine files; `node --test eclipse-state.spec.mjs` 28/28; `node --check probe-eclipse-sun-fade.mjs` clean. `gulp build` + the Edge probe run are the orchestrator's.

**Not in S1 (unchanged, still §D):** S2 scene-light + atmosphere dimming, S3 clouds + IBL (C13 rider after C13-39), S4 orbital-sunrise limb glow, S5 per-fragment globe umbra, S6 totality phenomena. `Sun.js:136-163`'s extinction integrator is untouched — it is S4 territory.
